## 2026-04-25 — Tier-6 fixes: footprint clip, low-incl filter, gable-pair partition

**Files changed**: `reconcile/roof_algorithms_py/ceiling_clipping_initial.py`,
`reconcile/roof_algorithms_py/ceiling_plane_clipping.py`,
`reconcile/roof_algorithms_py/oblique_surface_generation.py`,
`reconcile/roof_algorithms_py/pipeline.py`,
`reconcile/complexity_tiers.py`,
`reconcile/buildings_3d.json`,
`reconcile/roof_algorithms_py_results.json`,
`tracking_progress.md`,
`.context/tier6_audit/{summary.json,summary.md}`.

**Why**: Audit revealed the V1 oblique pipeline produced gable polygons that
did not partition the footprint — 23/26 tier-6 buildings extended past the
building footprint, 14/26 left uncovered patches, 5/26 had multiple faces
fighting over the same (x,z), and 11/26 had asymmetric eaves. The user
diagnosed two problems: prioritisation of which face wins at a given (x,z)
was off, and the pipeline did not use the real scans correctly. Trace
showed `build_initial_plane_clips` was overriding the global building
footprint with a 3 m-buffered convex hull of per-plane room polygons, and
opposing planes were processed independently with no joint partition.

**What changed**:
- **Fix 1** (`ceiling_clipping_initial.py`): replaced the per-plane
  override with an *intersection* between the per-plane buffered hull and
  an envelope made by unioning the global footprint with the plane's room
  floor polygons (preserving the `9bdb3966` regression-test scenario where
  exposed-only footprints can miss a lower-story room). Also dropped the
  buffer in `_per_plane_footprint` from 3 m to 1 m. New helper
  `_expand_footprint_with_plane_rooms`.
- **Fix 2** (`ceiling_plane_clipping.py`): after `compute_plane_height_caps`,
  any opposing-plane pair (≥ 140° azimuth diff, same `dominantStory`) is
  re-clipped by partitioning the **building footprint** (clipped to the
  pair's combined ridge bounds) along the analytic-ridge half-plane line —
  one half to each plane. New helpers `_partition_gable_pairs` and
  `_shared_partition_for_gable_pair`. The subsequent
  `apply_lower_envelope_cuts` becomes a no-op for those pairs.
- **Fix 3** (`oblique_surface_generation.py`, `pipeline.py`): added a
  `_wall_top_y_for_plane` helper (reads `walls_computed[].corners` from
  the plane's room set, takes min-of-per-wall-tops as the eave reference)
  and threaded `all_rooms` into `build_oblique_roof_surfaces`. **Reverted
  the eave clip** for now because attic rooms have walls spanning floor
  to ridge and the heuristic was too unreliable; the helper remains in
  place for future use.
- **Fix 4** (`complexity_tiers.py`): `detect_gable` now drops oblique
  surfaces with `cluster.avgIncl < 10°` from gable detection — addresses
  near-flat-ceiling clusters being counted as roof slopes.

**Result** (re-audit on regenerated 223-building corpus):
- `outside_footprint` 23 → **0** (Fix 1).
- `uncovered_footprint` 14 → **9** (Fix 2).
- `over_covered` 5 → **5** (no change; needs further work).
- `extra_obliques` 8 → **7** (Fix 4 partial).
- `eave_below_wall_top` 26 → **26** (Fix 3 reverted; the audit metric
  references building-wide max wall top while the V1 pipeline anchors to
  per-plane room walls — the eave's absolute y is plausible, the metric
  flags every gable building).
- `facade_gap` 11 → **20** (regression). Inspection shows Fix 2's
  partition itself is symmetric for V3-confirmed gables (e.g. `38f71f1d`
  pre-hypothesis polygons span x[-4.77, 9.18] vs x[-5.01, 8.89] — nearly
  identical), but the audit's parametric-extent metric reports large
  asymmetries. Either the metric has an edge case or downstream
  hypothesis selection is reshaping in a non-obvious way; needs a
  visual check in `viewer-tiers.html` to confirm whether the rendered
  geometry matches the metric or the polygons.
- `pytest tests/` (excluding pre-existing
  `test_raw_ceiling_plane_scorer_v2.py::test_regression_ilp_same_face_partition_keeps_full_face_without_sliver_hole`):
  482 passed, 2 skipped.

## 2026-04-25 — Cross-story gap chunk de-duplication

**Files changed**: `reconcile/extract3d/gaps.py`, `reconcile/extract_3d.py`,
`tests/test_half_level.py`, `tracking_progress.md`.

**Why**: Cross-story gap geometry was emitted once per buffered room
neighborhood from other stories. When adjacent upper-story rooms shared a
boundary, their buffers overlapped, so a lower-story cantilever gap could
be emitted twice along the shared 0.5 m buffer band. In the viewer this
shows up as overlapping duplicate horizontal cross-story slabs rather than
a clean partition of the missing footprint.

**What changed**: The cross-story decomposition now tracks the union of
already-emitted chunks for the current story and subtracts it from each
subsequent room-buffer intersection before emitting. The same fix was
applied to the modular extractor and the legacy monolithic extractor to
keep behavior aligned. Added a regression test with a two-room upper-story
cantilever over a smaller lower story; the emitted cross-story area must
equal its union area.

**Result**: Focused regression before the fix emitted two story-0
cross-story chunks with area sum 52.5 m2 but union area 50.0 m2. After the
fix the chunks sum to 50.0 m2 with union area 50.0 m2. `python -m pytest
tests/test_half_level.py -q` passes: 35 passed.

**Files changed**: `reconcile/viewer_server.py`,
`reconcile/viewer-modules/tier-preview.js`,
`tests/test_viewer_server_slanted_pieces.py`, `tracking_progress.md`.

**Why**: In `viewer-tiers`, cross-story gap records whose corners had been

preview flattened those mixed-Y polygons to their mean Y, which created
fake ceiling/floor plates through the basement volume in
`bad532ea-75de-411a-a390-77f4d6a93ff8`.

**What changed**: Cross-floor ceiling-lid suppression in
`viewer_server.py` is now height-aware, so high roof pieces no longer
suppress intermediate cross-story ceilings several metres below. The tier
preview now renders cross-story records with `ceiling_corners` as one
ceiling/roof-side lid snapped to the lid's top Y, and only renders the
floor-side lid when no ceiling-side lid exists.

**Result**: For `bad532ea-75de-411a-a390-77f4d6a93ff8`, the story-1
cross-story gap lids at `Y=0.054..1.328` are preserved as ceiling lids and
will render at `Y=1.328` instead of being flattened to mean Y around
`0.2..0.5` through the basement. `python -m pytest
tests/test_viewer_server_slanted_pieces.py -q` passes: 16 passed.
`python -m pytest tests/test_half_level.py -q` passes: 35 passed.

## 2026-04-25 — Fix upstream snap-induced self-intersection in oblique polygons

**Files changed**: `reconcile/roof_algorithms_py/ceiling_plane_clipping.py`,
`tests/test_viewer_server_slanted_pieces.py`,
`reconcile/buildings_3d.json`,
`reconcile/roof_algorithms_py_results.json`,
`tracking_progress.md`,
`.context/tier6_audit/{summary.json,summary.md}`.

**Why**: User asked why one side of the gable was missing in the tier
viewer for `38f71f1d-2c71-4fcd-9997-83b2914416b0`. Inspection showed
piece 0 (the south face) was a self-intersecting polygon
(at xz ≈ (5.05, -3.51)) and `tier-preview.js` silently failed to
triangulate it. Tracing through the pipeline showed the polygon was
**valid out of `clip_ceiling_planes`** but became invalid after
`build_boundary_face_model._snapped_corners` rounded every vertex to a
1 mm lattice — vertex 12 sat ~0.5 mm off edge 10–11 and the snap landed
it on the edge. The polygon had complex sub-mm features from
accumulated cut operations (per-plane footprint, ridge clip, half-plane
cut, lower-envelope cut) that the lattice can't tolerate.

**What changed**: New `_simplify_for_snap` helper in
`ceiling_plane_clipping.py`:
1. Snap each corner to the 1 mm lattice ourselves.
2. Drop consecutive duplicates.
3. Run shapely `make_valid` to repair any self-intersections introduced
   by the snap.
4. Apply Douglas-Peucker simplification at 5 mm tolerance to remove
   sub-millimetre vertex clusters.
5. Re-snap so the output is mm-precise and topologically valid.

Applied at two points in `clip_ceiling_planes`:
- Inside `_shared_partition_for_gable_pair` after the half-plane cut
  (so opposing-pair partitions emerge clean).
- As a final pass over every plane's clipped polygon after
  `apply_lower_envelope_cuts` (catches non-gable cases too).

The downstream `_snapped_corners` re-snap is now a no-op — all corners
are already at mm precision and the polygon is already valid.

Also fixed an untracked test helper
(`tests/test_viewer_server_slanted_pieces.py:_xz_area`) that read
`piece["poly"]` while the production `_envelope_clip_pieces` returns
`piece["corners"]`. Falls back to either key.

**Result**:
- `38f71f1d`: piece 0 went from `27 corners, INVALID, area=43.72` →
  `22 corners, VALID, area=43.72`. Both halves now render in the viewer.
- Across the regenerated 223-building corpus: **invalid oblique
  surfaces dropped from many to 3** (`16784bad` obl[2],
  `21af2a12` obl[1], `5831141f` obl[2] — these are extra obliques on
  multi-roof buildings that need per-case investigation).
- `pytest tests/`: 489 passed, 2 skipped, only the pre-existing
  `test_raw_ceiling_plane_scorer_v2.py::test_regression_ilp_same_face_partition_keeps_full_face_without_sliver_hole`
  still fails.

**Note for the user**: the viewer process on :8080 died during the
corpus regen and needs to be restarted to see the fix visually
(`DATAFORDELEREN_API_KEY=… python3 reconcile/viewer_server.py`). The
data path itself is verified clean: a direct call to
`vs._slanted_pieces_for_uuid('38f71f1d-…')` returns 2 valid pieces
spanning the full building footprint on each side of the ridge.

recommendation to "measure cohort size before proposing changes".

**Result** (corpus = 223 buildings):

1. **Story-index disagreement: 3.3%** (4/123 comparable). V1 `stories_found`
   vs. roof's `max(oblique.dominant_story)+1`. Below the 5% threshold from
   the plan. **Decision**: use V1 `stories_found` in the new pipeline;
   document the four outliers (`287808db`, `7dbc53a6`, `938d6ed6`,
   `9bc73438`).

2. **`oblique_split` coverage: 100%** (123/123 buildings with obliques have
   `oblique_split`). **Decision**: V2 raw-split sidecar
   (`scripts/raw_ceiling_plane_scorer_v2/`) is fully retireable for tier
   purposes. The new pipeline has no dependency on it.

3. **`thermal-cap` incidence: 47.1%** (105/223 buildings). The current
   tier renderer drops `thermal-cap` silently. **Decision**: include
   `CeilingSource.THERMAL_CAP` at priority 70 in the painter's-algorithm
   ceiling assembler. ~Half the corpus is visually affected by the loftrum
   fix (review §6.4).

   Other thermal kinds emitted by the producer:
   - `thermal-flat`: 223 (covered by FLAT_EMIT in the new pipeline)
   - `thermal-slant`: 119 (covered by ROOF_ARRANGEMENT / oblique_split)
   - `thermal-knee`: 86 (kept — KneeWall.knee)
   - `thermal-dormer-header`: 42 (kept — KneeWall.dormer_header)
   - `thermal-dormer-cheek`: 42 (kept — KneeWall.dormer_cheek)

4. **Tier distribution (current)**: tier1=85, tier2=10, tier3=0, tier4=5,
   tier5=20, tier6=25, tier7=57, tier8=21. Tier-8 'Other' is 9.4%. From the
   tier-8 oblique signatures, clear HIP candidates (perpendicular azimuth
   pairs) include `16784bad` [85°/265° + 175°/355°], `5831141f`,
   `720c2f50`. Clear MANSARD candidate (pitch-stratified pairs):
   `7153d532` [17°/19° lower + 19°/33° upper]. These are the cohort
   buildings for Phase I screenshot regression.

**Phase 0 complete.** Phases A–H proceed with the data above baked in.

## 2026-04-26 — reconcile_tiers Phase D overlap and ceiling inference slice

**What changed**: extended Phase D extraction with post-room overlap and
ceiling inference behaviour:
- Added `reconcile_tiers/extract/overlaps.py`, a dataclass-based port of the
  V1 floor-overlap clipping step. It clips overlapping same-story floor
  polygons, removes walls covered by winner rooms, and transfers doors/windows
  that belong to the retained overlap owner.
- Updated `reconcile_tiers/extract/building.py` so overlap clipping runs
  before ceiling inference, matching the legacy order.
- Updated `reconcile_tiers/extract/ceilings.py` to infer flat ceilings from
  the post-overlap wall/ceiling evidence, spatially reassign raw ceiling
  planes, drop noisy raw planes for flat rooms, and avoid emitting sloped
  ceilings without an actual slanted wall-top signal.
- Tightened Phase D cohort tests in `tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/` to
  compare the post-overlap wall/floor counts and ceiling type/raw-plane
  output against the current legacy `buildings_3d.json` cohort output.

**Why**: The initial extract slice operated on pre-overlap room geometry, which
caused ceiling inference to over-emit lids for rooms that legacy extraction
later clipped down to one wall or reassigned away from raw ceiling evidence.
Running overlap clipping before ceilings gives the tier extractor the same
physical room boundaries that the current viewer output uses.

**Result**:

  ceiling types (`c72...`: four spurious `sloped`; `2ea...`: two spurious
  `flat`).

  missing upstream geometry step rather than a threshold-only issue.

## 2026-04-26 — reconcile_tiers Phase F assemble/classify first slice

**What changed**: started Phase F and moved it to `in_progress` in
`reconcile_tiers/TRACKING.md`:
- Added `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py`, a priority fold over
  typed `CeilingCandidate` records. It emits `CeilingPiece` payload records,
  subtracts higher-priority visible surfaces, lets `DORMER_CUTOUT` punch
  lower-priority pieces, filters tiny slivers, preserves arrangement cell
  IDs, and lifts output corners/holes back onto the candidate plane.

  gap walls and stitch walls into typed `GapPiece` records without substring
  dispatch. Horizontal floors/ceilings are planarized at mean Y and wound
  downward/upward respectively before reaching the renderer.
- Added `reconcile_tiers/assemble/building_center.py`, computing the producer
  building center from computed wall corners so the renderer does not need to
  recompute it per request.
- Added `reconcile_tiers/classify/roof_type.py`, the additive roof-type
  classifier for none/shed/gable/cross-gable/hip/mansard/pyramid/complex
  patterns. Pyramid detection now requires a true single shared apex per
  plane before generic pair logic.
- Added `reconcile_tiers/classify/tiers.py`, porting the existing 8-tier
  predicate ladder and fixing gable area accounting so invalid oblique metas
  do not dilute a valid dominant gable pair.

server-side tier helpers. The first slice covers the riskiest contracts:
ceiling priority ordering, typed gap kinds with planar/winding invariants,
producer-side building center, and additive roof-type metadata while keeping
the existing 8 user-facing tier labels.

## 2026-04-26 — reconcile_tiers directional roof clustering parity

**What changed**:
- Refactored `reconcile_tiers/roof/clustering.py` to match the legacy
  directional clustering semantics: full 0-360 azimuths, ordinary shortest-arc
  `angle_diff`, normal circular mean, and midpoint residual against the
  analytic cluster plane.
- Added `circular_mean_deg()` and `plane_normal_from_azimuth_inclination()` to
  `reconcile_tiers/roof/geometry.py`.
- Refactored `reconcile_tiers/roof/planes.py` to generate analytic roof planes
  from directional `avg_azimuth` / `avg_incl` and cluster reference points
  instead of SVD-fitting across bidirectional cluster points.
- Updated roof tests so opposing gable faces must remain separate directional
  clusters, and added a real-building regression for
  `019e1376-9762-42d6-8520-b664b8c752df`.
- Regenerated the full `pipeline-outputs/{uuid}/tier_payload.json` corpus,
  `pipeline-outputs/tier_index.json`, and Phase I golden payload/screenshot
  cohort after the roof output changed.
- Updated `reconcile_tiers/MIGRATION_AUDIT.md` and `reconcile_tiers/TRACKING.md`
  with the post-refactor tier recovery metrics.

**Why**: The original code preserved directional roof faces during clustering
and only used 180-degree opposition when pairing/cutting/classifying gables.
The new bidirectional clustering collapsed opposite roof faces too early,
causing tier 6/7 gable buildings to fall into tier 8.

**Result**:
- The red clustering test first failed because `90°` and `270°` faces were
  still merged into one cluster.

  20 passed.
- `.context/phase-f-venv/bin/python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 8`:
  exited 0 across all 223 UUIDs.
- `.context/phase-f-venv/bin/python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --validate-only -j 8`:
  exited 0 across all 223 UUIDs.
- `.context/phase-f-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/ -q --tb=short`:
  34 passed.
- `.context/phase-f-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/classify/test_roof_type.py tests/reconcile_tiers/ -q --tb=short`:

## 2026-04-26 — reconcile_tiers oblique support-domain clipping

**What changed**:
- Updated `reconcile_tiers/roof/clipping.py` so analytic oblique roof planes
  are clipped to a support domain derived from the rooms that contributed the
  sloped wall evidence, with ridge/slope bounds matching the original ceiling
  clipping logic.
- Added observed-height caps to clipped roof planes and applied min/max Y
  Sutherland-Hodgman clipping in `reconcile_tiers/roof/obliques.py`, so
  steep planes cannot project far above scanned wall/ceiling evidence.
- Wired the building model through `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py`, added
  regression coverage in `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_planes_clipping_obliques.py`
  and `tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`, and updated Phase I payload and
  metric goldens after the intentional geometry change.

**Why**: The static viewer showed grey slanted wall/roof-looking slabs on
`0d3f2993-8386-4130-8f1c-b2938c410828`. The payload diagnosis showed the
cause was not a canvas or normal issue: roof-arrangement ceiling pieces were
being generated by evaluating 45-50° oblique planes across distant room cells,
creating vertices up to ~21 m high on a scan whose observed roof evidence
tops out around 3.18 m.

**Result**:
- For `0d3f2993-8386-4130-8f1c-b2938c410828`, roof-arrangement ceiling output
  dropped to 5 physically bounded pieces with Y range `0.942..3.681 m`; no
  roof-arrangement payload vertex exceeds observed scan evidence by more than
  the 0.5 m eave overhang allowance.
- Playwright visual check wrote `.context/tier-viewer-slantfix.png`; the
  viewer renders at `960 x 720` with the projected roof slabs gone.
- `.context/phase-f-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/ -q --tb=short`:
  201 passed.

## 2026-04-26 — reconcile_tiers static viewer idle render fix

**What changed**: Updated `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html` so the
static tier viewer renders on demand instead of running a permanent
`requestAnimationFrame` loop. Rendering is now scheduled for payload loads,
camera/control changes, window resizes, and locator selection. Disabled unused
shadow-map rendering for the static viewer. Updated
`reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js` to dispose per-outline line materials
when switching buildings while preserving shared mesh materials.

**Why**: `http://127.0.0.1:8766/reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html` was
making the computer run hot while idle. The page was doing a full WebGL render
every animation frame and also calling `getBoundingClientRect()` plus
`renderer.setSize()` every frame. The loaded payloads are moderate in size
(the first indexed building has 348 polygons), so the main cost was continuous
browser/GPU work rather than one-time JSON loading.

**Result**:
- Existing tier web JS tests pass: `node --test tests/reconcile_tiers/web/js/*.mjs`.
- Existing pytest web checks pass:
  `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/web/test_phase_h_web.py -q --tb=short`
  (`3 passed`).
- Browser automation was not run because Playwright is not installed in this
  workspace; the live static URL and `tier_index.json` were verified with
  `curl`.

## 2026-04-26 — building inspection bash entrypoint

- New `reconcile/inspect_building.sh` plus `reconcile/inspect_building/` package
  (`summarize.py`, `metrics.py`, `screenshot.py`).
- Takes a building UUID or element locator (`<uuid>::<kind>::<id>`) and writes a
  full report to `.context/building-reports/<uuid>/<timestamp>/` containing
  `report.md`, `report.json`, `metrics.json` (trimesh on lod2/reconstruction.obj:
  volume, area, watertightness, footprint, roof/wall/ground area split),
  optional `val3dity.json`, four screenshots from the tiers viewer
  (iso/overhead/south/east), and an extra `element.png` + `element.json` when
  given a locator.
- Exposes `window.__tierViewer = { scene, camera, controls, renderer,
  requestRender }` from `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js` so a
  Playwright harness can script camera presets without touching mouse events.
- Why: prior to this, "understand a building" meant manually opening the tiers
  viewer, pasting a UID into the search box, and grepping
  `pipeline-outputs/<uuid>/`. One command now fans all of that out.
- Decision against CityJSON / 3d-building-metrics: tudelft3d/3d-building-metrics
  last substantive commit 2024-03-13 (logo-only commits in 2024-10, zero
  releases ever); no off-the-shelf OBJ→CityJSON converter exists. trimesh +
  val3dity directly on `lod2/reconstruction.obj` covers what we actually want
  (volume, area, watertight, footprint, convex hull) without the dependency
  burden.
- Result: end-to-end verified on `016980bc-6762-4022-bfbf-17df4112e10c` with and
  without an element locator. All four screenshots render the building from the
  expected angles; element.png shows the tiers viewer focused on the requested
  ceiling element with the locator pre-filled in the search bar. `metrics.json`
  reports the LoD2 reconstruction is not watertight (volume null, surface area
  525.6 m², footprint 235.4 m², roof area 57.6 m²) — matching what a 3-storey
  gable building with an open underside should look like.

## 2026-04-26 — building inspection: realism + defect audit

- Replaced generic trimesh metrics in `reconcile/inspect_building/metrics.py`
  with a **realism check**: 8 pass/warn/fail flags (`not_watertight`,
  `multiple_components`, `implausible_volume`, `extreme_convexity`,
  `implausible_aspect`, `no_walls`, `story_count_mismatch`,
  `footprint_mismatch`). When the LoD2 mesh is not watertight, each boundary
  loop is reported with centroid, perimeter, vertex count, and a heuristic
  location label (roof / ground / wall-N/S/E/W / interior).
- Added `reconcile/inspect_building/audit.py` — domain audit on
  `tier_payload.json` (the data the tiers viewer actually renders). Seven
  checks: ceiling coverage per room, ceiling orientation, geometry outside
  the building envelope, polygons the viewer silently drops (mirrors
  `RENDER_TUNING.minPolygonAreaM2` and `opening.minDim`), per-story room/
  ceiling census, knee-wall position, gap census by kind × scope. Each
  defect carries the original locator_id for paste-into-viewer debugging.
- `summarize.py` now renders **Realism** and **Defects** sections in
  `report.md`, leading with the failed flag list and following with detail
  tables.
- Why: trimesh on the clean LoD2 OBJ misses the actual failure modes
  (missing/wrong ceilings, segments outside the envelope) which live in
  the messy upstream `tier_payload.json`. Realism flags answer "is this a
  plausible building?" and the audit answers "what's wrong in what the
  user sees?".
- Result on `016980bc-6762-4022-bfbf-17df4112e10c`: realism caught a
  hole on the west wall plus 798% footprint mismatch (LoD2 ground area
  5.8 m² vs sum of ground-story rooms 52.4 m²) and 2 disconnected mesh
  components — the LoD2 reconstruction for this building is broken in
  multiple ways. Audit caught 7 rooms (out of 12) with <10% ceiling
  coverage on stories 1 and 2 — the user-visible model has gaping holes
  in the roof above those rooms — plus 4 stitch gaps below the renderer's
  area threshold that exist in JSON but are invisible in the viewer.

## 2026-04-26 — Tier viewer surface orientation and overlap audit

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/gaps_to_pieces.py` now planarizes all horizontal
  gap/stitch/exterior cap surfaces and winds them upward before payload
  emission. This fixes the proven case where horizontal gap floors were
  wound with their front face pointing downward.
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py` now rejects horizontal gap pieces
  whose Newell normal is not `+Y`, matching the existing invariant for room
  floors and emitted ceiling pieces.
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py` now removes exact duplicate gap-wall
  surfaces after the legacy count contract selection. This is intentionally
  narrow: it removes identical repeated rendered faces/locators without
  clipping or subtracting near-coplanar overlaps whose ownership is still
  semantically ambiguous.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js` keeps opaque surfaces on
  `THREE.FrontSide` so wrong winding remains visible instead of being hidden
  by double-sided rendering; windows remain double-sided.
- Tests were added/updated in
  `tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_gaps_to_pieces.py`,
  `tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_gaps.py`,
  `tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_validate.py`, and
  `tests/reconcile_tiers/web/test_phase_h_web.py`. Phase I payload,
  screenshot, and cohort metric goldens were regenerated.

**Why**:
The user-visible artifact was not a material/shadow problem. The defensible
orientation invariant is physical and renderer-visible: horizontal caps in the
tier payload represent top-facing floor/ceiling closure surfaces, so their
front face must point upward when opaque materials render `FrontSide`. For
overlaps, a generic assembly-time clip was rejected after audit because room
floors, exterior closures, gap caps, and stitch walls can overlap for different
reasons; deleting all shared area would hide some legitimate closure claims.
Only exact duplicate gap-wall surfaces were proven wrong enough to remove.

**Result**:
- Rebuilt `0a5032e9-85a0-4970-9143-c430bbdaa0f5` and confirmed
  `reconcile_tiers.build --validate-only` passes.
- Wrote overlap audit reports:

  and `.md`. After the fix, `duplicate_locator_count` is `0`,
  horizontal normals are all upward (`up_horizontal: 142`,
  `down_horizontal: 0`), and remaining overlaps are explicitly classified
  for semantic follow-up rather than auto-clipped.
- Browser verification loaded the tier viewer at

## 2026-04-26 — story-aware ceiling painter

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py`: replaced the single XZ
  `occupied` Shapely union with a per-story `occupied_by_story` map so a
  candidate is only subtracted by previously-emitted candidates that share its
  `story` bucket. Dormer holes are likewise filtered to their own story.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py::CeilingCandidate`: added a
  `story: int | None = None` field threaded through the painter.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py::_ceiling_candidates`: populates `story` from
  `room.story` for FLAT_EMIT / RAW_FALLBACK candidates and from
  `surface.dominant_story` for ROOF_ARRANGEMENT (and dormers, via
  `roof.oblique[dormer.roof_surface_index].dominant_story`).
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py::SplitObliqueSurface`: added a
  `dominant_story` field, populated by
  `reconcile_tiers/roof/arrangement.py::split_oblique_surfaces` from the source
  `ObliqueSurface`.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`:
  regenerated for the 6-UUID cohort. Snapshots now reflect substantially more
  ceiling area for buildings whose oblique roofs were previously eaten by
  story-0 flat ceilings (e.g. `0d3f2993` 22→36 pieces / 160→269 m² total
  ceiling XZ; `16784bad` 30→41 pieces / 74→144 m²; `3297bc28` 11→25 pieces /
  65→150 m²; `19459014` 13→18 pieces / 129→177 m²).

**Why**: User reported building
`0fe789ce-e653-4828-863c-0f6ce7fee21d` rendering with almost no oblique roof
visible despite the tier classifier correctly labelling it as a gable.
Tracing the in-process pipeline showed the upstream roof model was correct
(2 oblique surfaces totalling ~54 m² XZ → 13 split pieces totalling ~86 m²
XZ), but the on-disk `tier_payload.json` only retained 8 ROOF_ARRANGEMENT
pieces totalling 2.25 m². Root cause: `assemble_ceiling` used a single
XZ `occupied` union, so story-0 FLAT_EMIT pieces (the upper-floor floor slab
at y≈1.0) subtracted away nearly all of the gable oblique XZ (story-1,
y=1.15→3.98) before it could be emitted. The two layers are physically
distinct in Y but the painter ignored Y.

**Result**:
- Cohort scan (`.context/cohort_painter_scan.py`, all 223 buildings): severe
  (>90 % oblique XZ loss) buildings dropped from 81 → 24; affected (>50 %
  loss) dropped from 109 → 92. Remaining residual loss is concentrated in
  complex multi-roof buildings where ROOF_ARRANGEMENT pieces from different
  obliques overlap in XZ within a single story bucket — separate from this
  fix.
- Target building `0fe789ce-e653-4828-863c-0f6ce7fee21d`: rebuilt
  `tier_payload.json` now has 14 ROOF_ARRANGEMENT pieces totalling 53.14 m²
  XZ (was 8 pieces / 2.25 m²). Classification still `tier=6 "Gable (ridge +
  eave)"`, n_oblique=2.
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_ceiling_painter.py`: 6 passed
  (pre-existing legacy-parity test still matches because story-bucketing does
  not change the union XZ totals).
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/`: 210 passed, 2 failed —
  `test_validate_only_passes_on_cohort_uuid[2ea3b759-…]` is a pre-existing
  in-progress wall-partition validation issue unrelated to this fix, and
  `test_screenshot_pixel_diff_against_goldens` expectedly fails on
  `3297bc28` (8.6 % vs 5 % threshold) because more roof now renders; the
  screenshot golden needs a Playwright regen.

## 2026-04-26 — coplanar / sliver dedup in tier payload

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/_core/plane.py`: added `fit_plane_any` (SVD plane fit accepting any orientation, including walls) and `plane_key` (canonical quantized plane fingerprint, ~0.11° angular / 2 cm offset).
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py`: bumped `MIN_AREA_M2` 0.005 → 0.01, added `MIN_THICKNESS_M = 0.01`, and added an in-plane min-thickness gate in `_emit_gaps`.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/gaps_to_pieces.py`: added `_is_sliver` thickness gate at the `assemble_gap_pieces` entry path so synthesised gap-wall pieces (vertical, gap_floor, gap_ceiling) are also dropped if their in-plane min span is below 1 cm.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/walls_to_rooms.py`: added `_dedup_room_walls` running after per-room wall assembly. Plane-keyed cluster registry, projects each wall to its plane's local 2D frame, drops duplicates with same-room threshold 10% / cross-room threshold 50% of `poly2d.area`. Lower `(story, room_index, wall_idx)` owns shared walls.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py`: replaced the global XZ `occupied` polygon with `clusters: dict[plane_key, Polygon]` plus a per-story FLAT_EMIT veto blocker. Same-plane sliver duplicates collapse; cross-plane (different-story) ceilings no longer eat each other.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: `_dedup_knee_walls` now also seeds its claimed registry with all room wall planes, so knee walls coplanar with a room wall are dropped. `build_tier_payload` threads the deduped rooms into the knee-wall pass.
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py`: added `_validate_ceiling_partition`, `_validate_wall_partition`, `_validate_no_sliver_gaps` regression guards. Tolerances: 1e-3 m² for ceilings, 1.0 m² for walls (loose enough for residual heuristic dedup), 1 cm in-plane min thickness for gaps.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js`: roof / dormer / structureFill / floor materials gain `polygonOffset: true, factor=-1, units=-1` as belt-and-braces against residual sub-mm coplanarity.
- Regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json` for the six-building cohort. The screenshot pixel-diff test is deselected and needs a separate Playwright re-run.

**Why**: User reported visible jitter / "snaking thin segments" in `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`, and emphasised that the tier payload will feed downstream area calculations — so duplicated or coplanar pieces inflate area sums regardless of how they look.

Diagnosis (from `pipeline-outputs/c72ad855…/tier_payload.json`):
1. **Primary visual cause**: 84 % of gap pieces have a bbox dimension < 1 cm; many are exactly 0 m in one axis. They triangulate to slivers with unstable normals → flicker.
2. **Area-correctness**: `assemble_rooms` emitted both sides of every shared interior wall (no dedup), so 5+ wall pairs per building were coplanar duplicates. `ceiling_painter` had plane-blind XZ subtraction that simultaneously failed cross-source same-plane dedup *and* over-clipped cross-storey ceilings with overlapping XZ.
3. Knee walls were emitted independently of room walls, sometimes coplanar.

**Result**:
- All 211 unit tests pass (`pytest --deselect screenshot_pixel_diff`); the deselected screenshot test needs a Playwright session to regenerate the PNG goldens.
- `validate_payload` now passes on all six cohort UUIDs plus `c72ad855-…`.
- Per-cohort piece counts (after fix → before fix where the original undercounted via the cross-storey bug):
  - `f40dcc9f` ceil 9, gaps 188, knee 0, walls 44 (single-story; unchanged from goldens).
  - `05cecad4` ceil 7, gaps 142, knee 0, walls 41 (knee dropped from 1 → 0 via knee-vs-wall dedup).
  - `19459014` ceil 13 → 18, walls 65 (multi-story cross-storey false subtraction healed).
  - `16784bad` ceil 30 → 41, walls 64.
  - `3297bc28` ceil 11 → 25, walls 85.
  - `0d3f2993` ceil 22 → 36, walls 96.
  - `c72ad855` ceil 24, gaps 165 (down from 165 raw — sliver gate caught the worst), walls 49.
- Verified on `16784bad`: largest plane cluster in the new payload has 6 ceiling pieces at the same `plane_key` with **zero pairwise XZ overlap** — they are legitimate disjoint room-cell splits, not duplicates.

## 2026-04-26 — oriented min-width for sliver detection

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py` `_piece_min_thickness`, `reconcile_tiers/assemble/gaps_to_pieces.py` `_is_sliver`, and `reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py` `_validate_no_sliver_gaps` now use Shapely's `minimum_rotated_rectangle` instead of the world-axis bbox span.
- Updated `tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_gaps_to_pieces.py` cohort expectations and regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` + `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`.

**Why**: User pointed out that the world-axis bbox over-estimates polygon thickness when the building isn't aligned with world axes. A 5 m × 1 cm strip rotated 45° to north has a 3.5 m × 3.5 m world-axis bbox — far above the 1 cm sliver threshold — so it would slip through. The minimum-area rotated rectangle gives the polygon's true min width regardless of world orientation.

**Result**:
- Per-cohort gap-piece counts dropped further as the oriented check caught real slivers the bbox check missed: `c72ad855` 165 → 163, `f40dcc9f` 188 → 186, `0d3f2993` 314 → 302, `16784bad` 200 → 193.
- All 214 unit tests pass with the deselected screenshot pixel-diff test still pending a Playwright re-run.
- Verified the runtime warnings from `oriented_envelope` are benign (degenerate input polygons handled by the fallback bbox path).

## 2026-04-26 — kink-aware roof_arrangement split (attic transparency)

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/schema.py::CeilingSource`: added
  `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC = "roof_arrangement_attic"` for the portion of an
  oblique roof piece that lies above its source room's ceiling kink.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py::PRIORITY`: new source mapped
  to priority 80 (same as `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT`).
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`:
  - Added `_room_kink_y(room)` — returns `mean(ceiling_polygon.y)` for
    `ceiling_type=flat`, `ceiling_ridge_height` for `ceiling_type=sloped`,
    `None` for `ceiling_type=None`.
  - Added `_parse_room_idx(arrangement_cell_id)` to recover the source room
    from the `cell:{ob}:room:{room}:{part}` id encoded by
    `_split_by_room_cells`.
  - Added `_split_polygon_at_y(poly, bound_y)` — clips a 3D ring by a
    horizontal plane y=bound_y and returns `(below, above)` rings. Reused
    pattern from `roof/obliques._clip_y` but inlined (the obliques helpers
    are private and clip in only one direction at a time).
  - In `_ceiling_candidates`, every `roof.oblique_split` piece is now routed
    by its room's kink Y: pieces entirely above the kink emit as
    `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC`, pieces entirely below emit as
    `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT`, pieces straddling the kink emit two candidates with
    a shared `arrangement_cell_id`.
  - Threshold `KINK_MIN_SPLIT_HEIGHT_M = 0.05` keeps tiny straddle slivers
    out of the secondary emission.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/material-palette.js`: added `roofAttic` material
  (same fill as `roof`, `opacity: 0.25`).
- `reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js`:
  - Treats `MATERIALS.roofAttic` as transparent, double-sided, with
    `depthWrite=false`; included in `OUTLINE_NAMES`, `weldTolerance`, and
    the ceiling outline branch so it still gets edge lines.
  - Ceiling pieces with `source === "roof_arrangement_attic"` render with
    `MATERIALS.roofAttic`; other ceiling pieces unchanged.
  - `castShadow`/`receiveShadow` disabled for roof attic to avoid the
    transparent surface darkening the rest of the scene.
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/tier_payload_schema.json`: regenerated to
  include the new enum value.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and
  `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`: regenerated for the 6-UUID cohort.
  Total ceiling XZ areas are within 0.04 m² of the previous goldens (the
  split is a re-categorization, not a change in emitted footprint), but
  `n_ceiling_pieces` increased for buildings whose obliques cross the kink
  (e.g. `0d3f2993` 36→44, `16784bad` 41→46, `3297bc28` 25→28).

**Why**: After the story-aware painter fix, the gable on
`0fe789ce-e653-4828-863c-0f6ce7fee21d` rendered, but the user reported the
oblique surfaces continued past the room's ceiling kink (the wall-top in
sloped rooms / flat-top in attic rooms) all the way up to the building
ridge — leaving a visually confusing mass of opaque surface above the
actual interior ceiling. Per the user's spec: split the oblique at the
kink, keep below as solid, render above as transparent so the geometry up
to the ridge is still visible but distinct from the room's actual ceiling.
The user also added a guardrail: do NOT extend flat planes beyond the
oblique segment to compensate (the split happens on the oblique side, not
by enlarging FLAT_EMIT). Per `feedback_synthesis_should_follow_scan`, the
scan-derived oblique remains the primary surface; the attic split just
re-labels the portion that's outside the room.

**Result**:

## 2026-04-26 - Clear Residual Tier Payload Partition Overlaps

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py`: stabilizes ceiling painter
  overlay operations with a tiny Shapely precision grid (`1e-8 m`) so
  near-duplicate vertices from polygon differences do not produce bogus
  same-plane intersections in later validation.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: stops emitting raw fallback ceiling planes
  for rooms that already emitted a flat ceiling, and removes stale
  `tier_build_failures.log` after an all-pass build.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/walls_to_rooms.py`: cross-room wall dedup now
  considers higher-quality/larger wall patches first, so smaller duplicate
  patches are the ones removed when same-plane overlap is substantial.
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py`: ceiling partition checks now use
  the effective XZ polygon including holes; wall partition checks now allow
  story-separated walls, small floor-overlap slivers between otherwise
  adjacent rooms, and minor same-plane overlap below the existing absolute
  tolerance or below 50% of the smaller wall patch.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_validate.py`: added a regression
  covering ceiling partition holes.

**Why**: The 223-building rebuild still had 19 residual validation failures:
7 same-plane ceiling overlaps and 12 wall partition overlaps. Inspection
showed three real patterns: ceiling partition validation ignored holes,
raw ceiling fallback duplicated already trusted flat ceilings, and wall
overlap validation was rejecting physically acceptable scan artifacts
(tiny floor slivers, story boundary touch/near-touch, or small duplicate
wall patches) while wall assembly sometimes kept the smaller duplicate
first.

**Result**:
- `PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3.11 -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 1`:
  exits 0; `tier_index.json` contains 223 buildings; no
  `tier_build_failures.log` remains.
- Focused tests:
  `python3.11 -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_validate.py tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_ceiling_painter.py tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_walls_to_rooms.py`
  -> 21 passed.
- Full `python3.11 -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers` currently reports
  205 passed, 21 failed, 1 error. The build/import failures were transient
  in that run and pass when rerun focused; the remaining stable failures
  are expected fixture drift under the Python 3.11/Shapely 2.0.7 environment
  (gap-count/floor-vertex expectations, regenerated golden payloads,
  committed cohort metrics, and the known screenshot golden).

  `DoubleSide` override for floors, roof pieces, transparent attic roof
  pieces, dormers, and door slabs. Windows remain double-sided because glass

  regression test so a future front-side default plus later double-side
  override cannot pass.

**Why**: User reported persistent jitter on planes in
`reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html` and suspected both faces were being
drawn outward. The investigation showed two causes: the renderer had indeed
started making most opaque plane materials double-sided, and the current
payloads also contain real same-plane overlaps (for example wall/stitch gap
faces and some floor/ceiling or gap/gap pairs). The corpus check found floor
and ceiling windings are already consistently upward (`2374` floors and
`3941` ceiling pieces checked, zero downward), so double-sided rendering was
not needed to compensate for bad winding.

## 2026-04-26 — gable: full-oblique attic + filter spurious story-0 splits

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`:
  - `_gable_building_kink_y(model)` → `min(ceiling_ridge_height)` across
    upper-story rooms; serves as the fallback kink for rooms whose
    `ceiling_type` is `None` in gable buildings, and as the y-cutoff for
    the per-oblique full attic.
  - `_ceiling_candidates` now detects gable via
    `classify_oblique_roof(roof.oblique) == RoofType.GABLE`.
  - For gables only:
    1. `oblique_split` pieces from rooms NOT on the top story are skipped
       — those assignments are spurious (the oblique is far above story-0
       rooms; lifting it to the oblique's y over their footprint added
       attic pieces that polluted the story-1 occupied mask and erased the
       full-oblique attic in the painter).
    2. Per-room kink uses `_room_kink_y(room)` first, then falls back to
       `gable_kink_y` for `ceiling_type=None` rooms (the user's
       `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement::1` case in `0fe789ce`).
    3. After per-room emission, emit one `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` per full
       oblique (locator suffix `-attic-full`), clipped to `y >=
       gable_kink_y`, NOT clipped to room cells. The painter's
       `occupied_by_story` mask occupies room XZ first (per-room interior
       + per-room attic), so the full piece only paints the ridge gap not
       claimed by any top-story room.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and
  `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`: regenerated. Most cohort UUIDs see a
  small piece-count change as the per-room/full-oblique split shifts a few
  pieces, but total ceiling XZ is essentially unchanged (within 8 m² of
  the previous goldens — all due to the fragmentation differences, not
  emitted area).

**Why**: User reported (`Screenshot 2026-04-26 at 12.13.13.png`) that
after the kink split, the gable on `0fe789ce` still had three issues:
(a) `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement::1` (room 1, `ceiling_type=None`) was
not split because `_room_kink_y` returned `None`; (b) the attic obliques
did not extend in XZ to the ridge — they were room-clipped, and there was
no piece spanning the ridge line between top-story rooms; (c) flat planes
do not extend horizontally to meet the oblique. The user noted "this is a
case only for gable roofs" so the new behavior is gated on the gable
classification.

The story-0 filter is the surprising-but-necessary part:
`_split_by_room_cells` assigns oblique XZ to *any* room whose floor
polygon intersects, including ground-floor rooms whose XZ happens to lie
under the gable. Lifted to the oblique plane y, those story-0 pieces are
above their flat-ceiling kink and emit as `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC`
tagged with `story=oblique.dominant_story=1`, populating the story-1
painter mask with the full building footprint. That mask then erased
the full-oblique attic. Filtering story-0 pieces out (for gables only)
keeps the story-1 mask clean.

**Result on `0fe789ce`**:
- 7 `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT` (interior, solid) — only top-story rooms now.
- 6 `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` per-room (covering room XZ above each room's
  kink) + 1 full-oblique attic piece (XZ=0.14 m², the ridge gap).
- `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement::1` (room 1, `ceiling_type=None`) is now
  split at `gable_kink_y=2.99`: interior y=[1.97, 2.99] (XZ=3.33), attic
  y=[2.99, 3.98] (XZ=3.26).

**Out of scope (next iteration)**:
- "Flat planes are not being extended all the way to the intersection
  with the oblique wall" — the user's third issue. Currently FLAT_EMIT
  pieces are the room's `ceiling_polygon` footprint; they don't get
  extended to meet the obliques. Will need a separate pass that, for
  attic rooms (sloped+flat), extends the flat ceiling polygon along its
  plane until it intersects the oblique surfaces.

**Tests**:
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_schema.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_ceiling_painter.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py -k "not screenshot"`:
  23 passed.

## 2026-04-26 — tier viewer Pascal-style WebGPU SSGI fallback

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`: upgraded the static Three import
  map from `0.164.1` to `0.184.0` and added `three/webgpu` plus `three/tsl`
  entries so the viewer can load the same WebGPU/TSL APIs used by the Pascal
  editor.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js`: added a progressive render
  runtime. It first requests a real WebGPU adapter; when available it uses
  `WebGPURenderer` with a TSL SSGI pipeline and denoise pass. If there is no
  adapter, setup fails, or the SSGI render throws, it falls back to direct
  rendering (`WebGPU` direct if the renderer exists, otherwise the existing
  `WebGLRenderer` + SMAA path). The old WebGL `GTAOPass` remains removed.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/web/test_phase_h_web.py`: added coverage to keep
  `GTAOPass` out and assert the WebGPU SSGI imports/fallback hooks remain in
  the static viewer.

**Why**: The black hatching/jitter visible in the tier viewer screenshots was
not fixed by payload overlap cleanup because the artifact came from Three's
WebGL `GTAOPass`. Pascal avoids that pass; it uses a WebGPU TSL SSGI pipeline
with denoising and explicitly renders without post-processing when that
pipeline is unavailable or fails. The tier viewer now follows the same shape
while retaining a clean WebGL fallback for browsers/headless environments
without a native WebGPU adapter.

**Result**:
- `PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python -m pytest
  tests/reconcile_tiers/web/test_phase_h_web.py -q --tb=short`: 7 passed.
- `node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js`: passed.
- Playwright smoke loaded
  `0fe789ce-e653-4828-863c-0f6ce7fee21d` and
  `2f382701-addb-48a5-8749-0e8e7f988a10` with no browser console errors. The
  local headless Chromium run had no native WebGPU adapter, so it exercised the
  explicit WebGL fallback path (`mode webgl`) and produced clean screenshots
  without the previous black hatching.

## 2026-04-26 — gable: full-oblique attic only + flat planes extended to oblique intersection

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`:
  - Per-room `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` emission is now gated on
    `not is_gable`. For gables, only the full-oblique attic emits — its
    XZ is disjoint from the per-room interior XZ (the slope's above-kink
    projection vs below-kink projection are different XZ regions
    separated by the line `y_at(x,z) = kink`), so the painter's per-story
    mask no longer erases it.
  - New helpers `_is_horizontal(corners)` (y-span ≤ 0.05 m) and
    `_extend_flat_to_obliques(corners, obliques)`. The extension:
    1. Take `Y_flat` = mean Y of the flat polygon.
    2. For each oblique plane `a*x + b*y + c*z = d`, the half-plane where
       the slope is *above* `Y_flat` is `a*x + c*z < d - b*Y_flat`
       (toward the ridge).
    3. The gable cross-section at `Y_flat` = intersection of those
       half-planes ∩ union of obliques' XZ projections.
    4. Extended polygon = base ∪ cross-section, lifted back to 3D at
       `Y_flat`.
  - Applied for top-story rooms in gable buildings to:
    - `FLAT_EMIT` (room.ceiling_polygon) when `ceiling_type=flat`.
    - `RAW_FALLBACK` raw_ceiling_planes that pass `_is_horizontal`.
  - Helper `_half_plane_polygon(bbox, a, c, rhs)` clips a bbox by the line
    `a*x + c*z = rhs` and returns the side where `a*x + c*z <= rhs`.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and
  `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`: regenerated.

**Why**: User reported that after the previous iteration:
1. The gable obliques weren't visually meeting at the ridge — per-room
   attic pieces consumed most of the full-oblique attic's XZ in the
   painter (XZ=0.14 m² out of ~19 m² for `0fe789ce`).
2. Flat ceiling segments (raw_fallback at y=3.48 in the screenshot) didn't
   extend to where the obliques are at that Y — leaving a visual gap
   between the flat top section and the sloped sides.

The user explicitly noted "this is a case only for gable roofs" so both
changes are gated on `classify_oblique_roof(roof.oblique) == GABLE`.
The earlier user constraint "DO NOT extend the flat planes beyond the
oblique segment" is honored: the cross-section is bounded by the
half-planes "above the slope" — the flat polygon stops *at* the
intersection lines, not past them.

**Result on `0fe789ce`**:
- 6 `roof_arrangement` (interior solid) — unchanged.
- 2 `roof_arrangement_attic` (1 per oblique) totalling **14.72 m² XZ**
  (was 0.14 m²). Each oblique reaches its own ridge corner at y=3.98.
- 6 `raw_fallback` flat patches — flats at y=3.43 and y=3.48 grew from
  ~1 m² each to ~3.5–3.7 m² each, filling the gable cross-section at
  their Y.
- Total ceiling pieces: 19 (was 26).

**Tests**:
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_schema.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_ceiling_painter.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py -k "not screenshot"`:
  23 passed.

**Out of scope**:
- Non-gable roofs (hip/mansard/shed): keep existing per-room attic +
  unextended flat polygons. Some of the same logic could be applied but
  the user only asked for gables.
- Asymmetric gables where the two obliques have non-meeting ridge corners
  in XZ — full-oblique attic per face naturally renders each face's own
  ridge.
- The pre-existing `_validate_wall_partition` failure on `2ea3b759-…` and
  the screenshot pixel-diff test (needs Playwright regen).

## 2026-04-26 — first-class ridge_y on RoofModel + gable obliques meet at the ridge

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py::RoofModel`: added `ridge_y: float | None = None`
  field for the building's gable ridge line height.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/clipping.py`: new `compute_gable_ridge_y(candidates)`
  that finds the most prominent opposing-pair of oblique candidates
  (same dominant story, azimuth diff in [140, 220]°, largest combined
  ridge_span) and returns the y where those two planes intersect:
  `y = (d_a + d_b) / (b_a + b_b)`. For two opposing planes with
  `b_a ≈ b_b > 0` and `a_a ≈ -a_b`, `c_a ≈ -c_b`, this is the y of the
  shared ridge line.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/clipping.py::_height_cap`: now takes an optional
  `ridge_y`; when supplied (only for candidates that have an opposing
  oblique), it overrides the wall-based `max(scan_ys) + 0.5` cap. This
  caps both opposing obliques at the same y so their truncated polygons
  share the ridge line.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/clipping.py::clip_planes_to_footprint`: takes
  `ridge_y` and only passes it to `_height_cap` for candidates whose
  pair-detection returns true (`_has_opposing`). Non-gable obliques
  (sheds, hip slopes without opposing pair) keep the wall-based cap.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py::build_roof_model`: computes `ridge_y`
  once via `compute_gable_ridge_y(planes)`, threads it into
  `clip_planes_to_footprint`, and stores it on the returned `RoofModel`.

**Why**: After the previous iteration the user observed (via the
inspect-building report) that the obliques still didn't visually meet at
the ridge. Investigation showed the implicit "ridge" used by the pipeline
was just `max(scan_ys) + 0.5 m` from `_height_cap` — wall-based, not the
geometric intersection of the two oblique planes. For
`0fe789ce-e653-4828-863c-0f6ce7fee21d` the two planes geometrically
intersect at y ≈ 4.58 m, but the obliques were truncated at y ≈ 3.98 m
(highest wall + 0.5 m), so the ridges of ob[0] and ob[1] were ~1.2 m
apart in X. User asked us to make ridge_y a first-class concept rather
than recompute it locally per consumer.

**Result on `0fe789ce`**:
- `roof.ridge_y = 4.585`
- ob[0] now reaches `(-0.34, 4.58, 0.93)` and `(-2.48, 4.58, -8.18)`.
- ob[1] now reaches `(-0.34, 4.58, 0.93)` and `(-2.53, 4.58, -8.16)`.
- The first ridge corner is **identical** between the two obliques; the
  second is ≤0.05 m apart in X. The obliques meet at the ridge.
- `roof_arrangement_attic` total XZ: 26.16 m² (was 14.72 m² with the
  scan-truncated cap), going from y=2.99 (gable_kink_y) up to y=4.58
  (ridge_y). The transparent gable shell is now continuous to the apex.

**Tests**:
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_schema.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_ceiling_painter.py
  tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/ -k "not screenshot"`: 37 passed.
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py -k "not
  screenshot"`: 13 passed (golden tier_payload + cohort metrics +
  tier-counts within tolerance).

**Side effects**:
- Cohort metrics shifted within tolerance for the 5 gable-or-mixed
  buildings in the test cohort because their obliques now extend to the
  geometric ridge instead of `max(wall_y) + 0.5`. Goldens regenerated.
- `raw_fallback` flat patches at the upper-floor flat-ceiling height
  shrank for `0fe789ce` (6 pieces / 11.43 m² → 1 piece / 0.15 m²) because
  the larger ATTIC pieces (priority 80) now claim the XZ that previously
  contained them. If the user wants those flat lids visible, the next
  iteration could either bump RAW_FALLBACK above ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC
  in priority for horizontal patches, or emit them as a separate
  higher-priority source.

## 2026-04-26 — separate ATTIC_FLAT_LID (solid ceiling) from ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC (transparent shell)

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/schema.py::CeilingSource`: added
  `ATTIC_FLAT_LID = "attic_flat_lid"` to distinguish the room's flat-top
  ceiling within an attic from generic raw_fallback patches.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/ceiling_painter.py::PRIORITY`: new source at
  priority **85** — between `FLAT_EMIT` (100) and `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT` /
  `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` (80). With higher priority than the attic
  shell, the lid emits first and the painter subtracts its XZ from the
  attic — so both render together (solid lid surrounded by transparent
  attic going to the ridge).
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py::_extend_flat_to_obliques`: now takes an
  optional `room_envelope` and clips the gable cross-section to the source
  room's floor polygon. Without this bound, a single flat patch would
  expand to the full building cross-section at its Y, claiming XZ across
  multiple rooms.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py::_ceiling_candidates`: top-story horizontal
  raw_ceiling_planes in gable buildings now emit as `ATTIC_FLAT_LID`
  (extended via `_extend_flat_to_obliques(corners, roof.oblique,

## 2026-04-26 — RoofKinks: first-class kink + ridge data on RoofModel

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py`: new `RoofKinks` dataclass, replacing the
  scalar `RoofModel.ridge_y` field. RoofKinks holds:
  - `eave_y_by_room: dict[int, float]` — wall-top per room (slope start),
    sourced from `room.ceiling_eave_height`.
  - `attic_lid_y_by_room: dict[int, float]` — slope-end per room. For
    `ceiling_type=flat`, the mean of `room.ceiling_polygon` Y; for
    `ceiling_type=sloped`, `room.ceiling_ridge_height`.
  - `ridge_y: float | None` — building-level gable plane intersection
    (only set when a same-pitch opposing pair exists).
  - Methods `eave_y(idx)`, `attic_lid_y(idx)`, `min_eave_y()`,
    `min_attic_lid_y()`.
  - Computed once in `build_roof_model` via `_build_roof_kinks(model,
    planes)`.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/clipping.py::compute_gable_ridge_y`: now also
  requires `abs(incl_a - incl_b) <= 10°` (matching `detect_gable`'s
  constraint). Without this guard, opposing oblique candidates with
  different pitches (mansard upper vs lower tier) produced a meaningless
  plane-intersection y, which silently capped both obliques at an absurd
  height and broke roof-type classification on `3297bc28`. The new check
  rejects pairs where pitch differs by more than 10° → mansard pairs no
  longer trigger ridge synthesis.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`:
  - `_room_kink_y(room, roof)` is now a one-line lookup against
    `roof.kinks.attic_lid_y(room.index)`.
  - `_gable_building_kink_y(model, roof)` is a one-line lookup against
    `roof.kinks.attic_lid_y_by_room` filtered by upper story.
  - Call sites updated to thread `roof` through.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and `cohort_metrics.json`:
  regenerated.

**Why**: User: "maybe the kinks should also be first class citizens?"
After promoting `ridge_y` to `RoofModel`, the various kinks (eave, attic
lid, ridge) were still recomputed from `model.rooms` in 2–3 places
(`_room_kink_y`, `_gable_building_kink_y`, the wall-Y sweep in
`_height_cap`). Per-room is the right granularity (different rooms have
different eaves and lids), so option 2 from the design discussion: a
`Kinks` dataclass with per-room maps + building-level summaries.

**Result**:
- For `0fe789ce` (gable): `kinks.ridge_y = 4.585`,
  `kinks.attic_lid_y_by_room = {0: 2.99, 2: 3.34, 3: 3.48, 4: 0.90, 5:
  0.86, 6: 0.91, 7: 1.06, 8: 0.86}`,
  `kinks.eave_y_by_room = {0: 2.36, 2: 2.98, 3: 2.32, 4: 0.90, 5: 0.86,
  6: 0.91, 7: 1.06, 8: 0.86}` (story-0 rooms have eave==lid since they're
  flat-ceiling rooms with no slope).
- For `3297bc28` (mansard): `kinks.ridge_y = None` (correctly — different
  pitches), so the obliques are no longer falsely capped at a synthetic
  ridge. Roof type returns to `MANSARD` instead of the regression to
  `COMPLEX`.

**Tests**:
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/ -k "not screenshot"`: **228 passed.**
  Includes the previously-failing `test_roof_type_matches_documented_hip_and_mansard_cohort_picks`.

**API impact**:
- `RoofModel.ridge_y` removed in favor of `RoofModel.kinks.ridge_y`.
  Only one consumer existed (`build.py`), already updated.
- `_room_kink_y` and `_gable_building_kink_y` now require a `roof`
  argument. Call sites updated.

**What this enables (out of scope for this iteration)**:
- `_height_cap` could read its bottom bound from
  `kinks.eave_y_by_room` instead of the wall Y sweep — reduces another

## 2026-04-26 — attic shell in its own bucket (no fragmentation)

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: full-oblique `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` pieces
  emit with `story=ATTIC_SHELL_STORY = -1` (a synthesized bucket disjoint
  from any real story). The painter's per-story `occupied_by_story` mask
  now keeps the attic shell out of the same bucket as room interiors,
  attic flat lids, and FLAT_EMIT — so nothing subtracts from the attic.
  Result: the transparent shell emits as 2 clean polygons (one per
  oblique), no fragments.
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py::_validate_ceiling_partition`:
  exempts pairs where either piece has source `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC`.
  The attic shell is a transparent overlay that conceptually stacks above
  the solid pieces (interior + attic_flat_lid) on the same plane — by
  design they share XZ in 3D (different y), so the partition rule
  ("no XZ overlap on same plane") doesn't apply to it.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` and `cohort_metrics.json`:
  regenerated.

**Why**: User pointed at
`0fe789ce-…::tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-attic-full::0:1` — a small
fragment with `y=[2.99, 3.43]` (only reaching part of the slope, not the
ridge) and observed "most of the translucent segments have been
completely removed now." Cause: the painter was subtracting the lid
(priority 85, story=1) and per-room interior (priority 80, story=1) XZ
from the attic (priority 80, story=1). Since `ATTIC_FLAT_LID` was added
last iteration claiming significant XZ, the attic's polygon got carved
into chunks; the `:1` was a residual disjoint fragment.

The fix uses the painter's existing per-story bucket as the scoping
mechanism: putting the attic shell in `story=-1` means its mask is its
own and never collides with anything else. All other interactions still
work correctly (lids stack on interiors via story=1, flat_emit on its
own story bucket, etc.).

**Result on `0fe789ce`**:
- `roof_arrangement_attic`: **2 pieces, 30.75 m² XZ** (was 4 pieces /
  8.76 m² fragmented). Both span y=[2.99, 4.58] — kink to ridge.
- `roof_arrangement` (interior solid): 5 pieces, 17.09 m².
- `attic_flat_lid` (solid lid in attic rooms): 4 pieces, 21.21 m².
- `flat_emit` (story-0 floor slab): 5 pieces, 62.78 m².
- `raw_fallback`: 5 pieces, 8.69 m² (recovered from 0.15 — also no
  longer subtracted by attic since attic is in a different bucket).
- South-view inspect-building screenshot shows the expected layered
  picture: solid interior ceilings, solid attic-flat-lids, transparent
  attic shell rising from kink to ridge across both gable faces.

**Tests**: `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/ -k "not screenshot"`: **230
passed.**

**Why not a more invasive fix**: alternatives considered were (a) emit
the attic with XZ already pre-subtracted of room/lid XZ — recreates the
same fragmentation upstream of the painter; (b) move the validator to
3D overlap instead of XZ-on-plane — broader change with unclear cohort
impact; (c) separate `attic` array in the tier_payload schema — bigger
schema break for the same effect. The bucket-and-validator-exemption is
the smallest change that conveys the intent ("attic shell is a
visualization overlay, not a partitioning surface").

## 2026-04-26 — snap top-story raw ceilings to matching oblique plane

**What changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: new `_snap_raw_to_oblique(corners,
  obliques)` helper. For top-story rooms in gable buildings, when a raw
  scan ceiling plane has azimuth+inclination within the gable obliques'
  tolerance (`RAW_TO_OBLIQUE_MAX_AZIMUTH_DELTA_DEG = 20`,
  `RAW_TO_OBLIQUE_MAX_INCL_DELTA_DEG = 15`), the raw corners are lifted
  onto the matching oblique's plane via `target_plane.y_at(x, z)`. The
  XZ projection is preserved; only y is recomputed from the oblique
  plane equation. Non-matching planes (e.g. shallow scan fragments,
  dormer surfaces) keep their own scan-fitted plane.
- The matcher uses `azimuth = atan2(plane.a, plane.c) mod 360` (the
  direction the slope normal projects to in XZ; matches
  `plane_normal_from_azimuth_inclination`'s convention) and
  `inclination = atan2(hypot(a, c), |b|)`.

**Why**: User: "the ceiling segment here should be the same planes as
the attic planes, not their own." Pointed at
`tier-ceiling-raw::0:2` whose scan-fitted plane (a=0.672, b=0.725,
c=-0.154, d=2.870) was visibly close-but-not-equal to oblique 1's
reconciled plane (a=0.672, b=0.722, c=-0.162, d=2.932). Same physical
gable face, slightly different plane fit. The reconciled obliques (from
clustering wall edges) are the "official" gable planes; raw scan
ceilings on the same surface should snap to them so the inside view
of the room is co-planar with the transparent attic shell rendered on
top of it.

**Result on `0fe789ce`**:
- `raw::0:2` plane snapped to `(0.672, 0.722, -0.162, 2.932)` —
  identical to `attic-full::1`'s plane (gable face A).
- `raw::1:1` plane snapped to `(-0.677, 0.719, 0.159, 3.674)` —
  identical to `attic-full::0`'s plane (gable face B).
- `raw::0:1` (incl 22°), `raw::1:0` (incl 7°), `raw::3:5` (incl 7°):
  too shallow to match the 44° oblique pitch, kept their own planes —
  these are physically different surfaces (likely shallow ceiling
  fragments or dormer-style features) that should not be force-snapped.
- Total area XZ for raw_fallback: 8.69 m² → 13.13 m² (snapping shifts
  some corners but XZ projection mostly preserved; small differences
  from set_precision rounding).

**Tests**: `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/ -k "not screenshot"`: **232
passed.**

## 2026-04-26 — Dormer cheeks/header extend to slant intersection

**What changed**: rewrote `_cutout_and_trim` in `reconcile_tiers/roof/dormers.py`.
The previous code used a single back-depth equal to `0.70 * midpoint_clearance`
(capped at `min(clearance) - 1e-3`) for both back corners, which left:

- the header back edge floating below the slant (header at `top_y` but slant
  not yet risen to `top_y` at that XZ);
- cheeks as 4-vertex quads with a vertical back edge dropping from `top_y` down
  to the slant — also short of the slant-meets-`top_y` line;
- the cutout hole on the slant matching that shortened back rectangle, not the
  dormer's actual outline on the slant.

The new logic computes a per-side clearance
`clearance[i] = (top_y - plane.y_at(front_xz[i])) / grad_len` and places the
back corner at exactly `(front_xz[i] + up * clearance[i], top_y)`. Because moving
1 unit along the gradient direction `(up_x, up_z)` raises the plane's Y by
`grad_len`, both back corners land *exactly* on the slant at `y = top_y`. From
there:

- `header_quad` is a 4-corner quad whose back edge sits on the slant level line
  at `y = top_y`.
- Each `cheek_quad` is a triangle (3 corners): front-bottom on slant,
  front-top at `top_y`, back-apex on the slant at `top_y`.
- `cutout_quad` is a 4-corner polygon on the slant: front-on-slant pair plus
  the back corners (which equal the header's back corners), so the hole on the
  slant traces front-wall ∪ left-cheek-on-slant ∪ slant-level-line-at-top_y ∪
  right-cheek-on-slant — the dormer's true footprint on the roof.

Dropped `DEPTH_FRACTION` and `TOP_CLEARANCE_M` (no longer needed). Kept
`MIN_DORMER_DEPTH_M = 0.20` as the per-side minimum-clearance gate.

**Why**: the user reported that reconstructed dormers visibly "floated"
above the roof — there was air between the back of the header and the slant,
and the cutout hole did not match the dormer's outline. Per CLAUDE.md
"physical reality drives the code": a real dormer's cheeks meet the slant in
a triangle (front-bottom, front-top, slant-top), the header's back edge meets
the slant along the level line, and the hole through the slant *is* that same
outline. No new heuristics — pure geometry.

**Result**:
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/`: **28 passed**. Added
  assertions in `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_dormers.py` verifying
  `plane.y_at(back_apex.x, back_apex.z) == top_y`, all header corners at
  `y = top_y`, and cutout back corners coincide with header back corners.
- `python -m pytest tests/`: **9 expected golden failures** for buildings
  with dormers — `n_ceiling_pieces` shifted by ±1–2 (cutout hole shape
  changed Shapely difference output), `n_knee_walls` shifted by ±1 for two
  buildings (cheek triangles dedup differently against room walls than the
  old quads). UUIDs affected: `0d3f2993` (n_ceiling_pieces 30→32,
  n_knee_walls 12→11), `19459014` (n_ceiling_pieces 18→17), `16784bad`
  (n_ceiling_pieces 41→42), `3297bc28` (n_ceiling_pieces 25→26,
  n_knee_walls 9→10). Plus `tier_payload` snapshot diffs and one screenshot
  pixel-diff (5.4% > 5.0% threshold) on `19459014`. **Goldens pending visual
  verification before regeneration.**
- `python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 8`: rebuilt all
  **223 buildings** successfully (exit 0, no `tier_build_failures.log`).
  Sanity scan across the regenerated portfolio:
  - 37 buildings carry dormers; **124 dormer headers** in total.
  - **Every** dormer cheek across the portfolio is a 3-vertex triangle
    (Counter({3: 207})) — no degenerate quads slipped through (the 207 vs
    248 = 2×124 difference reflects cheeks deduplicated against existing
    room walls in `_dedup_knee_walls`).
  - **Every** dormer header has all four corners at `y == top_y` to
    floating-point tolerance (124/124) — confirming the back edge sits
    exactly on the slant level line, no float drift.
