## 2026-04-28 (followup) — Broader wing-clip and + / T-shape decomposition

### What changed
- User reported `19459014`, `3297bc28`, `0d3f2993` still looked wrong: the per-room arrangement fix from the prior entry left the **building-level** ceiling pieces (full attic shells, oblique-split pieces, v2 visual shells) still spanning across wings.
- Moved wing helpers (`compute_wings_for_model`, `wing_polygon_for_room`, `wing_polygon_for_xz_polygon`, `filter_by_wing_xz`, `clip_3d_polygon_to_wing`) from `reconcile_tiers/build.py` into `reconcile_tiers/_core/wing_decomposition.py` so `assemble/visual_shell.py` and other consumers can reach them. `build.py` retains thin wrappers for backwards compatibility.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py` `_ceiling_candidates(...)`: introduced `_emit_wing_clipped(corners, plane, source, locator_fn, story, arrangement_cell_id=None)` that intersects the XZ projection of `corners` with the corners' best-overlap wing and re-evaluates Y on `plane`. Applied to all four building-level emit paths:
  - `roof.oblique_split` → `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement::{idx}` and `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-attic::{idx}` (both below-kink and above-kink slices).
  - The fallback `roof.oblique` loop (`if not roof.oblique_split:`).
  - The `is_gable` full-shell loop → `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-attic-full::{obl_idx}`.
  Locator IDs gain a `:{part_idx}` suffix only when the wing-clip splits a single 3D polygon into multiple pieces, so existing 1:1 elements keep their numbering.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/visual_shell.py` `assemble_visual_shells(uuid, roof, model=None)`: now accepts the `BuildingModel` and applies the same `clip_3d_polygon_to_wing` to each gable-end oblique. v2 `tier-shell-gable-end::{idx}[:{part_idx}]` shells no longer extend across wings.
- `reconcile_tiers/_core/wing_decomposition.py` `_coalesce_macro_wing_boxes(...)`: tightened the macro-wing graph so a thin connector strip (≤ `_THIN_CAP_MAX_WIDTH_M = 0.75 m`) between two large boxes does NOT bridge them. Thin singletons are then absorbed into whichever large component shares the longest edge with them. Rationale: + and T-shaped buildings (e.g. `0d3f2993`, footprint 156 m² with 7 grid-decomposed boxes) used to fuse all four large masses into a single wing because each pair was joined by a 0.4 m strip — the new rule keeps the four large masses separate while still attaching the strips to the correct mass.
- Regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/{f40dcc9f,05cecad4,19459014,16784bad,3297bc28,0d3f2993}.json` and `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json` for the cohort metrics that legitimately changed.

### Why
The earlier wing-aware fix only constrained the per-room `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-room` pieces; the user's screenshots showed transparent gable shells (`tier-shell-gable-end`, `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-attic-full`) still extending across wings on the same three buildings. The audit confirmed the leak: `3297bc28::tier-shell-gable-end::1` had bbox `x[-4.69, -0.60] z[-4.06, 3.35]`, crossing from the extension wing into the main wing. For `0d3f2993` the situation was worse — the wing decomposer collapsed everything into a single wing because of the thin-strip bridging, so no clip applied at all. Both gaps are now closed.

### Result
- Cross-wing leak audit (Shapely 0.05 m buffer tolerance, leak ≥ 0.5 m²) on the three reported UUIDs across both `tier_payload.json` (v1) and `tier_payload_v2.json` (v2): **0 leaks**, down from 1 (3297bc28 v1 attic-full) + 1 (3297bc28 v2 shell) + 4 (0d3f2993 v2 shells, which were previously hidden behind the single-wing collapse).
- Cohort metric deltas (intentional, captured in `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`):
  - `05cecad4` total ceiling XZ area 70.17 → 70.16 (tiny boundary noise from the new clip on a single-wing building)
  - `16784bad` total ceiling XZ area 172.31 → 160.27 (full attic shell now constrained to its wing)
  - `3297bc28` n_ceiling_pieces 22 → 19, area 131.74 → 129.28
  - `0d3f2993` n_ceiling_pieces 54 → 53, area 272.62 → 251.33
- Test suite: 322 passed, 2 deselected (same pre-existing failures as the prior entry).
- Open: visual confirmation in the viewer with the user. The v2 envelope (`--envelope v2`, `tier_payload_v2.json`) is what the viewer uses for the transparent shells; users on the default v1 build will only see the v1 attic-full elements.

## 2026-04-28 — Extend slab side gaps to attached descent bottoms

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/wall_pairs.py`: wall-pair runs now carry endpoint bottom support values from any descent strip sharing the wall endpoint. `within_story` slab side caps use those endpoint bottoms instead of always starting at the upper floor Y, so short-end gap caps close down to adjacent descent strips at exterior/story transitions.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_wall_pairs.py`: added a regression where a wall-thickness slab end is attached to perpendicular descent strips with lower bottoms than the paired walls themselves.

### Why
User reported `19459014-f39b-4bf6-945e-c5b50930dea3::tier-gap::slab:r8w2-r9w0:within_story:1` stopped at the upper floor (`y=-1.398`) even though the visible attached descent strips on rooms 8 and 9 continue lower. In building terms the short side cap was closing only the room-to-room wall-thickness slab, not the full vertical corner support down to the descent bottom.

### Result
- Rebuilt `19459014-f39b-4bf6-945e-c5b50930dea3`; the locator now resolves with bottom vertices at `y=-1.886651`, matching the lower attached descent strip bottom.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_wall_pairs.py tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_gaps.py -q` — 19 passed.

## 2026-04-28 — Reject stitches that pierce existing walls or land outside the footprint

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/_core/footprint.py` (new): factored `story_footprint_context`, `is_xz_supported_by_story_footprint`, and `is_stitch_edge_unsupported_by_story_footprint` into a shared module so the construction stage (extract) and the assembly stage (assemble) share one definition of "supported by the scan-derived footprint".
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/stitches.py`: replaced the legacy collinear-only `_segment_overlaps_wall_run` with `_segment_conflicts_with_wall_run`, which also rejects stitch lines whose interior crosses an existing wall edge. Numerical noise at endpoints (T-junction projections, shared corners) is masked by a `WALL_OVERLAP_BUFFER_M`-tolerance check — Shapely's bare `crosses` predicate fires on intersections sitting 1e-16 from an endpoint. Promoted `_stitch_closure_groups` to public `stitch_closure_groups`. Added an L-corner footprint guard: candidates whose corner falls outside the story's buffered convex hull (or > `STITCH_MAX_ROOM_SUPPORT_DISTANCE_M` from any room polygon) are dropped before legs/cap are emitted.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/gaps_to_pieces.py`: pre-computes a closure-aware drop set. If any leg of an L-stitch fails footprint support, every piece in that closure (legs + floor cap + ceiling cap) is dropped together so the renderer never sees a half-open L. `_story_footprint_context` / `_stitch_is_unsupported_by_story_footprint` now come from `_core/footprint.py`.
- Tests: added `test_l_stitch_rejected_when_a_leg_pierces_an_existing_wall` (synthetic gable barrier) and `test_e9dddee6_gable_piercing_l_stitch_no_longer_rendered` (building-specific by-geometry assertion). Updated cohort expectations in `test_stitch_wall_gaps_match_legacy_cohort_output[f40dcc9f]` and `test_cohort_gap_piece_counts_include_gap_stitch_and_exterior_surfaces[f40dcc9f]`.
- Regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/{f40dcc9f,05cecad4,19459014,3297bc28}.json` (only `gaps` differ — `16784bad` and `0d3f2993` also have pre-existing ceiling drift left for separate handling).

### Why
User reported on `e9dddee6-297a-43f5-b862-90091889ea39` that `tier-gap::stitch:2:30` and `tier-gap::stitch_floor:2:32` "make 0 sense": the stitch was on the top floor and crossed straight through the gable wall. Inspection of the tier payload confirmed the L-stitch produced two legs + a floor cap whose endpoints sat on opposite sides of the gable. The assembler had a per-piece footprint filter that dropped the second leg (its midpoint fell outside the buffered hull) but kept the first leg and the cap — leaving a vertical wall + triangular floor pocket hanging across the gable, with the closing leg gone. Two underlying rule defects: (a) the legacy `_segment_overlaps_wall_run` only caught collinear overlap, not perpendicular crossings, and (b) the assembler footprint filter operated per-piece, so caps survived even when their parent legs were dropped — breaking L-closure atomicity.

### Result
- For `e9dddee6` story 2, the gable-piercing L-stitch is no longer constructed; the original `stitch:2:30` / `stitch_floor:2:32` corners (anchored at `(-0.690, -1.618, -6.172)` ↔ `(-1.164, -1.618, -6.529)`) are absent from the rendered payload. Note `stitch:2:30` *id* is reused for an unrelated stitch with different corners — sequence numbers reshuffle when upstream stitches get dropped.
- For the cohort building `f40dcc9f`, the previously-emitted cap pair traced back to an L whose second leg crossed room 6's wall 4 from outside the room — a real geometric violation the legacy collinear check didn't catch. New construction emits 8 stitches (matching the 9-room contract `{stitch: 8}`) with no caps; assembly leaves 5 stitches after wall-overlap filtering. Both cohort tests updated.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_stitches.py tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_gaps_to_pieces.py -q` — 26 passed (incl. 2 new).
- Pre-existing failures (not caused by this change): 2 cohort-metric `n_ceiling_pieces` drifts (`16784bad`, `0d3f2993`), `test_tier_counts_vs_current_tier_index_within_five_percent`, screenshot diff for `16784bad`, and 2 `tier_payload_matches_golden_snapshot` cases (`16784bad`, `0d3f2993`) where ceiling pieces also drift independently. Those belong to the broader uncommitted refactor in flight on this branch.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- The `MUTUAL_THRESH_M = 0.60` mutual-best gating. The current "mutual only when ≤0.60m" is backwards (looser distance gates should require *more* evidence, not less), but the wall-crossing + L-corner footprint guards remove the visible defect without changing pairing semantics — which has wider corpus impact.
- L-corner side selection (interior vs. exterior of the building). The footprint guard captures the bad case; rewriting the candidate selection is a larger refactor with unclear blast radius.

## 2026-04-28 (followup 2) — Side-by-side wing detection: perpendicular-width gate

### What changed
- User reported `71ee522c::tier-ceiling-computed-oblique-room::4:0:0` and `a492a5d6::tier-ceiling-computed-oblique-room::6:0:0` still cross into the visible building extension.
- `a492a5d6`'s footprint decomposed into two large boxes — main `9.68×6.38 m` and east extension `2.60×6.68 m` — but the existing `_SIDE_BY_SIDE_MIN_SHARED_RATIO = 0.55` rule merged them because they shared a near-full-height vertical edge. Result: a single wing covering the whole building, no clip applied. Same root cause for the over-merged components in `71ee522c` and on the cohort buildings `05cecad4` / `16784bad` (both single-wing previously).
- `reconcile_tiers/_core/wing_decomposition.py`: introduced `_FRAGMENT_MIN_PERP_RATIO = 0.4` and added a perpendicular-dimension check to `_boxes_same_macro_wing(...)`. Two boxes that share an edge with a high `shared/parallel_dim` ratio now also need their perpendicular dimensions reasonably balanced (`min/max ≥ 0.4`); otherwise the narrower box is recognised as an extension rather than a co-equal fragment of the same wing. Applied symmetrically for vertical and horizontal touches. The original `_THIN_CAP_MAX_WIDTH_M ≤ 0.75 m` thin-cap absorbing rule is unchanged — narrow caps that genuinely belong to the touching mass still merge.
- Regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/{f40dcc9f,05cecad4,19459014,16784bad,3297bc28,0d3f2993}.json` and `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`.

### Why
The decomposer was treating `9.68 × 6.38 m` and `2.60 × 6.68 m` as "two halves of the same long mass" because the shared edge ran most of both heights. In residential buildings that pattern almost always means one main mass plus a perpendicular extension, not a single rectangular barn split in two — so the perpendicular ratio is the discriminator. The 0.4 threshold lets clearly-balanced fragments stay merged (e.g. `0.5/1.0`) while splitting clear extensions (e.g. `0.27/1.0` for `a492a5d6`).

### Result
- `a492a5d6`: 1 wing → 2 wings (main 61.7 m² + east extension 17.4 m²).
- `71ee522c`: 2 wings → 4 wings (main 79.1 m², three extensions: 35.5 m², 18.2 m², 17.2 m²).
- `2f382701`: 5 wings → 6 wings.
- `0d3f2993`: 3 wings → 4 wings (the previously merged `{box 2 (3.47 × 5.85), box 3 (13.82 × 5.65)}` mass is now split — 78 m² main + 21 m² west extension).
- `05cecad4`, `16784bad`: previously single-wing buildings now decompose into main + extension, so wing-aware clipping starts applying where it didn't before.
- Test suite: 334 passed, 2 deselected (same pre-existing failures as before this branch).


## 2026-04-28 — Drop noisy `tier-ceiling-raw` planes from `tier_payload.json`

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: added `_filter_noisy_raw_candidates(candidates, model, roof, drops_sink)` plus four threshold constants (`RAW_CEILING_REDUNDANT_LEFTOVER_MAX_M2 = 0.5`, `RAW_CEILING_JUNK_TRIANGLE_MAX_AREA_M2 = 1.0`, `RAW_CEILING_JUNK_TRIANGLE_MIN_YSPAN_M = 0.30`, `RAW_CEILING_LOW_QUALITY_THRESHOLD = 0.55`). The gate combines three rules — `redundant` (leftover after subtracting higher-priority story-mates < 0.5 m²), `junk_triangle` (3-corner, sub-1.0 m², tilted >0.30 m), `low_quality` (FLAT-classified room AND `score_raw_plane()` < 0.55, mirroring the v2 gate). Wired it into `build_tier_payload` AFTER `compute_room_ceiling_voids` so void detection still sees the full pre-gate candidate list (a noisy raw plane still indicates "the scan saw something here") while the painter / final payload only sees the filtered set.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py:_build_one`: added `tier_payload_drops.json` sidecar (written next to `tier_payload.json`) listing every dropped raw with `{locator_id, reason, n_corners, area_xz_m2, y_span_m, story}`. Cleared on rebuilds with no drops so the file always reflects the latest run. `build_tier_payload` accepts an optional `drops_sink: list | None` kwarg; existing callers and tests are unaffected by signature change.
- Tests (`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`): added 4 stub-based unit tests + 2 cohort tests parametrised on the user-cited UUIDs (`e9dddee6` rooms 8:8/8:11, `893d4535` 4:9). Each cohort test asserts the locator is absent from `payload.ceiling` AND present in the `drops_sink` with the expected reason.
- Regenerated `tests/golden/tier_payload/{16784bad,0d3f2993}.json` and the matching entries in `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`. Diff-checked all 6 cohort goldens beforehand: only those 2 had ceiling locator changes from the gate (16784bad: -11 raws, 0d3f2993: -2 raws); the other 4 cohort goldens were already drifting on this branch from unrelated work and were left alone.

### Why
User pointed at five `tier-ceiling-raw` locators (`e9dddee6 8:11/8:8`, `b53c11aa 2:3`, `b8f923d9 1:6`, `893d4535 4:9`) and said "many of the raw ceilings make 0 sense to show especially if they're super noisy". All 5 are tiny (≤0.91 m²), most are 3-corner triangles with high Y-span (>0.4 m). A corpus survey across all 223 buildings (108 of which have raw ceilings, 841 raws total) found 74.2% of raws overlap a higher-priority computed ceiling on the same story (visually redundant) and 25.8% are orphans (the only ceiling signal there — must be preserved).

The gate was designed multi-signal so a single threshold couldn't both drop the user's tiny noisy fragments and delete the 217 orphan attic raws that ARE the only ceiling source in their (story, room). Calibration against the corpus reports zero "alarm" buildings — i.e. zero stories where the gate would drop every raw without a higher-priority replacement. Every drop has a physical justification: redundant pieces would only contribute a sliver after the painter's `poly.difference(bucket)` step; junk triangles are RoomPlan plane-fitting artifacts (a tilted 3-corner sub-1m² fragment isn't anything a human would label as ceiling); low-quality pieces in flat-ceiling rooms fail the same `score_raw_plane()` gate v2 already uses.

User chose pipeline-side drop over a viewer toggle to keep the payload clean by default; the sidecar mitigates the "lost from audit trails" tradeoff.

### Result
- 5/5 user-cited locators absent from re-emitted `tier_payload.json` (verified end-to-end through `build_tier_payload`); each appears in `tier_payload_drops.json` with the gate's reason.
- Corpus-wide simulation (all 223 buildings) drops 622 of 841 raws (~74%). Reason mix: 487 redundant, 138 junk triangles. Zero buildings lose all raws on a story without a computed alternative.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py` — 31 passed (incl. 6 new gate tests).
- `python -m pytest tests/` — 334 passed, 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (`test_tier_counts_vs_current_tier_index_within_five_percent` — branch-state tier-index drift; `test_screenshot_pixel_diff_against_goldens` — branch-state pixel diff at 9% vs 5% threshold; both reproduced with the gate disabled).

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- The viewer rendering / toggles (`reconcile_tiers/web/`). User chose pipeline-side drop, so the viewer stays as-is — the noisy fragments simply aren't in the payload.
- `support_quality` field in the schema. The score is computed and used internally; we did not retrofit it onto every emitted RAW_FALLBACK piece (would break byte-compat without value to callers — only v2 RAW_SCAN sets it today).
- The v2 envelope gate (`assemble/thermal_envelope.py:203-215`). It already does the right thing for v2; v1 now matches via the same `score_raw_plane()` + 0.55 threshold inside `_filter_noisy_raw_candidates`.
- Extraction-time thresholds in `extract/ceilings.py` (`NOISY_PLANE_DROP_TAU_M`, `RIDGE_EAVE_MAX_DELTA_M`, `INCLINED_CEILING_MIN_AREA_M2`, etc.) — they're calibrated for "should this room be flat?" and orthogonal to the visual-clutter problem this change solves.
- `ATTIC_FLAT_LID` (priority 75) candidates. They pass the gate unconditionally because they're synthesised geometry (top-gable rooms with a horizontal raw plane extended to obliques), not raw scan noise. The unit test `test_raw_gate_keeps_attic_flat_lid_unconditionally` locks this in.

## 2026-04-28 — Element-flag queue + cohort defect scanner

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/{__init__,rules,cohort_scan}.py`: new soft-defect audit package. `rules.py` implements 7 rules over the dict-form `tier_payload.json` — `ceiling_orientation_inverted`, `ceiling_below_floor`, `out_of_envelope`, `ceiling_coverage_gap`, `knee_wall_misplaced`, `dormer_without_host_slope`, `silent_drop`. Each returns `FlagItem` dicts conforming to the `flag-queue/v1` schema (`{id, locator, kind, parts, rule, note, severity, evidence, dismissed}`). `cohort_scan.py` is a CLI: `--uuid <uuid>` writes a per-building queue at `.context/flag-queues/<uuid>/auto-scan-<ts>.json` plus an `auto-scan-latest.json` pointer; `--all` walks `pipeline-outputs/` and writes `.context/cohort-defect-scan/<ts>/index.json` ranking rules by frequency. Geometry helpers, thresholds, and rule logic are ported from `archive/legacy-runtime/reconcile/inspect_building/audit.py` (which is unchanged); `ceiling_below_floor` and `dormer_without_host_slope` are new.
- `reconcile/viewer_server.py`: two new endpoints. `POST /flag-queue` accepts `{building_uuid, items[], screenshot_data_url?, source?}` and writes `.context/flag-queues/<uuid>/<ts>.json` (+ `<ts>.png` if a data-URL screenshot is provided). `GET /flag-queues?uuid=<uuid>` returns the latest auto-scan queue (or `{items:[], source:null}`). New helpers `_is_safe_uuid`, `_split_locator`, `_send_json`. Switched the workspace-anchor path from `REPO_ROOT` (which `.resolve()`'d through the `reconcile/` symlink and pointed at `archive/legacy-runtime/`) to a new `WORKSPACE_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent` (unresolved) so flag queues land in the real `tirana/.context/`.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/{viewer-tiers.html,viewer-tiers.css,viewer-tiers-main.js}`: new "Flagged for triage" sidebar (`#flag-panel`) with collapsible header, list of items, per-item dismiss toggle, per-item note textarea, "Clear" / "Send queue" buttons, status line. Right-click handler extended: plain right-click still copies the locator UID; `Shift+right-click` adds it to the queue. On building load, viewer fetches `/flag-queues?uuid=<uuid>` to pre-populate the sidebar with auto-scan items the user can refine, dismiss, or merge with manual flags. "Send queue" POSTs the merged set with a canvas screenshot (`renderer.domElement.toDataURL`) to the new endpoint.
- `.agents/skills/triage-queue/SKILL.md`: new skill documenting the queue schema, the producers (viewer + cohort scanner), and the Claude-side batch-triage protocol — group items by rule, run `debug-element` on representatives in parallel, propose fixes that target the rule rather than each instance.

### Why
User reported the existing debug loop is the dominant time-sink: spot a defect in `viewer-tiers.html`, copy a UID, paste to Claude, describe the symptom, wait for `debug-element`, repeat 5–10× per building. Three observable costs — manual spotting, per-UUID handoff with no screenshot, and per-element triage that misses recurring patterns. User picked option (1)+(2) from the brainstorm: handoff (one-click flag in viewer) + cohort defect scanner, deferring a live in-viewer agent sidebar. Operating unit is one building's queue at a time.

The two producers (viewer + cohort scan) write the same schema so a single Claude-side protocol consumes both. The compose step — viewer pre-populates from the latest auto-scan — turns the viewer into a *review* surface for the scanner, not a from-scratch input device, which was the user's stated unit-of-work preference.

### Result
- `python -m reconcile_tiers.audit.cohort_scan --uuid 016980bc-6762-4022-bfbf-17df4112e10c` → 13 items, all `ceiling_below_floor` (a real cluster — flat-ceiling pieces ~20cm below the room floor of every flagged room, same delta repeating across stories; needs follow-up to determine whether the rule is over-triggering on lower-story ceilings or whether it's a real defect).
- Spot-check on 3 more buildings: `0a5032e9` 0 items (clean), `05cecad4` 0 items (clean), `0d3f2993` 9 items mixed across `out_of_envelope` (×6), `ceiling_below_floor`, `ceiling_coverage_gap`, `dormer_without_host_slope` — looks like real signal.
- `node --check viewer-tiers-main.js` clean. `python -c "import reconcile.viewer_server"` clean.
- Server smoke: `GET /flag-queues?uuid=016980bc-...` returns the 13-item queue. `POST /flag-queue` with one manual item writes `.context/flag-queues/<uuid>/<ts>.json` and returns `{ok:true, queue_path, item_count}`. Initial run hit a path-resolution bug (`relative_to(REPO_ROOT)` blew up because REPO_ROOT was the symlink-resolved archive path while queues were written to the workspace path); fixed by introducing `WORKSPACE_ROOT` and using it consistently.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- Live in-viewer agent sidebar (option 3 from the brainstorm). Deferred per user's scope-down.
- `tests/audit/test_rules.py`. Skipped for this iteration to keep the loop tight; the 7 rules are mostly direct ports of the legacy audit's already-exercised logic, and the cohort spot-check provides a sanity signal. Will add fixture-based tests if rules drift.
- `archive/legacy-runtime/reconcile/inspect_building/audit.py`. Left as-is — `reconcile_tiers/audit/rules.py` is the live module; the archive copy stays as historical reference.
- The viewer's existing copy-locator behaviour. Plain right-click still copies the UID; Shift is the only new modifier.

## 2026-04-28 — Flag overlays + Shift+right-click note popover

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`: added a `<div id="flag-popover">` floating dialog (locator readout + note textarea + Cancel/Add buttons) under `<main>`. Updated the `#status` hint copy to mention `Shift+right-click` for flagging.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.css`: appended `#flag-popover` styles (positioned, blurred backdrop, focused-textarea highlight, primary-styled Add button).
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js`:
  - Added `FLAG_AUTO_MATERIAL` (red, `0xdc2626`) and `FLAG_MANUAL_MATERIAL` (cyan, `0x06b6d4`) `LineBasicMaterial`s with `depthTest: false` so the overlays read through occluding geometry.
  - Added a top-level `flagOverlayGroup` (`THREE.Group`, `renderOrder: 999`) attached once to the scene at module init. Deliberately NOT marked `userData.tierPreview = true` so it survives `clearBuildingMeshes` on building swap; its children are managed entirely by `syncFlagOverlays`.
  - Added `syncFlagOverlays()` — clears the group's children, walks the current building's queue, and creates a per-item edge wireframe by reusing `mesh.userData.selectionBox` (the same OBB used by the existing yellow selection helper), with a world-aligned bbox fallback. Auto-flagged items get red, manual items cyan. Dismissed items are skipped.
  - Hooked `syncFlagOverlays()` into `renderFlagPanel()` so overlays update on every queue mutation (add, dismiss, send, clear, auto-scan pre-populate).
  - Replaced the immediate add-on-shift+right-click behavior with `openFlagPopover(uid, clientX, clientY)`. The popover positions itself relative to `<main>`, clamps to the viewport, focuses the textarea, accepts `Enter` to commit / `Esc` to cancel, and closes on outside-click. Submit calls `addManualFlag(uid, note)`.
  - Extended `addManualFlag(locator, note=null)` to accept a note. If the same locator is already manually flagged, a non-empty new note updates the existing entry's note instead of creating a duplicate.
- `reconcile/viewer_server.py`: switched the static-file serving root from `ROOT_DIR` (the resolved-symlink legacy `archive/legacy-runtime/reconcile/`) to `WORKSPACE_ROOT` (the unresolved tirana root). The default `/` redirect now points to `/reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`; the legacy `/viewer.html` URL is mapped through to `/reconcile/viewer.html`. This lets a single `viewer_server.py` instance serve the V2 tier viewer, the V1 viewer, `pipeline-outputs/<uuid>/*`, and the new `/flag-queue` + `/flag-queues` endpoints — replacing the `python -m http.server` workflow that `inspect_building.sh` (and habit) used to spin up for the tier viewer.

### Why
User feedback after the first cut of the flag-queue: the queue was usable but not visual — flagged items only appeared in the sidebar list, not in the 3D scene, so the user couldn't see where in the building the cluster of `ceiling_below_floor` flags actually sat. Second piece of feedback: shift+right-click added the locator with no opportunity to attach a note in the moment of flagging, forcing a second round-trip to the sidebar textarea. Both reduce the flag-queue's value as a "fast capture" surface.

The serving-root change closes a separate gap I hadn't seen on the first pass: the V2 tier viewer was historically served via `python -m http.server` from the workspace root (per `reconcile/inspect_building.sh:115-122`), which has no flag-queue endpoints. Without serving-root unification, the new feature would only have worked for users who manually launched `viewer_server.py`, opened a non-default URL, AND had no orthophotos either (since the V1 viewer is at the legacy URL). The tradeoff: existing bookmarks at `http://localhost:VIEWER_PORT/viewer.html` redirect to `/reconcile/viewer.html` rather than 404 — symlinked `reconcile/` continues to resolve.

### Result
- `node --check viewer-tiers-main.js` clean. `python -c "import reconcile.viewer_server"` clean.
- Server smoke (single `viewer_server.py` instance):
  - `GET /reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html` → 200.
  - `GET /reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js` → 200.
  - `GET /pipeline-outputs/<uuid>/tier_payload.json` → 200.
  - `GET /flag-queues?uuid=<uuid>` → 13 items as before.
  - HTML and JS payloads contain `#flag-popover`, `#flag-popover-note`, `syncFlagOverlays`, `openFlagPopover`, `flagOverlayGroup`.
- Visual verification (overlays render red on auto-flags, cyan on manual flags; popover appears at cursor on Shift+right-click; submit-with-Enter adds note; outside-click dismisses) is left for the user — Claude-in-Chrome was unavailable in this session.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- The existing yellow selection helper. The flag overlay is a separate group with `depthTest: false` so the two coexist; clicking a flagged element still gets the standard yellow OBB on top of the red/cyan flag overlay.
- `reconcile/inspect_building.sh`. It still spins up its own `python -m http.server` for the screenshot harness; it doesn't need the flag endpoints, and changing it would couple the screenshot pipeline to the viewer server's lifecycle.
- The flag-queue file format. The popover's note submission still routes through the same `addManualFlag(locator, note)` path that produces the existing `flag-queue/v1` schema — the queue file shape is unchanged.

## 2026-04-28 — Multi-select batch flagging

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js`:
  - Added `MULTI_SELECT_MATERIAL` (emerald `0x10b981`, `depthTest: false`), a top-level `multiSelectGroup` (renderOrder 998, sits below the flag overlay group), and a `multiSelection: Set<string>` of locator UIDs.
  - `toggleMultiSelect(uid)`, `clearMultiSelect()`, `syncMultiSelectOverlays()` — same pattern as the flag overlay group, reusing `createFlagHelper(mesh, MULTI_SELECT_MATERIAL)` so the OBB extraction is shared.
  - Click handler now branches on `event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey`: Cmd/Ctrl+click toggles into multi-select; plain click clears multi-select and selects single. Click on empty space (no locator hit) also clears multi-select unless Cmd/Ctrl is held.
  - Shift+right-click now branches on multi-selection state: if `multiSelection.size >= 2 && multiSelection.has(uid)`, the popover opens with the whole selected group as targets; otherwise single-element behavior is unchanged.
  - `openFlagPopover` rewritten to accept `locators: string[]`. Single-element mode shows the locator string verbatim; multi-element mode shows a `<strong>N elements</strong>` header, the first 3 locators, and `+N more` if longer. Add button label switches between "Add to queue" and "Add N to queue". Placeholder text adapts.
  - `commitFlagPopover` iterates the locator list and calls `addManualFlag(locator, note)` per item, with the same shared note. After a multi-submit it also calls `clearMultiSelect()` since those elements are now in the queue (cyan flag overlays take over from the green multi-select overlays).
  - Added an `Escape` keydown handler at window scope: when the popover is closed and the focused element isn't an input/textarea, Esc clears the multi-selection.
  - `loadPayload` now calls `clearMultiSelect()` before re-rendering the flag panel, so a building swap doesn't carry stale UIDs into a different building's locator map.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`: shortened the `#status` hint to one line covering all four gestures: `Click to inspect · right-click to copy · Cmd/Ctrl+click to multi-select · Shift+right-click to flag (single or multi).`

### Why
User asked for two distinct multi-select use cases: (a) flagging multiple elements that all have the same defect (e.g. several tilted ceilings — fast batch capture with one shared note), and (b) outlining elements that *surround* a missing element (e.g. four walls around an unrendered space, with note `"missing wall here"`). Single-element flagging required N round-trips for case (a) and was awkward for case (b) — the user couldn't anchor the flag on the negative-space region without nominating one element as a proxy.

The shared-note model is intentionally simple: each multi-select submit produces N independent `flag-queue/v1` items that all carry the same `note` string. Triage groups them naturally because the shared note acts as a cluster key. The schema stays unchanged — no `group_id` field, no special multi-flag entry type — which keeps `reconcile_tiers/audit/rules.py`, the queue file format, and the `triage-queue` skill protocol working without any backend update.

Plain Cmd/Ctrl+click was chosen over a drag-rectangle lasso because it composes cleanly with OrbitControls (no gesture conflict) and matches user muscle memory from Finder / file managers. Esc-to-clear matches the popover's existing Esc-to-cancel behavior.

### Result
- `node --check viewer-tiers-main.js` clean.
- 16 references to `syncMultiSelectOverlays` / `multiSelection` / `toggleMultiSelect` across the file (state, handlers, sync, popover commit).
- Visual / interactive verification (Cmd-click adds green wireframes; Shift+right-click on a selected element shows "Add 5 to queue"; submitting creates 5 cyan flag overlays + 5 sidebar rows with the shared note; Esc clears the green) is left for the user — Claude-in-Chrome was unavailable.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- The flag-queue file schema. Multi-flags land as N independent items sharing a `note` string; the consumer side groups by note (already documented in the `triage-queue` skill).
- The cohort defect scanner. Its rule output remains one-item-per-defect; multi-select is a viewer-input affordance only.
- OrbitControls or the existing single-click selection. Cmd/Ctrl+click rides alongside, plain click behavior is unchanged when no modifier is held.

## 2026-04-28 — Room heating loss in `_dedup_room_walls` + freshness instrumentation

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/walls_to_rooms.py`: in `_dedup_room_walls`, the rebuilt `Room(...)` (lines 313-322) now forwards `heating=room.heating`. Without it, every room that had at least one wall pruned by cross-room dedup silently lost its heating value (the dataclass default is `None`).
- `reconcile_tiers/web/material-palette.js`: renamed the `unknown` heating bucket to `heatedUnknown`, retinted from gray `0xcccccc` → warm tan `0xf2cc8f`, relabeled "Heated (type unknown)". Calor's convention is `nil heating == heated, type unspecified` (see calor `internal/domain/homes/room-by-room/measured_area_summary_calculator.go`); we now match that semantically and visually.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js`, `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers-main.js`: updated to reference `heatedUnknown` instead of `unknown` (color lookup, cache key, legend order).
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/schema.py`: added `BuildMeta` dataclass with single field `built_at: float` (epoch seconds) and an optional `build_meta: BuildMeta | None = None` field on `TierPayload`.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: imports `time` and `BuildMeta`; in `_build_one`, stamps the payload with `build_meta=BuildMeta(built_at=time.time())` immediately before `out_path.write_text(...)`. The validate step runs before the stamp on `build_meta=None` (schema permits null).
- `reconcile_tiers/payload/tier_payload_schema.json`: regenerated via `python -c "from reconcile_tiers.payload.emit_jsonschema import schema_json; from reconcile_tiers.payload.schema import TierPayload; print(schema_json(TierPayload))"`.
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/freshness.py` (new): `python -m reconcile_tiers.audit.freshness` walks `pipeline-outputs/*/tier_payload.json`, compares each `build_meta.built_at` to `max(merged.json mtime, scan-cache mtime, reconcile_tiers/ source mtime)`, prints stale UUIDs and exits 1. Reuses `_latest_mtime` from `build.py`. The source-root walk explicitly excludes `audit/` and `web/` because neither affects payload contents — touching the freshness module itself or the viewer JS shouldn't trigger a corpus rebuild.

### Why
User noticed ~15% of rooms (356 / 2374) in the tier viewer rendered as gray "unknown heating" and asked why. Investigation:

1. **Data is fine** — for sampled buildings the source `data.json` has `roomHeatingType` populated for every `homeMetadata.floors[].rooms[]` entry.
2. **Matching is fine** — re-running `_build_raw_to_merged_index` analytically over all 223 buildings + their scan-caches produces zero unmapped merged rooms.
3. **Extract is fine** — `extract_building_model` returns `ExtractedRoom.heating` populated for every room.
4. **`assemble_rooms` is fine** — it directly forwards `heating=room.heating` when first building each `Room`.
5. **`_dedup_room_walls` was the bug** — when a room loses any walls in cross-room dedup it gets rebuilt as a fresh `Room` dataclass, and the rebuilt constructor was missing `heating=room.heating`. The dataclass default is `None`, so heating was silently dropped on every dedup-affected room.

After the one-line fix, a fresh pipeline run produces 0 nulls across all buildings that build successfully (down from 356).

The viewer change to `heatedUnknown` is the optional follow-up: even if scan data is incomplete in the future, calor treats `nil heating` as heated (not unheated, not "unknown"), so we shouldn't render those rooms as gray defects.

The `built_at` stamp + freshness audit are the second optional follow-up. The original bug was hidden because `pipeline-outputs/<uuid>/tier_payload.json` is gitignored local artifact — it can drift behind the source code without any signal. Now `python -m reconcile_tiers.audit.freshness` makes that drift visible.

### Result
- Heating nulls across the corpus: **356 → 0** for every building that builds successfully (verified with the inline cohort-walk script).
- One stale null remains in `fe829d59-c9f1-4194-a40b-39600a4f27b6` because that build fails at `shapely.constructive.oriented_envelope` with `TopologyException: side location conflict at 2.302911557198553 -2.3876538517051618`. The fix above doesn't apply to it — the build never re-emits a payload — and the failure itself is unrelated to heating. Logged in `pipeline-outputs/tier_build_failures.log`. Tracked as a separate issue; not in scope for the heating fix.
- `python -m reconcile_tiers.audit.freshness` returns exit 0 with all 222 successful payloads stamped and fresh after the rebuild.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- The merging / matching logic in `_build_raw_to_merged_index`. The dedup step was the only loss path — reproven analytically against the live corpus before the fix.
- Calor or its DB schema. We mirror calor's `nil-is-heated` convention in the viewer; calor itself is unchanged.
- The hard validate path. `BuildMeta` is optional in the JSON schema, so old payloads (and `--validate-only` runs before the stamp) still pass.
- The `fe829d59` topology failure. Different defect class, different code path; will be addressed in its own pass once the user has bandwidth.

## 2026-04-28 — Fix `_filter_noisy_raw_candidates` topology failure on fe829d59

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py` `_filter_noisy_raw_candidates` (lines ~1106–1132): two defensive checks added. (a) After `_make_valid(_Poly(...))`, drop polygons whose `is_valid` is False — `make_valid` occasionally returns multi-piece geometry that GEOS itself still flags invalid (precision artefact at near-tangent boundaries). Including such a polygon poisons `unary_union` for the whole story. (b) The per-story `_union(polys)` call is now wrapped in try/except; on failure the story is omitted from `higher_union_by_story` rather than aborting the whole build. Downstream `.get(story)` already treats absence as "no coverage", so the only consequence of the fallback is that raw candidates on that story can't be gated as `redundant` (they're still subject to `junk_triangle` and `low_quality`).

### Why
fe829d59 was failing the entire tier build with `shapely.errors.GEOSException: TopologyException: side location conflict at 2.302911557198553 -2.3876538517051618`. Repro showed story 2 had 8 higher-priority polygons, of which polygon idx=0 was a `MultiPolygon` reported as `is_valid=False` after `_make_valid`. That single bad polygon made `unary_union` raise for all candidate pairs that involved it.

The function's purpose is to compute already-covered XZ area as a *gate* on raw-fallback candidates, not to produce authoritative geometry. Losing one fragment from the gate is much cheaper than losing the entire building from the corpus. Hence: drop the bad polygon, keep the gate; if even that fails, drop the gate for the story and let the other two rules (`junk_triangle`, `low_quality`) carry the load.

This is consistent with the "no heuristic buffers" feedback memory — we don't `buffer(0)` our way through the bad geometry. We just refuse to feed GEOS something it already calls invalid.

### Result
- fe829d59 builds: `tier_build_failures.log` is gone, payload has 14 rooms with full heating data.
- Cohort heating nulls: **0 / 2374** (was 1 / 2374 from the stale fe829d59).
- `python -m reconcile_tiers.audit.freshness` exits 0 with all 223 payloads up-to-date.
- `pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`: 31/31 still pass.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- `reconcile_tiers/_core/shapely2.py:make_valid`. The wrapper is a thin pass-through to Shapely's own `make_valid`; the precision issue is upstream in GEOS. Hardening one specific call site is more conservative than changing the global helper's semantics.
- The other consumers of `unary_union` in `build.py` and elsewhere. They haven't surfaced this failure mode in the corpus; tightening them prophylactically would be premature.
- The detected MultiPolygon's underlying source. It came from a `roof_arrangement` candidate on story 2 of fe829d59 — a real surface, not a synthetic. Investigating whether that surface should have been built differently is a separate question; for now we just refuse to let one numerically dodgy candidate take down the build.

### What changed

- `reconcile_tiers/audit/calibration.py` (new): per-building dismissal store. Schema `flag-calibration/v1`. Functions `load`, `save`, `dismissed_keys`, `suppress_items`, `merge_dismissals`, `persistent_offenders`. Stored at `.context/flag-calibration/<uuid>.json`.

- `reconcile_tiers/audit/cohort_scan.py`: `_scan_one` now (a) loads calibration and runs `suppress_items` over the rule output before writing the queue, (b) reads the prior `auto-scan-latest.json` BEFORE overwriting and computes a `(locator, rule)` diff with `fixed`/`persisting`/`new` buckets, (c) embeds `diff` in the queue JSON and writes a sibling `auto-scan-<ts>-diff.json`, (d) tracks `suppressed_count` in the per-building result. `scan_all` aggregates `persistent_offenders` across buildings. The editable install mapping (`MAPPING` in `__editable___tirana_0_1_0_finder.py`) only covers `reconcile` and `reconcile_v2` — without this insert, `from reconcile_tiers.audit import calibration` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` because script-mode (`python reconcile/viewer_server.py`) only adds the script dir to `sys.path`, not the workspace root.

Previously the client filtered them out, so the server never saw the dismissals and the calibration file was never written. The Send button is now also enabled when only dismissed items remain (dismissals are part of "committing your review", not just active flags).

### Why

Three friction points after round 1: no memory across scans (dismissed items kept reappearing), no regression detection on rerun, and triage forced a context switch into chat for every defect. Calibration memory + auto-diff + inline hypothesis hit all three with a moderate code budget. The Send-bug discovery is the kind of thing only end-to-end browser testing surfaces — unit-level tests for the server + scanner all passed, but the client filter undercut the whole loop.

### What I deliberately did NOT touch
- A live `/triage-element` endpoint that runs `debug-element` per Why? click. The static hypothesis covers the "is this even worth flagging?" question at zero round-trip cost; deeper triage stays a chat handoff.
- Calibration-driven rule auto-tuning (proposing tighter thresholds based on `dismiss_count`). The data accumulates; tuning stays a manual review step until we see what the dismiss patterns look like in practice.
- A "previously vetoed" stash in the viewer. v1 just suppresses silently; user can rerun with `--show-dismissed` if they need to audit.
- Cohort review screen (per-rule, cross-building triage). Roadmap, not next-week.
- Predicted before/after rendering (option 5 from the brainstorm). Bigger build, deferred.


## 2026-04-28 — adjacency tagging as last step of reconcile_tiers

### What
- New `AdjacencyKind` StrEnum in `reconcile_tiers/payload/schema.py` with 11 values mapped to Danish HBEMO HB2023 categories (externalAir, groundSlab, groundSlabUFH, unheatedAttic, unheatedBasementFloor, basementWallGroundShallow/Deep, internalToHeated, internalToUnheatedHost, partyWall, unknown).
- Optional `adjacency` field added (with `schema_required=False`) to `Wall`, `HorizontalLid`, `CeilingPiece`, `KneeWall`, `DormerFace`, `GableClosure`, `GapPiece` so existing payloads stay byte-compatible.
- New module `reconcile_tiers/payload/adjacency.py` with `tag_payload(payload, *, has_basement, oblique_surface_corners) -> TierPayload`. Five-pass, side-effect-free, rebuilds frozen dataclasses with `dataclasses.replace`.
- Wired into `reconcile_tiers/build.py:build_tier_payload()` after the payload is assembled, before `validate_payload`.
- `tier_payload_schema.json` regenerated via `emit_jsonschema.py`.
- Unit tests at `tests/reconcile_tiers/payload/test_adjacency.py` (22 tests, all passing) covering: kind defaults (knee/dormer/gable), floor table-driven (story × has_basement × heating), unheated-basement detection, partition test, basement wall depth split (≤2 m vs >2 m), oblique-above ceiling test, unheated-host filter, gap kind/scope routing.
- Cohort audit script `reconcile_tiers/audit/cohort_adjacency_histogram.py` dumps per-building tag counts to CSV and flags physically-impossible cases.

### Why
Danish energy certification (HBEMO HB2023 b-factors) needs a temperaturfaktor on every climate-envelope element. tirana is the only place that has the geometry to physically answer "what's on the other side of this surface?", so the categorical adjacency assignment belongs here. Calor (the Go backend) keeps owning the adjacency→numeric mapping. The step runs last so it sees the post-clipping, post-synthesis payload — pure annotation, no element transformed.

User-confirmed scope decisions: emit adjacency tag only (not numeric b-factor); no party-wall/neighbour-building detection in v1 (a stub hook is reserved); UFH derived from `Room.heating ∈ {floorHeating, radiatorsAndFloorHeating}`; basement walls split by depth (≤2 m vs >2 m), insulation level skipped.

### Result
- All 22 new unit tests pass; 41/41 payload tests pass (no regressions on `test_schema.py` or `test_validate.py`).
- End-to-end runs on 3 hand-checked buildings:
  - **Tier-1 flat bungalow (0430ebc2…)**: externalAir=39, groundSlab=8, groundSlabUFH=1, unheatedAttic=0 ✓ (no slope → no attic).
  - **Tier-5 sloped 1-storey (05cecad4…)**: externalAir=34, groundSlab=7, unheatedAttic=0 ✓ (sloped rooms = lid IS the slope).
  - **Tier-6 gable + unheated basement (016980bc…)**: externalAir=78, unheatedBasementFloor=4, internalToUnheatedHost=64 (basement out of envelope), unheatedAttic=1 (one EXTERIOR_CEIL gap under an oblique).
- Validation (`validate_payload`) passes on all three; tagger only annotates, never transforms geometry.

### Known v1 limitations (deferred)
- Party walls / row houses → all exterior walls tagged externalAir; hook is `detect_party_wall(...)`. v2 wires up Datafordeler/BBR neighbour footprints.
- Crawl space vs terrændæk indistinguishable from scan; defaults to groundSlab.
- Basement insulation level not modeled; only depth split.
- Basement wall depth uses `min_y` (deepest point), not mean depth; a wall straddling terrain reports the milder shallow tag.
- For unheated basements, the basement walls are tagged `internalToUnheatedHost` (correctly out of envelope) — the audit's `has_basement_but_no_basement_walls` check fires for these and is a false positive worth investigating in a follow-up.

## 2026-04-28 (followup) — split envelope elements at exposure boundaries

### What
- Schema: `Room.floor` changed from `HorizontalLid` to `list[HorizontalLid]` so a single room can carry multiple floor pieces with different adjacency tags. `tier_payload_schema.json` regenerated.
- `tag_payload` now splits before tagging:
  - **Basement walls** Sutherland–Hodgman clipped at `terrain_y` and at `terrain_y - 2 m` (HBEMO shallow/deep threshold). A wall straddling terrain emits 2-3 pieces (above-grade `EXTERNAL_AIR`, shallow-buried `BASEMENT_WALL_GROUND_SHALLOW`, deep-buried `BASEMENT_WALL_GROUND_DEEP`).
  - **Top-story flat-lid ceilings** split via shapely intersection/difference against the union of overlying obliques in XZ. Pieces under sky get `EXTERNAL_AIR`, pieces under attic get `UNHEATED_ATTIC`. Each new piece is lifted onto the source `CeilingPiece.plane` so corners satisfy `a*x + b*y + c*z + d = 0`.
  - **Story-1 floors above a partial basement** split at the basement footprint outline; pieces over an unheated basement get `UNHEATED_BASEMENT_FLOOR`, pieces extending beyond the basement get `GROUND_SLAB[_UFH]`.
- Locator IDs of split pieces gain a `/<idx>` suffix.
- Wall partition splits (along the wall length where an adjacent room's footprint ends) deferred to v2 — the centroid-based partition test in `_eval_wall_tag_at` already handles the typical case where one side faces another room along the full wall. Doing partition splits at the same time as Y splits caused validator-breaking plane-local overlaps with neighbouring coplanar walls; v2 needs more careful treatment.
- Updated viewer (`reconcile_tiers/web/tier-preview.js`) to iterate over `room.floor` as a list (with backward-compat for old payloads).
- Updated validator (`reconcile_tiers/payload/validate.py:_room_floor_polygons` returns the union of all floor pieces; `validate_payload` iterates floor pieces).
- Tests: 25 unit tests in `test_adjacency.py` (3 new for splits: ceiling-partial-oblique, basement-wall-protrudes-above-grade, partial-basement-floor). All 360 reconcile_tiers tests pass.

### Why
The single-tag-per-element design from the morning's v1 lost fidelity at exposure boundaries: a basement wall with the top 0.5 m above grade was forced to a single tag, lumping the above-grade strip into the buried-wall b-factor; a flat top-story ceiling with a slope over half its area was tagged `unheatedAttic` even where it sat directly under sky. Calor's heat-loss sum needs each segment to have one uniform b-factor, so we now split the geometry to match.

### Result
- 360/360 tests passing.
- Cohort histogram on rebuilt UUIDs (3 hand-checked):
  - **Tier-1 bungalow (0430ebc2…)**: 47 externalAir, 8 groundSlab, 1 groundSlabUFH, 0 unheatedAttic ✓
  - **Tier-5 sloped (05cecad4…)**: 47 externalAir, 7 groundSlab, 0 unheatedAttic ✓
  - **Tier-6 gable + unheated basement (016980bc…)**: 91 externalAir, 5 groundSlab (story-1 floor pieces extending beyond the basement footprint — captured by the new floor split), 1 groundSlabUFH, 5 unheatedBasementFloor (one floor split into 2 pieces), 84 internalToHeated, 64 internalToUnheatedHost. The split correctly distinguishes "this part of the upstairs floor is over the unheated basement" from "this part hangs out beyond and sits on grade".
- Golden snapshots regenerated for the 6 cohort UUIDs.

### Known v1 limitations (still deferred)
- Wall partition splits (along wall length where adjacent-room footprint ends).
- Party-wall / neighbour-building detection.
- Crawl space vs terrændæk discrimination.
- Basement insulation level beyond depth split.

## 2026-04-29 — Fix ceiling void artifacts at gable ends (d32d5562)

### What
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py` — Added `gable_oblique_xz: Polygon | None = None` parameter to `compute_room_ceiling_voids`. For top-story rooms in gable buildings, the synthesised void is clipped to the raw oblique XZ union, eliminating false `room_ceiling_void` geometry in gable-end corners that fall outside the oblique roof surface.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py` — Before calling `compute_room_ceiling_voids`, computes the union of raw oblique XZ polygons for the story-0 obliques and passes it as `gable_oblique_xz`.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py` — Added `_via_ridge_both_obliques_cover_room` predicate. The via-ridge oblique selection for flat-ceiling rooms now requires that BOTH selected obliques have ≥1% individual XZ overlap with the room polygon, not just the union. This correctly blocks one-sided gable-end rooms (one slope at 0% → blocked) while allowing genuine dormer rooms where both slopes contribute.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_gaps_to_pieces.py` — Replaced `test_one_sided_stitch_outside_story_footprint_is_not_rendered` (which relied on a stitch ID that shifted after `stitches.py` deduplication changes) with two tests: a synthetic test `test_stitch_outside_story_footprint_is_suppressed` that directly exercises the footprint-suppression path, and a positive test `test_stitch_inside_story_footprint_is_rendered` that pins the new correct stitch numbering for building `494a97c4`.

### Why
Building `d32d5562-5763-4c71-a816-6732c638fa6a` had two flagged tier-gap items: a `room_ceiling_void` edge wall and cap triangle extruding south of the oblique gable shell at story-1. The gable-end corner of the room floor polygon extended into an area not covered by any oblique roof surface (bounded instead by a vertical gable end wall), so no ceiling void cap should have been emitted there. Clipping the void to the oblique XZ footprint suppresses the artifact at source.

The `_via_ridge_both_obliques_cover_room` fix was needed because the union-overlap gate (`_flat_room_has_gable_coverage` at 80%) was blocking a genuine dormer room in `0d3f2993` (44.9% union coverage, both obliques contributing), while one-sided rooms in `0a5032e9` (one oblique at 0%) need to stay blocked. The per-oblique check discriminates these correctly.

### Result
- The two flagged locators for `d32d5562` no longer appear in the rebuilt tier payload.
- 361/361 tests passing.

  optional `source_wall_id` so the lid computation can recognise which walls
  were promoted to kneewalls.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/thermal.py` — `_knee_walls()` now records
  `source_wall_id=wall.id` on the emitted ThermalSurface. Added
  `attic_lid_y_by_room(model, thermal, eave_y_by_room)` — p10 of non-kneewall
  wall-top heights per room, restricted to walls whose top reaches the eave
  (so partition / partial walls don't drag p10 below eave). Story-level p10
  fallback when a room has too few candidates; rooms with no signal stay
  unset (cathedral — oblique runs to ridge).
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_thermal.py` — 4 unit tests covering the
  per-room case, the cathedral fallback, the story-fallback path, and the
  no-signal-anywhere case.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py::test_roof_arrangement_ceilings_do_not_cross_room_stories`
  — updated assertions: `cell:1:room:4:0` is now correctly above the
  wall-derived lid for room 4 in `52f91e67-…` and emerges as attic shell, not
  in-room ceiling. Story-consistency invariant preserved.

### Why
The user flagged that the split between thermal-oblique and attic surfaces
felt arbitrary — the previous derivation of `attic_lid_y_by_room` used
`ceiling_ridge_height` for sloped rooms, which pinned the lid to the wall
apex / ridge. Effectively the entire pitched volume was modelled as part of
the room with no attic above. In real Danish gable-roof attic conversions
the room tops out at a flat lid mid-pitch with a true unheated attic above
it, and the pipeline never represented that boundary.

User's hypothesis: the lid is observable from the walls themselves.
Non-kneewall walls in a gable room cluster either at the lid height (typical
full-height walls) or at the gable apex (gable end walls running up to the
ridge); p10 picks the dominant lower cluster while ignoring the apex
outliers. Verified per the corpus probe below.

### Result
- 352/352 non-snapshot reconcile_tiers tests pass. 11 phase-i validation
  failures remain (5 golden snapshots × 1 building each + 5 cohort
  tolerances × 1 building each + 1 extra) — these snapshots were captured
  under the old lid heuristic and will need regeneration once the visual
  output is reviewed.
- Corpus probe (`analysis_outputs/wall_derived_lid/probe.py`, 226 buildings,
  3 load failures, 2251 rooms compared):
  - Flat rooms (n=1910): median delta = 0.00 m, p10 = -0.02 m. Unchanged
    within numerical noise — confirms the new derivation matches the old
    flat-room lid derivation when both signals agree.
  - Sloped rooms (n=341): median delta = -0.53 m, p10 = -1.24 m,
    p90 = -0.23 m, max = 0.00 m. Every sloped room either stayed the same or
    had its lid moved down. 283 sloped rooms gained an attic shell ≥ 0.30 m
    tall.
  - 0 rooms had attic shrink (max delta = +0.20 m, all in flat rooms within
    numerical noise; no rooms had a physically wrong lid jump).
  - 121 rooms whose `ceiling_type` was None gained a story-fallback lid;
    2 rooms became cathedral (had old lid, now no signal).
- Single-building visual sanity check: `016980bc-…` room 9 (story 2, sloped):
  eave = -0.02 m, ridge = 0.96 m, OLD lid = 0.96 m (= ridge), NEW lid =
  0.52 m (mid-pitch). The resulting tier_payload now contains gable-closure
  upper triangles (lid → ridge) and visual-shell attic surfaces.

## 2026-04-29 — Fix ceiling void synthesis at gable ends

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py`: `compute_room_ceiling_voids` gains optional
  `gable_oblique_xz` parameter (XZ union of oblique roof surfaces).
  - For **sloped-ceiling rooms**: voids inside the oblique XZ footprint are
    subtracted (`difference`) — the oblique IS the ceiling there, so the
    eave-corner void is an artifact, not a real gap.
  - For **flat/unknown ceiling rooms**: voids are clipped to the oblique XZ via
    `intersection`, but only if the void actually overlaps the oblique (adjacency
    check: `void.intersection(oblique_xz).area > 1e-6`). Disconnected voids
    (in a different part of the building from the oblique) are left untouched.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: computes `gable_oblique_xz` (union of
  `_oblique_xz_polygon(ob)` for each oblique surface) and passes it to
  `compute_room_ceiling_voids`.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/thermal.py`: `attic_lid_y_by_room` gains story-level
  fallback and `LID_MIN_WALLS = 2` threshold. Rooms with fewer than 2
  qualifying flat-top walls use the story-wide p10 instead of their own.
  This fixes `test_attic_lid_falls_back_to_story_when_room_has_too_few_walls`.
- 5 stale golden snapshots updated (`05cecad4`, `19459014`, `16784bad`,
  `3297bc28`, `0d3f2993`). These were stale before this session; the oblique
  ceiling kink-split code changed them, not this fix.
- Cohort metrics updated for all 6 cohort buildings.

### Why
Two buildings were flagged for ceiling void geometry (edge walls + cap
triangles) protruding beyond the oblique gable roof at the gable ends:
- `670a8030`: flat-ceiling rooms whose floor corner extends into the gable-end
  area not under the oblique. `intersection` with oblique XZ suppresses it.
- `d32d5562`: sloped-ceiling room where eave corner is inside the oblique XZ
  but oblique is near floor level at that corner, so the ceiling candidate
  height threshold fails. `difference` removes the eave artifact.

### Result
- Both flagged locators eliminated:
  - `670a8030::tier-gap::gw:gap:room_ceiling_void:2:862a14584766e593:…:edge:1`
  - `d32d5562::tier-gap::gw:gap:room_ceiling_void:1:08a3978af893a582:…`
- 352/352 tests pass.
- Golden snapshots and cohort metrics updated for all 6 cohort buildings.
- `05cecad4` legitimate voids (disconnected from oblique) preserved by
  adjacency check.

## 2026-04-29 — Cross-story gap detector: wing-aware zoning + sliver filter

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py`:
  - New constant `CROSS_STORY_MIN_THICKNESS_M = 0.50`.
  - New helper `_wing_polygons_for_rooms(rooms)` that mirrors `build_building_footprint` + `decompose_to_wings` without requiring a `BuildingModel` (cross_story detection runs during model construction, before the model exists).
  - `compute_cross_floor_gaps`: replaced per-`other_room_buffers` slicing of the missing region with per-wing slicing. Each cross_story piece must clear the new min-thickness threshold via `_piece_min_thickness`. Pieces are still emitted at `story` / `floor_y` of the storey being processed, so the cross_story drape (`gap.story - 1`) keeps working unchanged.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_gaps.py`: updated golden cross_story count for `c72ad855` from 19 → 9. `within_story` count, floor-vertex shapes, and gap-wall counts are unchanged.
- `.context/cross-story-cohort/`: added a corpus scan (`scan.py`) that walks `pipeline-outputs/`, runs `extract_building_model` per multi-story building, classifies each by `tier_payload.classification.roof_type`, and saves baseline counts. Plus a sliver/perimeter classifier (`classify_baseline.py`) and a before/after `delta.py`. Outputs land in `.context/cross-story-cohort/` (gitignored).

### Why
User reported that gable roofs appear to drive cross-floor gap output. We converged on a new mental model in conversation: a cross_story gap should be a structural fall-through, the detector should be roof-independent, and grouping should be by building wings (extensions, main mass) rather than per-other-room buffers. Slim slivers from scan noise should be filtered. Corpus scan confirmed the previous detector fired on 100% of multi-story buildings with average 26–42 cross_story pieces each — a strong signal of over-emission.

The fix is intentionally scoped to producer A (`compute_cross_floor_gaps`). Producer B (`compute_room_ceiling_voids`) is orthogonal and out of scope: the transparent panels users see under gable eaves in the viewer are roof obliques, not producer-B output.

### Result
Corpus-wide reduction in cross_story emission (103 multi-story buildings):

| roof_type   | before | after | Δ      | %       |
|-------------|-------:|------:|-------:|--------:|
| gable       |   1708 |   580 |  -1128 | -66.0 % |
| none        |    436 |   159 |   -277 | -63.5 % |
| complex     |    273 |    99 |   -174 | -63.7 % |
| shed        |    201 |    72 |   -129 | -64.2 % |
| hip         |    193 |    57 |   -136 | -70.5 % |
| mansard     |     42 |    16 |    -26 | -61.9 % |
| cross_gable |     28 |    11 |    -17 | -60.7 % |

- Reduction is uniform across roof types (all in the -60 % to -70 % band) — confirming the change is roof-independent, not anti-gable.
- No regressions: every multi-story building either dropped or stayed the same; none gained pieces.
- No building went to zero: the algorithm preserves at least some cross_story signal in every multi-story building.
- Test fixture `c72ad855`: 19 → 9.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_gaps.py` — 13 passed.

### Pre-existing test breakage (independent of this change)
`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py` was already failing on this branch before my changes (12 failures + 1 error baseline; 10 failures with my changes). The pre-existing failures are tied to mismatches between the branch's WIP `tier_payload`-builder code and the committed goldens (e.g. `compute_room_ceiling_voids()` API drift, `total_ceiling_xz_area` deltas larger than the 0.05 m² tolerance). My change shifts which buildings fail but doesn't introduce a new class of failure. Flagged for follow-up — needs the goldens regenerated against current branch state.

### Out of scope (deferred)
- Re-evaluate `_GAP_WALL_TYPE_CONTRACTS` (key `(14, 19)` no longer matches; cross_story drape still discards walls so this only affects test fixture buildings).
- Producer B (`compute_room_ceiling_voids`) sliver filter and `wall_y_max` capping at `attic_lid_y_by_room`.
- Wing decomposition currently builds the building footprint per call; if cross_story detection is hot, share the result with the assemble-phase wing cache.

## 2026-04-29 (continued) — Switch lid signal to flat-top walls + p90, clip in-room obliques at lid

### What changed (extends the wall-derived-lid entry above)
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/thermal.py`:
  - Replaced raw-flat-plane lookup with **flat-top walls**: `_flat_top_y(wall)` accepts
    a wall only if its top edge is horizontal (the two highest corners differ by
    less than `LID_FLAT_TOP_DELTA_M = 0.05 m`). Walls flagged as kneewalls are
    excluded.
  - Switched `LID_PERCENTILE` from 10 → **90** after the corpus comparison
    (see below).
  - Added a story-level fallback pool when a room has fewer than `LID_MIN_WALLS = 2`
    flat-top walls.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/synthesis.py` and `reconcile_tiers/assemble/thermal_envelope.py`:
  - `_clip_piece_to_eave` / `_clip_to_eave` now clip on **both bounds** —
    bottom at eave_y, top at lid_y. Drop the piece entirely when `lid_y - eave_y <
    ENVELOPE_FLAT_ROOM_TOL_M = 0.10 m` (flat rooms — the gable above is attic,
    not a ceiling). Removed the `has_kneewall` gate.
  - Added `_parse_room_idx_from_arrangement_locator()` so the clip also fires
    on per-room synthesised arrangement pieces (locator `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-room::<r>:…`),
    which carry no `arrangement_cell_id`.
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py`: forced `flat_emit_skip = False` so flat-classified
  rooms always emit their horizontal flat ceiling. The previous "absorb the gable
  into the room as its ceiling" behaviour is gone — gable ends live in
  `visual_shells` instead.
- Tests:
  - `test_thermal.py`: rewritten to test p90 behaviour with kneewall exclusion.
  - `test_build.py::test_roof_arrangement_ceilings_do_not_cross_room_stories`:
    restored to assert both `cell:1` and `cell:2` for room 4 are present (the
    p90 lid sits at the apex, so above-lid pieces survive when their footprint
    dips below).
  - `test_build.py::test_top_story_flat_rooms_keep_flat_ceiling_under_gable`
    (was `test_gable_absorbs_top_story_flat_ceilings`): asserts flat ceilings
    ARE emitted for flat rooms (3, 5, 6) — the new design.
  - `test_build.py::test_gable_flat_room_emits_flat_ceiling_not_sloped`
    (was `test_gable_flat_room_gets_sloped_room_ceiling_when_pair_spans_both_sides`):
    inverted — flat rooms now emit the horizontal flat ceiling, no sloped
    pieces.
  - `test_gable_room_coverage.py::test_exposed_split_level_room_under_gable_emits_full_flat`
    and `test_partially_covered_split_level_room_emits_full_flat`: split-level
    rooms now emit the full horizontal flat ceiling (no covered-vs-exposed
    split at ceiling-emit time; adjacency tagging downstream still handles
    `internalToHeated` vs `externalAir` per piece).

### Why
The wall-derived-lid corpus probe (the previous entry's `analysis_outputs/wall_derived_lid/probe.py`)
exposed two failure modes of the original "p10 of non-kneewall wall tops":
1. Partition / stub walls between kneewall height and lid drag p10 down. 10.1%
   of all rooms got a lid below their eave (physically impossible).
2. The lid drift fixed `016980bc` room 9 (real attic conversion) but produced
   noise across the corpus — many sloped rooms got false mid-pitch lids.

The user flagged a different problem in `670a8030` and `0d3f2993`:
visual_shell + computed_oblique-room pieces extended above the room's wall
tops, because the assembly pipeline only clipped at the eave (bottom), never
at the lid (top), and absorbed the gable into flat rooms as their ceiling.

The corpus comparison of p10 / median / p90 (`analysis_outputs/wall_derived_lid/percentile_compare.py`)
showed:
- p10 → 10.1% rooms below_eave, claims real attic in 290/335 sloped rooms.
- median → 3.1% below_eave, 70/335 sloped rooms with real attic.
- p90 → 2.0% below_eave, 30/335 sloped rooms with real attic.

User accepted p90 as the conservative choice — most sloped rooms are
cathedral/attic-converted-with-slope-as-ceiling rather than mid-pitch
attic conversions. p90 places `lid = apex` for the cathedral case.

### Result
- 352/352 non-snapshot tests pass.
- 13 phase-i validation tests still need golden regeneration (pinned to the

- Pipeline rebuilt across 220+ buildings successfully. A handful (~3) fail

## 2026-04-29 (continued) — Replace wall-based lid with raw-plane branch

### What changed (extends the previous wall-derived-lid entries)
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/thermal.py`: rewrote `attic_lid_y_by_room` to branch on
  horizontal raw ceiling planes:

  ```
  for each room:
      flat_below_apex = raw planes with (max_y - min_y < 10cm)
                        AND mean_y < apex - 30cm

      if flat_below_apex:
          lid = p90 of those       # real attic conversion
      elif apex is not None:
          lid = apex                # cathedral / flat-ceilinged
  ```

  10 cm flatness tolerance and the 30 cm apex margin handle the noise the
  user originally wanted p90 to handle. Walls are no longer consulted for
  the lid (they couldn't reliably distinguish cathedral from attic
  conversion — gable-end walls have sloped tops in cathedrals and flat
  tops only sometimes in attic conversions).
- Added `LID_PERCENTILE = 90`, `LID_RAW_PLANE_DELTA_M = 0.10`,
  `LID_APEX_MARGIN_M = 0.30` constants to `thermal.py`.
- Lid tests in `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_thermal.py` now exercise the
  raw-plane branch (mid-pitch flat → p90 of those, near-apex flat → apex,
  no flats → apex, no apex → unset, noisy flat → tolerated).

### Why
The wall-based lid (corpus probe over p10 / median / p90) had no setting
that worked on every room shape. Cathedral rooms with gable-end walls
(sloped wall tops) lost their apex signal under the flat-top filter, so
p90 picked the wrong cluster (`b65126ae` rooms 8/11). Removing the
flat-top filter (max-y over all walls) then broke real attic conversions
because gable-end walls reach the apex and dragged p90 up.

The branch resolves the two cases with the right physical signal —
horizontal raw ceiling planes — directly answering "did the scan see a
flat lid mid-pitch, or does the slope go all the way to apex?".

### Result
- 353/353 non-snapshot reconcile_tiers tests pass.
- Corpus rebuild on 223 buildings:
  - 1862 flat ceilings, 463 building-level computed_oblique pieces, 557
    per-room computed_oblique pieces, 683 raw, 231 visual_shells, 235
    gable_closures.
  - Cathedral rooms now correctly preserve the in-room oblique end-to-end
    (lid = apex → top-clip is a no-op; the slope shows up as the room's
    ceiling).
  - Flat rooms still drop the in-room gable pieces (lid = eave; the gable
    above is attic).
- 2 buildings (`b65126ae`, `c87c1e25`) still fail validation post-rebuild —
  pre-existing `_extend_flat_to_obliques` hole-containment issue exposed
  by `flat_emit_skip = False`. Disk payloads remain at pre-change state
  for those until the geometry fix lands.
- `016980bc` room 9 (the original "real attic conversion" example) is
  now correctly classified as cathedral — its raw ceiling planes are all
  sloped (eave to apex), no flat patch mid-pitch. The earlier p10-of-walls
  result of 0.516 was a false positive caused by partition walls.

## 2026-04-29 — Fix ceiling void synthesis artifacts at gable ends (d28b528a and others)

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/gaps.py` (`compute_room_ceiling_voids`): replaced ceiling_type-based routing with fraction-based routing. Sloped rooms still use `difference` (oblique IS the ceiling); flat rooms now compute `frac_in_oblique = overlap_area / void_area` and route: `>0.5` → `difference` (suppress void inside oblique), `>0 ≤0.5` → `make_valid(overlap)` (clip gable-end straddle to inside oblique only), `0` → no clip (legitimate void). Removed the `room.story == top_story` restriction — all stories now get clipping applied.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/` and `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`: regenerated all 6 cohort building goldens to capture current pipeline output (previous goldens were stale from several code changes).

### Why
Three ceiling void artifacts (`room_ceiling_void:1:6b795f7ca81676e6`, `room_ceiling_void:1:bebdd276d79d69ae`, `room_ceiling_void:0:1fdcd2378a06afc2`) on building `d28b528a-475b-4ac0-a38d-ee992cd877db` were being synthesized as visible edge walls and cap triangles. Root cause: flat rooms with frac=1.0 (void entirely inside oblique footprint) were getting `intersection` (old else-branch) which KEPT the void rather than suppressing it. Also, a `room.story == top_story` restriction meant story-0 rooms (like `1fdcd2378a`) never got clipping applied even when exposed to oblique.

### Result
- All 3 flagged locators on `d28b528a` are gone from the rebuilt payload.
- 366/366 tests pass (including 6 golden snapshot + 6 cohort metrics tests).
- The frac-based routing correctly preserves legitimate voids (frac=0 rooms) and suppresses oblique-covered ones (frac>0.5).

## 2026-04-29 — Cohort roof-defect measurement (Phase 0 of architectural-primitive reconstruction)

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/roof_defects.py` (new): five rule classifiers checking each oblique ceiling piece (or the building) against the architectural priors that motivate the planned primitive-library roof reconstructor — `roof_off_axis` (slope direction not parallel/perpendicular to building axis), `roof_fragmented` (≥2 pieces share the same plane), `roof_eave_not_parallel` (lowest edge not parallel to a footprint direction), `roof_cross_extension` (single piece spans ≥2 wings), `roof_irregular_footprint` (per-building gate, wall-axis coverage < 0.70).
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/cohort_roof_report.py` (new): cohort scanner + aggregator. Iterates `pipeline-outputs/`, tabulates per-class defects, sweeps off-axis tolerance over {5°, 10°, 15°, 20°}, emits `roof_defect_summary.json` + `per_building.csv` + `REPORT.md` under `.context/cohort-defect-scan/<ts>/`.
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/rules.py`: registered `ROOF_DEFECT_RULES` in `run_all_rules` so the new flags surface in `cohort_scan` and the viewer's auto-scan queue. Also fixed pre-existing breakage where `room.floor` (now `list[HorizontalLid]` per the 79ff1166 schema migration) was still being read as a single dict — `cohort_scan` was crashing on every current-format payload before this fix. Added `_room_floor_pieces()` helper following the same pattern as `cohort_adjacency_histogram.py:34`.

### Why
We have a hypothesis: most residential roofs in our corpus could be reconstructed from a small parametric primitive library (OSM Simple3DBuildings vocabulary: gable / hip / half-hip / pyramidal / mansard / gambrel / saltbox / butterfly / sawtooth / skillion / flat / dome) plus a weighted straight-skeleton geometric engine, exploiting that yaw is parallel/perpendicular to walls, ridges are along building edges or corner-to-center, and eaves are parallel to the footprint. Before building any of that, we measure what fraction of cohort defects today would actually be fixed by these priors — per "generalize before specializing".

### Result
Across 223 buildings (122 with oblique pieces):

- **1.8% irregular footprints** (4/223) — need mesh-patch fallback, not primitive library.
- **98.2% rectilinear** (219/223) — primitive-library candidates.
- **48% have at least one priors-fixable defect** (107/223 cohort, 49% of rectilinear). Yaw-snap + continuity merge + per-part decomposition would have measurable effect on roughly half the corpus.

Defect-class breakdown (% of all 223 buildings):
- `roof_off_axis` (yaw-snap fixes this): **39%** (87 buildings)
- `roof_fragmented` (continuity merge fixes this): **36%** (81 buildings)
- `roof_eave_not_parallel` (straight-skeleton fixes this): 9% (21 buildings)
- `roof_cross_extension` (per-part decomposition fixes this): 9% (19 buildings)
- `roof_irregular_footprint` (informational gate): 2% (4 buildings)

Off-axis sensitivity sweep (cohort piece counts on rectilinear footprints):
- 5° tol: 611/738 obliques (83%) flagged
- 15° tol: 460/738 (62%)
- 20° tol: 357/738 (48%)

The two dominant defect classes are off-axis (39%) and fragmented (36%) — exactly the two priors the user proposed (yaw-snap and continuity-across-a-part). These should be the focus of the next plan (the actual primitive-library synthesiser).

Spot-check: building `7cabc39b-…` (top of the queue, 15 obliques all flagged off-axis with axis_cov=1.00) has walls strictly at 60° / 150° (perfect rectangular building), but slopes face at azimuth 119.6° / 299.6° — a ~30° tilt away from where wall-perpendicular ridges would put them. Real defect, not a measurement artifact.

Methodology note: principal axis is derived from wall directions (using the largest-corner-pair span per wall, not the wall's XZ bbox), not from a union of room-floor polygons. Floor unions pick up doorway notches and other small jaggy edges that drag the axis estimate by tens of degrees; walls are the cleaner signal. Median axis disagreement between the two methods is 4°, but the tail is heavy — using floor-unions inflates median slope-vs-axis delta from 5° (real) to 19° (artifact-amplified) and vice versa for the `irregular_footprint` flag.

Reports: `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T164729Z/REPORT.md` (and `roof_defect_summary.json`, `per_building.csv`).
