## 2026-04-29 — Architectural-priors Phase 1: yaw-snap + continuity-merge (ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS toggle, default OFF)

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/architectural_priors.py` (new): `clean_oblique_surfaces(surfaces, model)` post-processor with two priors. **Yaw-snap**: rotate each oblique surface so its slope direction lands on the nearest building-axis-aligned direction (`{axis, axis+90°, +180°, +270°}`), preserving inclination and centroid Y. Snap fires when the delta is in `[1°, 40°]` (the cohort's empirical 90th percentile is 40°; deltas above that are likely real architectural choices). **Continuity-merge**: union-find groups surfaces by plane equivalence (same `roof_defects` tolerances), and merges co-planar groups whose XZ polygons union into a single connected `Polygon` (`MultiPolygon` → kept separate, that's coplanar coincidence not a fragment). Re-emits with area-weighted average plane, lifts corners through `Plane.y_at`. Building principal axis derived from `walls_merged` corners with the largest-corner-pair span (corrects for the bbox-aliasing bug noted in Phase 0).
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:218-222`: gated call site, `if os.environ.get("ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS") == "1"`. Default OFF — no behavior change unless toggle set.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_architectural_priors.py` (new): 9 unit tests covering snap small/large delta, inclination/centroid preservation, merge connected/disjoint, idempotence, toggle off no-op, axis-from-walls.

### Why
Phase 0 measurement showed 39% of buildings with off-axis slopes and 36% with fragmented/co-planar pieces — together ~75% of cohort priors-fixable defects. Phase 1 implements just these two priors as a post-processing pass, behind a toggle for safe A/B comparison before flipping the default.

### Result
**Mixed signal — geometric improvement is real, but the audit's eave detection penalizes a downstream side effect.**

Cohort comparison (223 buildings, 122 with obliques) — toggle OFF baseline vs toggle ON:

| Metric | OFF | ON | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off-axis pieces (5° tol) | 611 | 370 | **−39%** |
| Off-axis pieces (15° tol) | 460 | 329 | **−28%** |
| Off-axis pieces (20° tol) | 357 | 300 | −16% |
| Buildings with off-axis defect | 87 (39%) | 71 (32%) | **−18%** |
| Buildings with fragmented defect | 81 (36%) | 80 (36%) | −1% |
| Buildings with eave-not-parallel | 21 (9%) | 64 (29%) | **+205%** |
| Buildings with cross-extension | 19 (9%) | 18 (8%) | −5% |
| Buildings priors-fixable (any) | 107 (48%) | 106 (48%) | −1% |

Yaw-snap is working: piece-level off-axis drops 28-39% across tolerances, building-level off-axis drops 18%. **But `roof_eave_not_parallel` more than tripled (21 → 64 buildings)**, cancelling out the priors-fixable headline.

**Root cause of the eave-not-parallel inflation** (diagnosed via instrumented build of `7cabc39b`): the snap rotates the plane normal about the surface centroid, preserving XZ corners and centroid Y. But it changes the Y values of individual corners (since the slope direction is now different). Downstream, `_emit_wing_clipped` in `build.py:967-1011` splits each surface at `kink_y` (eave/ridge) — surfaces that didn't straddle the kink before may now straddle it, producing extra above/below pieces. The audit's `roof_eave_not_parallel` rule finds the polygon edge with smallest sum of vertex Y values; after the snap, the "lowest edge" can be a different edge in XZ space, and that new edge isn't always parallel to the building axis.

**Phase 1 success criterion (from the plan)**: drop priors-fixable rate from 48% → ≤15%. **Failed**: rate stayed at 48% due to the eave inflation. Target met for off-axis specifically (substantial reduction) but the headline number didn't move.

**Implications for Phase 2**:
- The yaw-snap prior works as intended at the source-surface level. Its effect is real and measurable in off-axis counts.
- The audit's `roof_eave_not_parallel` rule is sensitive to the snap's Y-coordinate side effect, treating it as a defect. Either (a) the audit needs to be Y-shift-tolerant (e.g., check eave direction against the *snapped* plane's down-slope-perpendicular direction, not against the actual lowest-Y edge), or (b) the snap needs to preserve Y range, not just centroid Y (this is over-determined — preserving min, max, and centroid Y simultaneously is generally infeasible for a rotated plane).
- Continuity-merge had little observable effect because (i) most co-planar pairs in the cohort were post-split cells from one source surface (which my pre-split processor doesn't touch), and (ii) snap-created co-planarity tends to be between physically separate pieces (kept separate by the connectedness gate).
- **Recommendation**: don't flip the toggle default to ON yet. Either revise the audit (Phase 1.5) or accept that Phase 1's net cohort impact is "moves defects from off-axis bin to eave-not-parallel bin". Visual A/B in the viewer would clarify whether the snapped roofs look better than baseline.

Toggle OFF preserves all prior behavior — 381 tests pass (372 baseline + 9 new) with `unset ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS`.

Reports: `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T172620Z/REPORT.md` (toggle ON cohort), `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T164729Z/REPORT.md` (toggle OFF baseline from Phase 0).

## 2026-04-29 — Phase 1.5: replace eave-not-parallel lowest-Y heuristic with plane-derived direction

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/roof_defects.py`: dropped `_lowest_edge_xz_angle_deg`, added `_expected_eave_angle_deg(plane)` which derives the eave direction from the plane normal (perpendicular to the XZ projection of the down-slope direction). `rule_roof_eave_not_parallel` now uses this plane-derived angle instead of the polygon's lowest-Y edge.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/audit/test_roof_defects.py`: added `test_eave_uses_plane_not_corner_y` (regression for the snap artifact: shuffled corner Y values on an axis-aligned plane should NOT fire the eave rule) and `test_eave_fires_when_plane_is_off_axis` (sanity check that the rule still detects real off-axis defects).

### Why
Phase 1 cohort run (toggle ON) inflated `roof_eave_not_parallel` from 21 → 64 buildings. Root cause: `_lowest_edge_xz_angle_deg` selected the polygon edge with smallest sum-of-Y, which moves to a different XZ edge after yaw-snap rotates the plane (corner Y values shift). The plane normal is rotation-invariant in concept, so deriving the eave direction directly from `(a, c)` is artifact-free. The two methods are mathematically equivalent mod 90 (eave direction = slope direction + 90 deg, both fold to the same axis check), so the rule now mirrors `roof_off_axis` exactly — its independent signal value is zero, but it remains a separate rule for taxonomy clarity.

### Result
**Apples-to-apples cohort comparison, both runs with the new plane-derived eave rule:**

| Metric | Toggle OFF | Toggle ON | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off-axis pieces (5° tol) | 598 | 370 | **−38%** |
| Off-axis pieces (15° tol) | 447 | 329 | **−26%** |
| Off-axis pieces (20° tol) | 359 | 300 | −16% |
| Buildings with off-axis defect | 85 (38%) | 71 (32%) | **−16%** |
| Buildings with eave-not-parallel | 85 (38%) | 71 (32%) | **−16%** (now mirrors off_axis) |
| Buildings with fragmented defect | 76 (34%) | 80 (36%) | +5% |
| Buildings with cross-extension | 19 (9%) | 18 (8%) | −5% |
| **Buildings priors-fixable (any)** | **104 (46.6%)** | **98 (43.9%)** | **−6% (−2.7 pts)** |

Phase 1's geometric signal is now visible without the audit artifact: yaw-snap reduces off-axis piece count by 26-38% across tolerances, and reduces affected buildings by 16%. Continuity-merge contributes much less (fragmented buildings actually drift up by 5%, because most "fragmentation" in the cohort comes from post-split room-cell fan-out — co-planar split cells that my pre-split processor doesn't see).

**Phase 1 success criterion** (drop priors-fixable rate from 48% → ≤15%): **still failed**. Real improvement is 47% → 44% (~6% relative reduction).

**Why the improvement is modest**: The snap fires correctly on source obliques (4 in, 4 out for the 7cabc39b smoke test). But `split_oblique_surfaces` then fans each source into N room-cell pieces. The audit measures per-emitted-piece, so a building with 4 source surfaces all snapped becomes ~10-15 emitted pieces all sharing axis-aligned planes. Off-axis count drops at the source level but not as dramatically at the piece level. Fragmented count actually increases because more emitted pieces share the same (now axis-aligned) plane.

**Implications for Phase 2**:
- The audit's per-piece view conflates source-surface count with split-cell count. A future improvement: dedupe pieces by plane within the audit's `_oblique_pieces` filter, so the audit measures physical surfaces. That would expose Phase 1's full effect.
- Continuity-merge needs to operate post-split (or the renderer should not emit per-cell fan-out for co-planar slopes). Current pre-split placement misses ~80% of the fragmentation cases.
- The biggest residual signal is still off-axis (32% of buildings). Phase 2 should either tighten the snap (e.g., aggressive corner rotation) or accept Phase 1's modest gain and move on to non-axis priors (eave-to-wall snapping, per-part decomposition).

Reports: `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T193809Z/REPORT.md` (toggle OFF, Phase 0+1.5), `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T193624Z/REPORT.md` (toggle ON, Phase 1+1.5).

## 2026-04-29 — Phase 1.6: audit dedupe-by-plane + post-split continuity-merge

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/roof_defects.py`:
  - Added `_oblique_physical_surfaces(payload)`: groups `_oblique_pieces` by plane equivalence and returns one representative per group (largest XZ area). Use this for rules that ask "is this physical surface defective?" — the previous approach counted emitted pieces, which inflated rates by the post-split room-cell count.
  - `rule_roof_off_axis` and `rule_roof_eave_not_parallel` now consume `_oblique_physical_surfaces` (count physical surfaces, not split cells).
  - `rule_roof_cross_extension` now unions all pieces in a plane group before checking wing overlap (recovers the pre-split surface footprint, which the largest-piece proxy would miss when the largest cell is confined to one wing).
  - `rule_roof_fragmented` continues to consume `_oblique_pieces` directly — that rule literally exists to count emission duplicates per plane, so deduplication would defeat its purpose.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/architectural_priors.py`:
  - Added `clean_split_oblique_surfaces(surfaces)` — mirror of `_continuity_merge` but for `SplitObliqueSurface` (post-split). Groups co-planar split cells, unions XZ polygons, emits a merged cell when the union is connected. Disjoint groups are left as-is.
  - Trade-off documented in the docstring: cross-room merging picks the largest cell's `arrangement_cell_id`, losing per-room adjacency granularity. Acceptable for cohort measurement; may need tuning for production heat-loss calc.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:228–233`: gated call to `clean_split_oblique_surfaces` after `split_oblique_surfaces`, same `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1` toggle.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_architectural_priors.py`: added 3 unit tests for the post-split merge (abutting → merged, disjoint → kept separate, disabled → identity).

### Why
Phase 1 + 1.5 yielded only a 3-percentage-point drop in priors-fixable rate (47% → 44%), even though piece-level off-axis count fell 26%. The gap was the audit measuring per emitted piece while Phase 1 operates on source surfaces. (1) realigns the audit's per-building view with physical-surface counts. (2) shrinks the actual emission so per-piece counts don't inflate either.

### Result
**With all changes (Phase 1 + 1.5 + 1.6), apples-to-apples cohort comparison using the deduped audit:**

| Metric | Toggle OFF | Toggle ON | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total oblique pieces | 780 | 895 | +15% (raw fan-out, see below) |
| Off-axis pieces (5° tol) | 598 | 482 | **−19%** |
| Off-axis pieces (15° tol) | 447 | 426 | −5% |
| Off-axis pieces (20° tol) | 359 | 384 | +7% |
| **Buildings with off-axis defect (deduped)** | **84 (38%)** | **75 (34%)** | **−11%** |
| Buildings with eave-not-parallel | 84 (38%) | 75 (34%) | −11% (mirrors off-axis) |
| Buildings with fragmented defect | 76 (34%) | 80 (36%) | +5% |
| Buildings with cross-extension | 33 (15%) | 29 (13%) | −12% |
| **Buildings priors-fixable (any)** | **104 (47%)** | **98 (44%)** | **−6 buildings, −2.7 pts** |

**Phase 1 success criterion still not met** (target 48% → ≤15%; actual 47% → 44%). Modest improvement persists, not the dramatic one we hoped for.

**Why (1)+(2) didn't unlock more improvement** — diagnosed on `7cabc39b`:
- The audit's per-building view now correctly counts physical surfaces (4 in the OFF state). With toggle ON, it counts 8 physical surfaces — *more* than OFF. Why?
- Toggle ON corpus has more raw-emitted pieces. Locator-kind breakdown for `7cabc39b` post-rebuild: 5 flat + 5 computed-oblique + **10 raw**. The raw pieces come from `room.raw_ceiling_planes` directly via `build.py:927` (`CeilingSource.RAW_FALLBACK`), bypassing `roof.oblique` and therefore my Phase 1 snap.
- `build_raw_oblique_surfaces` does add raw obliques to `roof.oblique` (`obliques.py:107–145`), and those DO get snapped by my pass. But the `tier-ceiling-raw::N:M` emission path is separate — it reads `room.raw_ceiling_planes` and emits them with the original (un-snapped) plane.
- So the residual off-axis is dominated by the raw-emission path. To close the gap, the snap would need to also rewrite `room.raw_ceiling_planes` (or have the raw-emission path use `roof.oblique`'s snapped planes when they cover the same scan footprint).

**The toggle-ON pieces total went UP** (780 → 895). The (2) post-split merge did reduce piece count for snapped surfaces (`7cabc39b` went 22 → 15 between Phase 1 alone and Phase 1+(2)). But the kink-Y straddle artifact from the snap creates additional below/above splits in `_emit_wing_clipped` that (2) can't merge across (different planes after the kink-Y split). Net: more pieces, but the audit's deduped view normalizes this.

**Implications**:
- The architectural-priors plan as scoped (snap roof.oblique only) hits a ceiling at ~3 pp reduction in priors-fixable rate. The remaining defect signal lives in the raw-fallback emission path.
- A genuine Phase 2 would need to either (a) snap raw planes at emission time, (b) prefer snapped `roof.oblique`-derived geometry over raw when they overlap, or (c) rebuild the raw-fallback path to consume snapped planes.
- The audit measurements are now cleaner and won't mislead future plans. `_oblique_physical_surfaces` is the right primitive for "is this building's roof physically defective?".

Reports: `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T195144Z/REPORT.md` (toggle OFF, Phase 1.6 audit), `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T195316Z/REPORT.md` (toggle ON, Phase 1+1.5+1.6).

## 2026-04-29 — Phase 1.7: fix compass-vs-math convention bug (the audit was lying)

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/audit/roof_defects.py`: introduced `_axis_misalignment_deg(slope_az_compass, wall_axis_math)` that correctly compares angles in different conventions. Updated `rule_roof_off_axis` and `rule_roof_eave_not_parallel` to use it.
- `reconcile_tiers/roof/architectural_priors.py`: `_nearest_axis_aligned_az` now uses snap-target candidates `{-axis + k*90}` instead of `{axis + k*90}`. The earlier formula picked targets in the wrong convention.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/audit/test_roof_defects.py`: added `test_off_axis_does_not_fire_on_aligned_slope_with_rotated_walls` — a regression test with non-zero axis. Existing tests all used axis=0° (where math and compass coincide), so they passed despite the bug.

### Why
Visual review of `7cabc39b` and `0b75d30e` revealed both looked broken with toggle ON: roof slopes tilted in chaotic non-perpendicular directions even though the OFF state showed clean cross-gables with slopes correctly aligned to walls. The user's instinct ("transforms of the segment") nailed it. Investigation traced to a coordinate-convention bug:

- `slope_az` from `atan2(-a, -c)` is in **compass convention** (0° = +Z, 90° = +X)
- `wall_axis` from `atan2(dz, dx)` is in **math convention** (0° = +X, 90° = +Z)

These are reflections (`compass = 90 - math`), so `slope_az mod 90` and `wall_axis mod 90` are **complementary** for axis-aligned roofs. For 7cabc39b: walls at math 60°, slopes at compass 119.6°. Sum mod 90 = 0 → **perfectly aligned**. The buggy comparison reported 30° misalignment, and the snap rotated correctly-aligned slopes by 30° to "fix" non-defects — producing the visible breakage.

### Result
**The audit's earlier off-axis numbers were inflated by the bug.** Apples-to-apples cohort comparison with the convention fix in place, both runs:

| Metric | Toggle OFF | Toggle ON | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off-axis pieces (5° tol) | 604 | 584 | −3% |
| Off-axis pieces (15° tol) | 453 | 463 | +2% |
| Buildings with off-axis defect | 32 (14.3%) | 34 (15.2%) | +6% (slightly worse) |
| Buildings with fragmented | 76 (34.1%) | 75 (33.6%) | −1% |
| Buildings with eave-not-parallel | 32 (14.3%) | 34 (15.2%) | mirrors off-axis |
| Buildings with cross-extension | 33 (14.8%) | 26 (11.7%) | **−21%** |
| **Priors-fixable (any)** | **81 (36.3%)** | **80 (35.9%)** | **−1 building** |

**The real cohort baseline is ~36% priors-fixable, not 48%.** The convention bug had been inflating off-axis counts by 25+ percentage points — most buildings were *already* axis-aligned and we'd been mis-counting them as defective. Phase 0 results (39% off-axis, 48% priors-fixable) were artifacts of the broken comparison.

**Phase 1's actual effect, with corrected measurement**: essentially zero on priors-fixable rate. The architectural-priors hypothesis (yaw-snap + continuity-merge fixes 75% of cohort defects) was solving a phantom problem. With the audit honest, there's nothing for yaw-snap to do — slopes are already in the right direction. Continuity-merge across rooms (Phase 1.6) does deliver a real ~21% reduction in cross-extension flags, which is the only measurable Phase 1 contribution.

**Visual confirmation**: 7cabc39b and 0b75d30e both render cleanly with toggle ON now. The classification correctly returns to "cross_gable" for 7cabc39b. Identical to OFF for axis-aligned slopes; modest geometric differences only where snap genuinely had something to do.

### Implications and recommendation
- **The convention fix is mandatory** — it makes the audit honest. ~50 buildings that were previously flagged as off-axis are NOT actually off-axis.
- **Phase 1 yaw-snap is not worth shipping** as a default. Net effect is ~zero on the priors-fixable rate, slightly negative on off-axis counts. Keep behind toggle for experimentation.
- **Post-split continuity-merge (Phase 1.6) is the only piece worth keeping** — modest cross-extension improvement.
- The 14% true off-axis rate is small. The dominant cohort defects are now `fragmented` (34%, mostly emission-redundancy) and `cross-extension` (12–15%, building-decomposition issue). Both are pipeline-architecture problems, not architectural-priors problems.
- **The architectural-priors arc is finished** — the hypothesis tested negative once the measurement was fixed.

Reports: `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T202033Z/REPORT.md` (toggle OFF, fixed convention), `.context/cohort-defect-scan/20260429T201855Z/REPORT.md` (toggle ON, Phase 1 + fixed convention). 387 tests pass with toggle OFF.

## 2026-04-30 — Close gaps where a wide door + parallel wall straddle a stitch

**Files changed**:
- `reconcile_tiers/extract/exterior.py` — `_find_parallel_wall` gains a `projection_coverage ≥ 0.5` gate; `dist_along` upper bound bumped from 1.0 m → 1.30 m. New `_projection_coverage()` helper. Diagnostic log (`EXTERIOR_DEBUG=1` env flag) records every accepted match and every rejection with the failing gate + value.
- `reconcile_tiers/assemble/gaps_to_pieces.py` — new `_stitches_covered_by_side_closures()` filter: stitches whose XZ endpoints coincide (within 0.20 m) with an exterior side-closure's bottom edge are dropped via the existing `dropped_stitch_indices` mechanism (atomic L-stitch-group drop preserved).
- `reconcile_tiers/build.py` — `_build_one` writes `exterior_debug.json` per uuid when `EXTERIOR_DEBUG=1`.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_exterior.py` — fixture cohort updated (f40dcc9f, 2ea3b759 gain new indicators); two new regression tests for the d98923f0 stitch:0:36 case and a projection-coverage rejection.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/assemble/test_gaps_to_pieces.py` — cohort piece counts updated for f40dcc9f, 2ea3b759.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json` — six golden snapshots regenerated (largely pre-existing branch drift from prior commits, plus the small exterior-closure deltas from this change).

**Why**: User reported that on building `d98923f0-3373-4d3c-ba03-c0df5d8b29d8`, tier-gap `stitch:0:36` should be closed because a wide door (`B0E1BD5D…`, 2.94 m) sits parallel to a wall (`9D54…`, 2.91 m) on the other side, ~1.10 m away. The detector in `detect_exterior_gap_indicators` was rejecting the pair on its `dist_along ≤ 1.0 m` gate (actual value 1.0985 — a 0.10 m miss), so no `gap_closure` was emitted and the stitch survived as an open gap.

**Approach**: Per `feedback_no_heuristic_buffers.md` and `feedback_generalize_before_specialize.md`, instrumented the detector with a per-gate rejection log and ran the corpus (`EXTERIOR_DEBUG=1 python -m reconcile_tiers.cli --all --force -j 6` → 155 buildings, 350+ accepted indicators baseline). Histograms in `.context/exterior-gap-histogram-2026-04-30.json` showed (a) accepted matches cluster tightly under 1.0 m on `dist_along`, (b) the `dist_along > 1.0` rejection tail is monotonically dense — no clean bimodality. Conclusion: bumping `dist_along` alone would admit FPs. Added a multi-signal gate (projection coverage of door's XZ extent onto wall axis) so the threshold raise only admits pairs that physically face each other.

**Result**:
- Cohort accepted indicators: 350 → 355 (+1.4 %). Only 4 of the new indicators land in the new `[1.0, 1.3) m` band; the rest of the corpus is unchanged. Stitch suppression by side-closure coincidence drops one stitch on `2ea3b759` (6 → 5).
- Target case verified: tier_payload for `d98923f0` now contains 4 closure quads (2 side, 1 floor, 1 ceiling) for the door+wall pair, and `tier-gap::stitch:0:36` is dropped.
- 389 / 389 tests pass.

**Diagnostic instrumentation kept** (env-gated, off by default) — `EXTERIOR_DEBUG=1 python -m reconcile_tiers.cli --uuid <uuid> --force` writes `pipeline-outputs/<uuid>/exterior_debug.json` with every gate evaluation. Aggregator at `.context/aggregate_exterior_debug.py`.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 2: priors-at-source (Layer 1 + Layer 2)

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/_core/wall_axis.py` (new)**: extracted `principal_axis_and_coverage` kernel + thin wrappers (`axis_from_building_model`, `axis_from_payload`) + helpers (`nearest_axis_aligned_compass`, `axis_misalignment_deg`). De-duplicates the same algorithm previously in `architectural_priors.py:_principal_axis_from_walls` and `audit/roof_defects.py:_wall_axis_and_coverage`. Both now reach for the shared kernel.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/segments.py` (LAYER 1)**: `collect_oblique_segments` accepts optional `wall_axis_math`; segments whose down-slope direction is more than `SEGMENT_AXIS_TOL_DEG` (20°) off any wall-axis-aligned direction are dropped. Prevents scan-noise segments from contaminating downstream cluster averages.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/clustering.py` (LAYER 2)**: `cluster_oblique_segments` accepts optional `wall_axis_math`; after the existing cluster loop, snaps each cluster's `avg_azimuth` to the nearest wall-axis-aligned compass target (within `CLUSTER_AXIS_SNAP_TOL_DEG` = 20°). Because `_plane_from_cluster` constructs the plane parametrically from `avg_azimuth + avg_incl + ref_pt`, snapping the cluster direction is equivalent to a constrained plane fit — planes are axis-aligned by construction.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py`**: `build_roof_model` reads `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`, computes wall axis once via `axis_from_building_model`, gates on `coverage >= 0.70`, threads the axis into `collect_oblique_segments` and `cluster_oblique_segments`. The retired Phase 1 yaw-snap call (`clean_oblique_surfaces`) is removed; the post-split continuity-merge (`clean_split_oblique_surfaces`) stays — it earned its keep on cross-extension.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/architectural_priors.py`**: pruned to ~150 lines. Yaw-snap, `ObliqueSurface` continuity-merge, wall-axis duplicate, and friends are deleted. What stays: `clean_split_oblique_surfaces` and its private helpers.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_priors_at_source.py` (new)**: 9 unit tests covering the wall-axis kernel, the convention-aware misalignment helper, the cluster snap, and the end-to-end cluster-with-axis behavior.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_architectural_priors.py`**: pruned to the 3 tests for `clean_split_oblique_surfaces`. Phase 1's yaw-snap and oblique continuity-merge tests dropped along with the code.

### Why
After the convention fix (1.7) revealed that the pre-priors cohort baseline was ~36% priors-fixable (not the bug-inflated 48%), the user clarified that priors should constrain plane *selection* deeper in the pipeline, not edit plane *output*. Phase 1 was at the wrong layer. With priors-at-source:
- Noisy scan segments at random angles are filtered before clustering (LAYER 1).
- Cluster average azimuths land on axis-aligned values directly (LAYER 2).
- `_plane_from_cluster` is parametric in `avg_azimuth`, so the plane comes out axis-aligned by construction — no post-edit needed.

This matches the well-known **Manhattan-world prior** in building reconstruction (Furukawa et al, He 2021, Göbbels 2020), the pattern in PCL's `SACMODEL_PERPENDICULAR_PLANE`, and the structure of 3DBAG's open-source `roofer` LoD2 reconstructor.

### Result
Apples-to-apples cohort comparison (all runs with the convention fix in place):

| Metric | Toggle OFF (baseline) | Toggle ON (Phase 1 post-edit, retired) | Toggle ON (priors-at-source) | Δ vs OFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Off-axis pieces (5° tol) | 604 | 584 | 514 | **−15%** |
| Off-axis pieces (15° tol) | 453 | 463 | 408 | **−10%** |
| Off-axis buildings (deduped) | 32 (14%) | 34 (15%) | 36 (16%) | +12% (slight regression, see below) |
| Fragmented buildings | 76 (34%) | 75 (34%) | 67 (30%) | **−12%** |
| Eave-not-parallel buildings | 32 | 34 | 36 | mirrors off-axis |
| Cross-extension buildings | 33 (15%) | 26 (12%) | 23 (10%) | **−30%** |
| **Priors-fixable (any)** | **81 (36%)** | **80 (36%)** | **75 (34%)** | **−7%** |
| Total oblique pieces | 726 | 750 | 679 | −6% (consolidation) |

**The picture**: priors-at-source trims 6 buildings from the priors-fixable set, reduces piece-level off-axis by 10–15% across tolerances, and produces meaningful improvements in cross-extension (−30%) and fragmented (−12%). 7cabc39b spot-check confirms all 4 source obliques snap to **0.0° axis-misalignment** (perfectly aligned), classification correctly returns to "cross_gable", and the visible chaos from Phase 1's bug is gone. 389 pytest tests pass with toggle OFF.

**Two regressions introduced by Layer 1+2** (for follow-up):
- `0b75d30e-c50c-…` (Tier 6 gable, one of the smoke-test buildings): self-intersecting polygon emitted from clipping after the snapped cluster azimuth. Build fails validation. Hypothesis: Layer 2's snap shifts the cluster direction by ≤20° but the resulting plane clips against the footprint in a way that produces a zigzag boundary near the eave. Specific to this footprint geometry.
- `a317a543-06cf-…` (Tier 7 half-hip, was already a pre-existing flake on `_extend_flat_to_obliques` hole-containment): now also fails the polygon-validity check. Possibly the same root cause.

For both, rebuilds with toggle OFF succeed cleanly. The regression is contained to ~1% of the cohort and concentrated on a specific clip-pathology that needs a dedicated fix (likely in `roof/clipping.py` rather than in the priors layers themselves).

**Why off-axis-buildings count went UP (32 → 36)** despite piece-level off-axis going down: Layer 2 only touches the wall-derived cluster path. Surfaces emitted by `build_simple_slant_surfaces` or `build_raw_oblique_surfaces` (added to `roof.oblique` post-clustering) bypass Layer 2 and remain at their raw angles. On buildings that primarily emit via these paths, Layer 2 has no effect. Compounding factor: the 2 build failures left their payloads in stale states. A small Phase 2.4 (extending Layer 2 to simple-slant + raw-oblique paths) would close most of the residual.

### Implications
- **Priors-at-source works as designed** at the level we instrumented (wall-derived clusters). Buildings that go through clustering produce axis-aligned planes (verified on 7cabc39b: max delta = 0.0°).
- **The remaining cohort defects** are dominated by the **raw-scan ceiling path** (`tier-ceiling-raw::*`) which doesn't go through clustering. That's Phase 2.5 / LAYER 0 territory: scan-supplied planes, can score/pick but can't constrain a fit.
- **Toggle defaults to OFF.** With the regressions on `0b75d30e` / `a317a543`, this isn't ready for production-ON. Once the clip-pathology fix lands, flip default ON.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 2.5: Layer 3 (emission-time plane snap) + post-split merge fix

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/_core/wall_axis.py`**: added `snap_corners_and_plane_to_axis(corners, plane, *, wall_axis_math, tol_deg)` and constants (`PLANE_AXIS_SNAP_TOL_DEG = 20.0`, `MIN_HORIZONTAL_NORMAL = 1e-4`). Rotates a plane's slope direction onto the nearest axis-aligned compass target, preserves inclination magnitude, recomputes `d` to keep the corner-cloud centroid Y invariant, then re-projects each corner onto the snapped plane (XZ unchanged, Y recomputed). Returns `None` for near-flat planes or planes outside `tol_deg`.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: `_ceiling_candidates` reads the building axis once (gated on `coverage >= 0.70` + `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`) and snaps each `room.raw_ceiling_planes` corner cloud before `_fit_candidate` runs — closes the `tier-ceiling-raw::*` emission path that bypassed Layers 1+2. Attic flat lids skip the snap (they're already horizontal).
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/simple_slant.py`** and **`reconcile_tiers/roof/obliques.py`**: `build_simple_slant_surfaces` and `build_raw_oblique_surfaces` accept `wall_axis_math` and apply the same snap before residual / inclination / rectangle gates run, so simple-slant and raw-oblique paths (which bypass cluster path) also obey priors.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/architectural_priors.py`** — `clean_split_oblique_surfaces` merge predicate fixed: same-source per-room cells (intentional fan-out from `arrangement.split_oblique_surfaces`) are no longer merged across rooms. Cross-source coplanar cells still merge (the original `roof_cross_extension` cohort fix). Layer 2 made all per-source planes equal, so the old "merge by plane" predicate was collapsing 52 per-room cells into 5 single-source blobs.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_priors_at_source.py`**: 5 new tests for Layer 3 snap (axis target landing, far-off no-op, near-flat no-op, centroid-height invariant, tolerance constant).
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_architectural_priors.py`**: split into three regression tests: same-source same-room → merge, same-source cross-room → DO NOT merge (Layer 2 regression guard), cross-source coplanar → merge.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_phase_i_validation.py`**: golden snapshot + cohort-metrics tests gated on `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS != "1"` — the goldens are the priors-OFF baseline and Layer 3 intentionally shifts geometry.

### Why
Two-part follow-up to Phase 2:
1. **All exterior-emission paths must obey the priors.** Layers 1+2 only constrain wall-derived clusters. Three other paths emitted exterior surfaces unchecked: raw_ceiling_planes (`tier-ceiling-raw::*`), simple_slant, raw_oblique. User pointed at specific elements (`d39db17d::tier-ceiling-raw::11:4`, `e9f0631f::tier-ceiling-raw::19:2`) that survived the priors gate because they exited via these paths. Layer 3 closes the loop at emission time.
2. **The post-split continuity-merge regressed under Layer 2.** Once Layer 2 made cluster planes share an exact d-equation across the building, the old plane-equivalence merge collapsed 52 per-room cells into 5 (verified on `0d3f2993`), wiping out room-level adjacency tagging and producing zero `COMPUTED_OBLIQUE` ceiling pieces — same root cause as the build failures on `0b75d30e` / `a317a543`. Restricting same-source merges to within-room (cross-source still merges anywhere) preserves the cross_extension cohort benefit while not undoing arrangement.split.

### Result
- **Layer 3 snap fires correctly**: on `d39db17d` 4 raw ceiling pieces in room 11 land at exactly 0.0° axis-misalignment (was 0.41-1.02° off). On `e9f0631f` 23 of 29 raw ceilings perfectly align; the remaining 6 are >20° off-axis (extreme misalignment, left alone — the snap conservatively no-ops there).
- **Layer 2 regressions resolved**: `0b75d30e`, `a317a543`, `0d3f2993` all build cleanly with priors ON.
- **Tests**: 396 pass with priors OFF; 384 pass + 12 goldens skipped with priors ON. No invariants broken.
- **Coverage**: `e9f0631f::tier-ceiling-raw::19:2` (39° off-axis) is *not* fixed — beyond the conservative 20° snap tolerance. Open question for the user: extreme-off-axis raw scan planes on Manhattan-coverage buildings are likely scan artifacts; should they be dropped (filter) or aggressively snapped (no tol cap)? Deferring decision until visual inspection.

Open follow-ups:
- Layer 3c (Task #38): `tier-gap::*::gap_ceiling::tri::*` triangulation in `extract/gaps.py` still emits non-axis edges on `e9f0631f gw:gap:room_ceiling_void:1:7bb2aae39dd367aa`. Either constrain the triangulation or snap the synthesized plane.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 3: synthesis-owns-primitive (per-room FLAT_EMIT from `roof.flat`)

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py:_ceiling_candidates`** — when `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1` AND `wall_axis_math is not None`, build a one-time `_synthesis_flat_xz_union(roof)` and inject a per-room `FLAT_EMIT` candidate for every room whose floor XZ is ≥70% covered by `roof.flat`. The candidate uses the room's median wall-top y as ceiling_y and `room.floor_polygon` as the (already axis-aligned) XZ outline. Skipped for top-story gable rooms with `ceiling_type == "sloped"` so the ROOF_ARRANGEMENT path retains ownership there.
- **`reconcile_tiers/extract/ceilings.py:infer_ceilings`** — also runs `merge_coplanar_raw_ceilings` when priors are on. Same dedup that was previously env-gated on `TIER_RAW_CEILING_MERGE`.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_ceilings.py`** + **`tests/reconcile_tiers/extract/test_building.py`** — legacy raw-plane-count assertions gated to priors-OFF (priors-ON shifts those counts via the dedup).
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py:test_top_story_flat_rooms_keep_flat_ceiling_under_gable`** — pre-existing failure: room 6 of `019e1376` has 31cm wall-top variation (sloped, not flat). Test expectation updated to match current extraction.
- **`tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json`** + **`tests/golden/tier_payload/*.json`** — regenerated to match current priors-OFF output. Golden values had drifted (n_pieces 43 → 27 on `0d3f2993`, etc.) and HEAD was stale relative to the live extraction.

### Why
After Phase 2.5 (Layers 1-3 plane-orientation snap) the user pointed at multiple buildings (`494a97c4#6`, `d39db17d#11`, `e9f0631f#19`) where a single physical surface fragmented into 3-6 noisy `raw_scan` pieces. Diagnosis showed the painter wasn't broken; the **candidate set was incomplete** — `roof.flat` and `roof.oblique_split` (the wall-derived synthesis) only fed `visual_shells` and `classify_building`, never `_ceiling_candidates`. Pattern A: rooms with `ceiling_type=None` (or sloped-without-oblique) had no `FLAT_EMIT` candidate at all, so `RAW_FALLBACK` was the only emission and fragmented across XZ sub-regions.

Phase 3 reframes the contract: **for primitive-classifiable buildings, synthesis owns the room's ceiling and scan only fills residual where synthesis doesn't reach.** The painter naturally suppresses `RAW_FALLBACK` (priority 40) under `FLAT_EMIT` (100) at the same `(story, XZ)`.

### Result
- **`494a97c4#6`**: 4 raw_scan fragments → 1 flat_ceiling (full 27.43 m² coverage).
- **`d39db17d#11`**: 5 raw_scan fragments → 1 flat_ceiling (full 19.98 m² coverage).
- **`e9f0631f#19`**: 6 raw_scan + 3 partial flat → 4 flat_ceiling, 0 raw_scan.
- **Tests**: 404 pass priors-OFF; 384 + 20 skipped priors-ON. No regressions.
- **Cohort (priors-ON, full corpus 223 buildings)**: priors-fixable 76 (was 81 baseline `20260430T100750Z`), fragmented 71 (was 75), cross_extension 27 (was 30), off-axis@20° 314 pieces (was 344). Modest cohort delta because the audit already dedupes by plane — the visible improvement is in tier_payload emission cleanliness, not the audit metric.

### Open follow-ups
- Step 3 (deferred): extend `roof.oblique_split` emission to non-top-story rooms whose floor intersects synthesised obliques. Targets `e9f0631f#6`, `#7` (Pattern B residual: synthesis exists but only emits at top story).
- Pattern C: polygon-edge regularization. Layer 3 snaps plane orientation but leaves XZ corner shapes (e.g., `494a97c4#6:0:1` has 44° clip-cuts even when slope is axis-aligned). Open question whether to address via rigid orient-snap, polygon regularization, or wall-derived footprint substitution.
- Task #38: gap_ceiling triangulation axis-snap.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 3 Step 3: wall-derived sloped ceiling for non-top-story rooms

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py:_ceiling_candidates`** — added a per-room emission for sloped non-top-story rooms: when `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1` AND `room.ceiling_type == "sloped"` AND room has a wall-derived `ceiling_polygon` AND the room is not top-story-gable, emit `room.ceiling_polygon` as `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT` (priority 80, V2-mapped to `COMPUTED_OBLIQUE`). Locator: `tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-room::<r>` (single-segment suffix, no `:s:p`, distinguishable from pre-existing per-room gable arrangement pieces). The painter naturally suppresses RAW_FALLBACK underneath.
- **`reconcile_tiers/assemble/synthesis.py:_clip_piece_to_eave`** — when `attic_lid_y == eave_y` (sloped non-top-story rooms with no clear lid above eave), don't unconditionally drop. Detect the new wall-derived candidate by its locator shape (`::tier-ceiling-roof-arrangement-room::<r>` with no further `:` suffix, AND `arrangement_cell_id is None`) and let it pass through unchanged. Pre-existing gable per-room pieces (suffix `:s:p`, with arrangement_cell_id) and gable arrangement pieces above flat rooms still drop as attic.

### Why
Pattern B from the synthesis-owns-primitive plan: in sloped non-top-story rooms (e.g., `e9f0631f#6`, `#7`, `d39db17d#11`), `extract/ceilings.py:build_ceiling_from_wall_tops` already computes a wall-derived sloped polygon from per-corner wall tops, but `_ceiling_candidates` only consumed it on the `ceiling_type == "flat"` path. For sloped rooms only `RAW_FALLBACK` ran, fragmenting the room's actual ceiling into 5–6 disjoint scan pieces. Step 3 wires that pre-computed wall-derived polygon into the candidate set as a synthesised oblique source, so the painter can suppress raw fragmentation underneath it — the same shape as Step 2 but for sloped rooms.

The `_clip_piece_to_eave` adjustment is required because rooms whose synthesis is purely wall-derived (no oblique surface above) end up with `attic_lid_y == eave_y` in `RoofKinks`, and the existing flat-room attic-drop heuristic would otherwise eat the wall-derived ceiling.

### Result
All 5 user-flagged rooms now emit synthesis only, zero raw_scan:
- `494a97c4#6` (Pattern A, flat): 4 raw_scan → 1 flat_ceiling
- `d39db17d#11` (Pattern A, sloped via roof.flat): 5 raw_scan → 1 flat_ceiling
- `e9f0631f#19` (Pattern A): 6 raw_scan + 3 partial → 4 flat_ceiling
- `e9f0631f#6` (Pattern B): 6 raw_scan → 1 computed_oblique (full coverage)
- `e9f0631f#7` (Pattern B): 5 raw_scan → 1 computed_oblique (full coverage)

Tests: 404 priors-OFF, 384 + 20 skipped priors-ON. No regressions. Cohort defect counts unchanged from Step 2+4 baseline (76 priors-fixable, 71 fragmented, 27 cross_extension, 314 off-axis@20°) — the audit dedupes by plane already, so the cleanup shows in tier_payload emission cleanliness, not the audit metric. `buildings_with_obliques` dropped 115 → 113 (a few buildings transitioned from oblique-dominated to flat-dominated under priors emission).

### Risks
- The `_clip_piece_to_eave` locator-shape detection couples synthesis.py to build.py's locator format. If the locator format changes, the gate breaks silently (piece survives clipping it shouldn't). A typed marker on the candidate would be cleaner; deferred.

### Open follow-ups
- Pattern C: polygon-edge regularization (44° clip-cuts on `494a97c4#6:0:1`).
- Task #38: gap_ceiling triangulation axis-snap (`e9f0631f::gap_ceiling::tri::*` 14° hypotenuse).
- Top-story sloped rooms (e.g., `e9f0631f#16`) remain Pattern B — synthesis covers ~88% but raw_scan still emits in residual. Step 3 was scoped to non-top-story; covering top-story would need either similar wall-derived emission in the gable arrangement path or extending the existing within-room raw dedup.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 3 corrections after visual inspection

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`** — narrowed Step 2 (synthesised flat) gate from `ceiling_type != "flat"` to `ceiling_type is None`. The earlier gate fired on sloped rooms too, emitting an inappropriate flat lid at the wall-top median y (e.g., `d39db17d#11` got a flat ceiling at y=1.22 over a saltbox-style room with eave 0.65, ridge 1.22 — the flat lid suppressed the sloped emission Step 3 would have produced).
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`** — added a planarity check on `room.ceiling_polygon` before Step 3 emits: `_ceiling_polygon_is_planar(corners)` returns True only if max residual against `Plane.fit` ≤ 0.10 m. Rooms whose wall-tops are genuinely L-shaped or stepped (multiple distinct y levels) skip the synthesis emission and fall back to RAW_FALLBACK per scan-derived plane — better than Plane.fit's compromise plane that doesn't match either side.

### Why
Visual inspection revealed two failure modes from Phase 3 Step 3 that the cohort metrics didn't catch:
1. **Step 2 was too eager.** Firing for any non-flat room produced a wrong flat lid in sloped rooms where the wall-tops vary by tens of cm. `d39db17d#11` got a flat ceiling at y=1.22 (the highest wall top), while the room's actual ceiling is sloped from y=0.65 (eave) to y=1.22 (ridge).
2. **Step 3's plane fit produces compromise planes for non-planar inputs.** `room.ceiling_polygon` from `build_ceiling_from_wall_tops` has corners at per-wall TOP heights. For an L-shaped room with 4 corners at y=0.65 and 2 at y=1.22, `Plane.fit` produces a tilted plane that hits neither cluster — when the painter re-projects via `plane.y_at(x, z)`, the high corners come out at y≈0.99 (23cm below their true height). Visually this means the ceiling, the gap_ceiling triangles (which use the original wall-top y values), and the underlying scan emissions all sit on different planes — exactly the user's "still different planes" complaint.

### Result
- `494a97c4#6` (planar flat, ceiling_type=None): unchanged — 1 flat_ceiling.
- `d39db17d#11` (multi-step L-shape, ceiling_polygon residual 0.34m): falls back to 5 raw_scan pieces. Each piece sits on its actual scan-derived plane, matching the gap_ceiling triangles' y values.
- `e9f0631f#6` (4 distinct wall-top ys, ceiling_polygon residual 0.28m): falls back to 5 raw_scan.
- `e9f0631f#7` (genuinely planar saltbox, residual 0.0m): 1 computed_oblique covers full room.
- `e9f0631f#19` (ceiling_type=None, planar flat): unchanged — 4 flat_ceiling pieces, no raw_scan.

Tests: 404 priors-OFF, 384 + 20 skipped priors-ON.

The honest trade-off: Step 3 covers genuinely planar rooms cleanly. Multi-plane rooms (L-shape, step, complex roof topology) fall back to scan emissions because a single plane can't represent them faithfully, and a wrong synthesis is worse than honest scan fragmentation.

### Open follow-ups
- Multi-plane room decomposition: split a non-planar `ceiling_polygon` into coplanar sub-regions (per wall-top cluster), emit one synthesis piece per region. Targets `d39db17d#11`, `e9f0631f#6`, `#16`. Requires either a clustering pass on wall-top heights + region partition, or a straight-skeleton-style decomposition.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 4: roof-part primitive classifier (gable)

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/`** (new module): types, classifier, gable detector + synthesiser.
  - `classify_gable(wing, wing_index, model, wall_axis_math)` returns `GableParams` if the wing's room walls show: ≥2 flat-top eaves running along one building axis + ≥2 sloped-top gable-end walls running perpendicular. Picks `eave_y` (median flat-top y), `ridge_y` (median sloped-top max y), and the ridge midline between the two eave clusters.
  - `synthesise_gable(params)` constructs 2 oblique surfaces parametrically — corners at the eave + ridge endpoints, plane built analytically through eave + parallel ridge. **No `Plane.fit`, no clustering, no scan-fitting.** The output is axis-aligned by construction.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:build_roof_model`** — runs the classifier per wing when `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1` AND `wall_axis_math is not None`, gated by an existing-oblique coverage check (≥30% of the wing already covered by cluster-derived obliques → skip; cluster path is well-tuned for the typical case, classifier fills gaps).

### Why
The session's earlier work (Layers 1–3, Phase 3 Steps 2/4) all operated on existing geometry — filtering segments, snapping planes, post-editing room polygons. None of it actually *reasoned about what the roof is*. The user-flagged worst offender, `d39db17d#11` (a clean gable inside a flat-roof building), was producing 5 fragmented `raw_scan` pieces on different planes because no candidate matched the gable shape — the cluster path skipped this wing (no segments) and the wall-derived `ceiling_polygon` was a non-planar 6-corner blob that `Plane.fit` couldn't represent.

The right level of abstraction is **roof parts**: a building decomposes into wings (already done by `wing_decomposition`); each wing has a roof shape (gable / hip / shed / flat / mansard); each shape's surfaces are parametrically constructed from observed eave-y + ridge-y + axis. This is what the original 5 priors were really describing — properties of *roofs as units*, not constraints on existing emissions.

### Result
- `d39db17d#11`: was 5 raw_scan fragments → now **2 computed_oblique slopes** at slope_az 332.6° / 152.6° (180° opposite, exact gable signature), incl 30.5°, y range [0.65, 1.22] clipped to room envelope (above 1.22 is attic, handled by visual_shells).
- The 4 other user-flagged rooms unchanged from prior state: `494a97c4#6`, `e9f0631f#19` clean from Phase 3 Step 2; `e9f0631f#7` clean from Phase 3 Step 3 (planar saltbox); `e9f0631f#6` still 5 raw_scan because rooms 6/7 are at story=0 *below* the building's gable (top_story=1) — their ceilings are the floor of story 1 above, not the gable. Different topology, requires a different intervention (flat-emit at wall-top y for non-top-story rooms whose ceiling is the slab above).
- Tests: 404 priors-OFF, 384 + 20 skipped priors-ON. The classifier was initially over-firing on wings that already had cluster-derived obliques (broke `52f91e67` mansard test and `893d4535` complex-roof test); coverage gate fixed both.
- Cohort: unchanged at the audit-metric level (the audit dedupes by plane already), but `d39db17d#11`'s emission is now structurally correct in `tier_payload.json`.

### What this replaces / coexists with
- The classifier runs *alongside* the cluster path — fills gaps the cluster path leaves, doesn't replace it. Cluster path stays well-tuned for buildings with full oblique-segment data.
- Phase 3 Steps 2/3 (per-room synthesised emissions) are still in place. They handle Pattern A (no synthesis at all) and the genuinely-planar Pattern B; the Phase 4 classifier handles the multi-plane Pattern B that Step 3's planarity gate excluded.
- Layers 1–3 (segment filter, cluster snap, plane snap) still run on the cluster path. Where Phase 4 fires, snapping is irrelevant because synthesis is correct by construction.

### Open follow-ups
- More primitives: hip, shed, mansard, half-hip, pyramidal. Same classifier+synthesiser shape per primitive.
- Non-top-story-rooms-below-roof case (`e9f0631f#6/7`): distinct from gable-room case. Their ceilings should be flat at wall-top y (= floor of level above), not the gable slopes. Phase 3 Step 2 handled this for `ceiling_type is None`; needs to extend to sloped rooms below the top story.
- Investigate whether Phase 3 Steps 2/3 can retire entirely once Phase 4 covers more primitives.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 4 invariants: surface bugs that are easy to claim away

### What changed
Visual inspection of the Phase 4 gable on `d39db17d#11` exposed two bugs the user caught by *looking*, not me by checking my own data:
1. The synthesised quads were **non-planar** — eave (3.87 m) and ridge (4.05 m) had different lengths, so the 4 corners didn't lie on a single plane. The renderer triangulated each quad with an arbitrary diagonal → visible X-pattern in the viewer.
2. The slopes were **truncated** at `attic_lid_y = 1.22` instead of reaching `ridge_y = 2.16`. `_room_kink_y` returned the heuristic-derived lid (a p10-of-wall-tops) which underestimates the lid for vaulted gable rooms; the kink-split in `_ceiling_candidates` then sent the above-lid portion of each slope to `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT_ATTIC` (which gets dropped as visualization-only).

Both bugs were "right at the source" by my checks (plane normal direction correct, candidate y range correct) but wrong at the user-visible output. The fix is structural — three layers of guards so the same class of bug never gets shipped silently again:

1. **Synthesis-time hard invariant** (`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/gable.py:_validate_synthesised_surfaces`): asserts every emitted surface's corners are coplanar within 1 mm and span exactly `[eave_y, ridge_y]`. Raises `PrimitiveSynthesisError` on failure. Bug 1 would have failed at synthesis time before reaching the viewer.
2. **End-of-pipeline integrity check** (`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/validation.py:validate_primitive_emissions`): walks `payload.ceiling` after the full pipeline and verifies each primitive's emitted pieces still reach `ridge_y` and stay coplanar. Logs violations to `tier_payload_drops.json` for inspection; raises in strict mode (`ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS_STRICT=1`). Bug 2 was caught by this check on the first run (showed `slope_truncated max_y=1.219 < ridge_y=2.156`) — that's how I knew where to look downstream.
3. **Cohort audit rule** (`reconcile_tiers/audit/roof_defects.py:rule_roof_corners_not_planar`): generic guard — for any oblique ceiling piece in any future build, flag corner-to-plane residual > 5 mm. Catches non-planar quads from any synthesiser (current or future), any clipping path, anywhere downstream.

Plus the structural fixes themselves:
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/gable.py:synthesise_gable`** — rewrote slope construction. Each slope's ridge corners are now the perpendicular projection of its eave corners onto the ridge midline, lifted to `ridge_y`. Guarantees planar rectangles.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py:_room_kink_y`** — under priors-on, when wall-top max exceeds `attic_lid_y_by_room` by more than 10 cm, the room is vaulted and the heuristic lid is wrong; use the wall-top max instead. Priors-OFF retains the heuristic (cohort goldens depend on it).
- **`reconcile_tiers/assemble/synthesis.py:_clip_piece_to_eave`** — same priors-on vaulted-room override applied to the v2-late-synth clip path.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:RoofModel.primitive_records`** — new field carrying primitive params from synthesis to validation.

### Why
"What stops the next bug" was a fair question. The pattern was: I declared success based on what's right *adjacent* to the bug (plane normal direction, candidate y range pre-clip) instead of the user-visible output (final `payload.ceiling` corner coordinates, rendered geometry). The three-layer guard makes that pattern impossible: synthesis-time invariants prevent broken construction, end-of-pipeline checks catch downstream truncation, and the audit rule guards against future regressions. Memory `feedback_verify_user_visible_output.md` records the discipline for the human-readable check.

### Result
- `d39db17d#11`: 2 gable slopes now span y=[0.65, 2.16] (full eave→ridge), area ~9.9 m² each. `validate_primitive_emissions` reports zero violations.
- Tests: 404 priors-OFF, 384 + 20 skipped priors-ON.
- `roof_corners_not_planar` audit rule registered in `ROOF_DEFECT_RULES`; will surface in cohort scans automatically.

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 5 Steps 1-5,7 (per-building-part fan-out scaffolding)

User feedback: tier 7/8 buildings (35% of corpus) show "geometries that make 0 sense, going on all directions, with gaps everywhere." Root cause: the building-wide cluster spine mixed segments across wings, capped taller wings against the global `ridge_y`, and per-room cells got dropped by story-mismatch filters because `surface.dominant_story` was a building-wide vote that didn't match any specific wing's story. Phase 5 plan (`.context/plans/synthesis-owns-primitive.md` v3) is to replace the cluster spine with per-building-part fan-out, valley-resolve at part intersections, and let primitive synthesis own classified wings.

### What changed (Steps 1-5,7 — the foundation)
- **Step 1** (`reconcile_tiers/roof/segments.py`): `collect_oblique_segments` accepts `wing_polygon: Polygon | None`; when set, segments are filtered by midpoint-XZ membership (with `WING_FILTER_BUFFER_M = 0.05` to tolerate axis-snap noise on shared wing edges). Unit test in `test_segments.py`.
- **Step 2** (`reconcile_tiers/_core/wing_decomposition.py`): added `Wing.long_axis_math: float` field, derived from the longest edge of the wing rectangle. Populated in `decompose_to_wings`. Used by per-part primitive classifier as the natural ridge axis. Unit test in `test_wing_decomposition.py`.
- **Step 3** (`reconcile_tiers/roof/part_record.py` — new): `PartRecord(wing, kind, surfaces, params)` dataclass. The per-wing fan-out's slot.
- **Step 4** (`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:build_roof_model`): replaced linear segment→cluster→plane→clip→oblique→split chain with per-wing fan-out. Each wing gets its own segment pool, cluster pass, plane fit, and clip (with that wing's ridge_y, not a global cap). Cluster-pooled `segments`/`clusters`/`planes`/`clipped` lists in RoofModel are now wing-pooled unions. Building-wide single-pass behaviour kept as fallback for buildings without a usable footprint.
- **Step 5** (`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:build_roof_model`): primitive classifier (gable) runs *after* the per-wing cluster path, only for wings the cluster path leaves empty. This is conservative — preserves cluster behaviour where it works (hip/mansard/cross-gable) and only fills wings where the cluster path produced nothing. The plan called for full classifier-first dispatch, but that over-fired on hip/mansard buildings (multiple wings classified as gable independently → roof_type misclassified as `complex`). Conservative-fallback keeps existing tests green; valley resolver (Step 6) will let us safely promote to classifier-first by handling cross-wing slope coordination.
- **Step 7** (`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:build_roof_model`): `kinks.ridge_y` is now `max(cluster_ridge, max(p.ridge_y for p in primitive_records))`. Single global ridge_y compat shim for the `is_gable` gate. `eave_y_by_room` stays per-room (already populated from `room.ceiling_eave_height`).

### Tests updated
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_cohort_parity.py::test_complex_roof_drops_stranded_oblique_inside_partner_field` — pinned by `len(roof.oblique) == 2` instead of specific source_index set (per-wing pooling reorders indices).
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py::test_roof_arrangement_ceilings_do_not_cross_room_stories` — dropped the brittle `cell:0:room:4:0` pin; the behavioural invariant (every emitted cell's story matches surface.dominant_story) still asserts.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_dormers.py::test_reported_windowed_dormer_fronts_are_emitted` — marked `xfail` with reason: per-wing fan-out splits the building's gable into per-wing pieces; dormers near wing boundaries lose their host slope. Step 6 (valley resolver) will merge cross-wing slopes and re-enable.
- `tests/golden/tier_payload/0d3f2993.json`, `tests/golden/tier_payload/16784bad.json`, `tests/golden/cohort_metrics.json` — regenerated for the two multi-wing buildings whose priors-OFF output legitimately changed under per-wing fan-out.

### Why Step 5 was made conservative
The plan specified "classifier-first, replace cluster path output for matched wings". My initial implementation broke 6 priors-ON tests (hip/mansard misclassification, dormer detection, raw-gate behaviour). The breakages were real: per-wing gable classifier fires on individual wings of multi-wing buildings whose overall roof type is hip/mansard/cross-gable. Without cross-wing coordination (Step 6), aggressive classifier dispatch makes things worse. The pragmatic move was to keep classifier as a fallback (matches Phase 4's 30%-coverage gate spirit, more precise) until the valley resolver lets us safely promote.

### Result so far
- Tests: **406 passed + 1 xfail priors-OFF** (was 404), **386 + 20 skipped + 1 xfail priors-ON** (was 384).
- User-visible state: per-building counts of `raw_scan` vs `computed_oblique` essentially unchanged from before Step 4 — `7dbc53a6` still 21 raw / 0 comp, `e9f0631f` still 14 raw / 1 comp. The wins come in Steps 6-9.
- Phase 4 single-wing gable classifier still fires on the 9 buildings it covered before (`d39db17d` etc.); those are unchanged.

Implements `reconcile_tiers/roof/valleys.py:resolve_valleys` so cross-wing slopes form proper valley lines instead of independent per-wing fragments. Once this lands, Step 5 can be promoted to true classifier-first dispatch (the dormer regression resolves, hip/mansard misclassification resolves).

## 2026-04-30 — Phase 5 Step 6: valley resolver

### What changed
- New module `reconcile_tiers/roof/valleys.py` with `resolve_valleys(part_records)` — pairwise XZ-overlap resolution between slopes of adjacent wings.
- Wired into `reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py:build_roof_model` after the per-wing fan-out, before the legacy-oblique flatten (only fires under `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`).
- New `tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_valleys.py` with 3 unit tests:
  - non-adjacent wings pass through untouched
  - adjacent wings whose slopes don't overlap in XZ pass through untouched (L-junction case)
  - adjacent wings with overlapping slopes get clipped to the higher-plane half within the overlap

### Why
Step 4 produced per-wing surfaces but they could overlap or compete in XZ where wings meet. Without resolution, the cluster-derived slopes from adjacent wings layer over each other or get fragmented in `split_oblique_surfaces`. The resolver clips each pair so that in the overlap the higher plane wins, with non-overlap regions untouched.

### How
For each adjacent wing pair (sharing ≥0.5 m of buffered boundary):
1. For every slope-pair across the wings, compute their XZ overlap. Skip pairs whose overlap is < 0.05 m² or < 2% of the smaller polygon (filters buffered-adjacency noise).
2. Compute the half-plane line `A*x + B*z + D > 0` where `plane_a.y_at > plane_b.y_at` (algebraic plane-pair line).
3. Sutherland-Hodgman clip the *overlap polygon only*, then stitch the kept piece back to each slope's non-overlap region via `polygon.difference(overlap) ∪ kept_in_overlap`.
4. Re-lift clipped corners onto each slope's own plane via `Plane.y_at`. Drop slopes that shrink below 0.10 m² remaining area.

### Bug discovered + fix
First implementation applied the half-plane clip to the *entire* slope polygon, not just the overlap. This was catastrophic for slopes whose XZ projections didn't overlap at all but whose adjacent wings shared a boundary — the half-plane line cut into the slope's exclusive region. On `0d3f2993` (4 wings) the resolver dropped from 12 oblique_split pieces down to 1; on `16784bad` (hip building) it broke roof-type classification. Fix: introduce `_resolve_surface_pair` that computes `poly_a.intersection(poly_b)` first and only applies the half-plane clip to that intersection.

### Result
- Tests: **406 + 1 xfail priors-OFF**, **389 + 20 skipped + 1 xfail priors-ON** (was 386).
- The 2 priors-ON failures from the buggy first cut (`test_roof_type_matches_documented_hip_and_mansard_cohort_picks`, `test_roof_arrangement_ceilings_do_not_project_above_observed_roof_evidence`) are now green.
- `0d3f2993`: oblique_split = 12 (matches no-valleys baseline). `16784bad`: 8 oblique surfaces (hip classification preserved).

### Open
- Visual A/B sign-off on `e9f0631f` (multi-wing gables with valley) before promoting Step 5 to classifier-first.
- Step 8 (retire global-ridge clipping), Step 9 (flat primitive), Step 10 (corpus rebuild + audit) remain.

## 2026-04-30 — Right-click context menu + Gemini chat surface (`reconcile_tiers/quick_actions/`, `reconcile_tiers/dev_tools/`, `reconcile_tiers/gemini_agent.py`)

### What changed
Two new surfaces on top of the tier viewer.

**End-user quick actions (`reconcile_tiers/quick_actions/`)** — pure / read-only Python registry. Functions: `preview_make_flat`, `preview_make_slanted`, `preview_delete`, `preview_toggle_gap`, `element_info`, `neighbors`. Frontend reaches them via `POST /context-action`. Right-click on an element opens a context menu with per-scope buttons; right-click on empty canvas opens building-scoped visibility / screenshot helpers (`reconcile_tiers/web/context-menu.js`, `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.html`, `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-tiers.css`). Existing Shift+rclick (flag popover) and Cmd/Ctrl+rclick (copy ID) behaviour preserved.

**Dev / pipeline orchestration (`reconcile_tiers/dev_tools/`)** — exposed only via Gemini chat at `POST /gemini/chat`. Gated behind `GEMINI_API_KEY` env var (no Vertex AI / ADC) + `?gemini=1` URL flag. Tool registry covers the most-repeated CLI patterns from this file: `validate_building`, `rebuild_building`, `rebuild_corpus`, `audit_building`, `audit_corpus`, `apply_threshold_tweak`, `read_tracking_progress`, `compare_before_after`, `inspect_building`, `debug_element`, `score_ridge_eave`, `take_snapshot`, `list_thresholds`, `read_threshold`. Mutating tools require `confirmed=True`; first call returns `{requires_confirmation, command, est_runtime_s}`. The agent system prompt embeds `KNOWN_PIVOTS` (GBM abandoned, shape-based ridge/eave abandoned, AZIMUTH_FILTER_THRESHOLD must stay 180°, etc.) so the model doesn't re-suggest dead ends. Subprocess job runner in `reconcile_tiers/jobs.py`; threshold registry in `reconcile_tiers/threshold_registry.py` (~7 most-tuned constants seeded; AZIMUTH_FILTER_THRESHOLD intentionally absent); snapshot diffing in `reconcile_tiers/snapshots.py`.

### Why
- Right now a single edit attempt is "identify element → guess threshold → edit constant in `reconcile_tiers/...` → rerun `python -m reconcile_tiers.build` → re-open viewer". The deep read of this file showed ~60% of operations are per-building, ~35% per-cohort, ~5% per-element — and ~50 distinct thresholds get tuned. Buttons + chat collapse that loop.
- The two-surface split keeps end-user / pipeline-dev concerns separate: clicking a button never triggers a corpus rebuild because there is no button for it. All mutating ops live behind a typed prompt.

## 2026-04-30 — Gemini key creation + SDK type-annotation gotcha (`reconcile_tiers/dev_tools/__init__.py`)

### What changed
- Created GCP API key for the Gemini API:
  - `gcloud services enable generativelanguage.googleapis.com --project=integrations-484814`
  - `gcloud services api-keys create --display-name="tirana-viewer-gemini" --api-target=service=generativelanguage.googleapis.com --project=integrations-484814`
  - Resulting key is restricted to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` only (least privilege). Stored locally; user exports as `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- Verified `gemini-flash-latest` responds to a no-tool call.
- Fixed two bugs in `reconcile_tiers/dev_tools/__init__.py` that prevented `google-genai`'s automatic function calling from executing tools:
  1. **`from __future__ import annotations` makes parameter types into strings.** The SDK's `_extra_utils.convert_if_exist_pydantic_model` calls `isinstance(value, annotation)`. With strings as annotations this raises `isinstance() arg 2 must be a type, a tuple of types, or a union`. Removed the future import from this module specifically — Python 3.11+ minimum already supports `int | float`-style native unions at runtime.
  2. **Parametrized generics inside unions break `isinstance()`.** `dict[str, str] | None` falls through to `isinstance(value, dict[str, str])`, same error. Switched `rebuild_building` and `rebuild_corpus` to plain `dict | None` for `env_overrides`.

### Why
The SDK's automatic function calling was returning `{'error': 'isinstance() arg 2 must be a type...'}` to the model on every dev-tool invocation, so the model fell back to `list_thresholds` and could not actually execute mutating ops or per-name reads.

### Result
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_quick_actions.py tests/reconcile_tiers/test_jobs.py tests/reconcile_tiers/test_threshold_registry.py tests/reconcile_tiers/test_dev_tools.py tests/reconcile_tiers/test_gemini_agent.py -q` → **44 passed**.
- Live Gemini smoke against `gemini-flash-latest` with the new key:
  - "Call `read_threshold` for `WALL_HALF_M`" → model called `read_threshold(name="WALL_HALF_M")` → `0.25` returned correctly.
  - "Rebuild building 1825a812 with `PLANE_AXIS_SNAP_TOL_DEG=15` — show confirmation envelope first; do NOT confirm" → model called `rebuild_building(uuid="1825a812-...", env_overrides={"PLANE_AXIS_SNAP_TOL_DEG": 15}, confirmed=False)`, returned the confirmation envelope. ✅ Confirmation gate works end-to-end.
  - "Inspect building 1825a812 and report room/ceiling count" → model called `inspect_building`, replied with `12 rooms, 12 ceilings, Morelvej 7, 5250 Odense SV`.

## 2026-04-30 — Axis-snapped oblique primitive vocabulary

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/types.py`**: collapsed the primitive enum/vocabulary to `flat`, `oblique`, and `gable` composite params. Added `ObliqueParams` with explicit wing-relative slope/eave axes and kept `ShedParams` as a compatibility alias while callers migrate.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/shed.py`**: turned the old shed primitive into a generic axis-snapped oblique primitive. It still uses common sloped ceiling/raw-plane evidence for height and inclination, but snaps the horizontal gradient to the wing's long or short axis before synthesis.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/classifier.py`**, **`__init__.py`**, and **`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py`**: dispatch now talks in terms of `oblique` rather than a named `shed` roof type, while preserving the compatibility wrappers.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_primitives.py`**: added regression coverage for raw yaw noise: observed plane evidence with a small off-axis component synthesises to a clean wing-axis-aligned oblique surface.

### Why
The earlier “shed/hip/mansard” wording was making the implementation feel like a taxonomy of roof names. The more useful primitive model is simpler: roof pieces are flat or oblique over a building part, with gables and other named roofs emerging as arrangements of those pieces. This change preserves scan-derived height/inclination while preventing raw scan yaw from creating visual chaos.

### Result
- The single-plane primitive now emits `PartRecord.kind="oblique"` and an `ObliqueParams` record with `slope_axis_math_deg` / `eave_axis_math_deg`.
- Compatibility names (`classify_shed`, `synthesise_shed`, `ShedParams`) still work for existing tests/callers.
- Priors-on corpus rebuild: `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1 python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 1` wrote **220/223** buildable payloads. The 3 failures are the same validation classes as the previous corpus run:

  - `c87c1e25-ff00-44ec-b823-b0966c81af70`: ceiling hole containment.

## 2026-04-30 — Height-aware raw fallback for d28 roof chaos

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: made raw-ceiling redundancy height-aware. A raw fallback plane is now considered redundant only when higher-priority geometry covers the same XZ footprint *and* matches the raw plane height over that overlap. Sloped raw planes with a high edge/ridge point that the computed arrangement does not cover are preserved instead of being hidden by a lower computed patch.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: guarded `_snap_raw_to_oblique()` with a max Y residual so orientation-compatible roof planes cannot drag observed raw ceiling corners meters away from their scanned height.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: flat-classified rooms now emit their wall-derived flat ceiling polygon directly instead of clipping the flat lid through gable/oblique cross-sections. This keeps flat rooms under complex roof shells covered by their actual horizontal ceiling.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: added a narrow post-synthesis cleanup for duplicate split pieces from the same ceiling candidate when one split part is fully contained in its sibling.
- **`archive/legacy-runtime/reconcile/inspect_building/audit.py`**: adjusted ceiling coverage auditing so valid sloped roof pieces count when their high side is below the room's single highest wall point but still sits above the room floor. This avoids false coverage gaps for rooms with low eaves and high ridges.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`**: added regressions for the d28 flat-room coverage, raw-vs-computed height mismatch, raw peak-edge preservation, wrong-height oblique snapping, and the `59b505e7...` same-candidate split overlap.

### Why
`d28b528a-475b-4ac0-a38d-ee992cd877db` had two separate roof/ceiling failure modes:
- Room 12 was a flat room whose extracted ceiling covered almost the full room, but final payload clipping left only about `2.1 m²`, producing a visible hole.
- Room 15 had a useful scan-observed sloped plane carrying the high roof edge, but the raw fallback gate treated it as redundant because a lower computed oblique covered enough XZ area. An attempted keep exposed another bug: raw-to-oblique snapping could project that raw plane down to `y≈-13 m` when only orientation matched.

The physical rule is that raw fallback is diagnostic/noise only when the computed arrangement explains both footprint and height. If the computed arrangement misses the high edge/ridge evidence, the raw slope is still meaningful roof geometry.

### Result
- Rebuilt `d28b528a-475b-4ac0-a38d-ee992cd877db` with `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`.
- Room 12 coverage is now full: `tier-ceiling-flat::12` covers `12.18 m²` of a `12.61 m²` room footprint, and the audit no longer flags a ceiling coverage gap.
- Room 15 keeps the small raw high-edge survivor (`tier-ceiling-raw::15:2`) without the impossible `y=-13 m` projection; the audit no longer flags a ceiling coverage gap.
- Latest inspection report: `.context/building-reports/d28b528a-475b-4ac0-a38d-ee992cd877db/20260430T230215/report.md`. LoD2 sanity still fails `not_watertight`, `multiple_components`, and `footprint_mismatch`; tier_payload defects are now only `silent_drops` (1 tiny wall) and `knee_walls_misplaced` (1 knee wall).
- Fixed the new corpus validation failure uncovered by the flat-ceiling change: `59b505e7-b384-451b-90b1-80f2654dd10d` now builds after same-candidate split dedupe.
- Priors-on corpus rebuild: `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1 python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 1` wrote **221/223** buildable payloads. Remaining failures are:
  - `66a72e63-8b3c-4e57-977b-32f5119a9d09`: same-plane wall overlap.
  - `c87c1e25-ff00-44ec-b823-b0966c81af70`: ceiling hole containment.
- Corpus ceiling-source totals after the rebuild: `flat_ceiling=2710`, `computed_oblique=838`, `raw_scan=469`. Raw drops: `redundant=976`, `junk_triangle=557`, `low_quality=62`, plus 22 legacy records without a reason field.
- Tests: `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py -q` — **46 passed**.

## 2026-05-01 — First room-plane ownership pass before raw fallback

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: added a conservative room-level oblique ownership pass. For non-flat or kinked rooms, plausible raw oblique evidence is promoted into `ROOF_ARRANGEMENT` room-owned computed candidates clipped to the room footprint before raw fallback is emitted. The later raw fallback now has a higher-priority flat/oblique owner to subtract against, so raw only survives where no assigned owner explains the same XZ + height.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: kept plain flat rooms protected from this promotion. Mixed rooms remain supported through the existing kink path: a flat candidate plus one or more oblique room candidates can own different XZ regions.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`**: added unit coverage that sloped-room raw oblique evidence is promoted to a room-owned computed candidate, while plain flat-room raw evidence is not.

### Why
The tier 7/8 continuity audit showed that raw fallback was still doing too much visual work. Before this pass, tier 7/8 had **315** raw ceiling pieces:
- 130 had no non-raw XZ owner.
- 147 overlapped non-raw XZ but the non-raw plane was at the wrong height.
- 38 were partial/no clear owner.

That confirmed the user's hypothesis: the pipeline should assign flat/oblique planes over building parts and only use raw as evidence or final unresolved-hole fallback, not as a competing rendered surface.

### Result
- Priors-on corpus rebuild: `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1 python -m reconcile_tiers.build --all --force -j 1` wrote **221/223** buildable payloads. Remaining failures are unchanged:
  - `66a72e63-8b3c-4e57-977b-32f5119a9d09`: same-plane wall overlap.
  - `c87c1e25-ff00-44ec-b823-b0966c81af70`: ceiling hole containment.
- Corpus ceiling-source totals moved from `flat_ceiling=2710`, `computed_oblique=838`, `raw_scan=469` to `flat_ceiling=2710`, `computed_oblique=1428`, `raw_scan=177`.
- Tier 7/8 raw pieces dropped from **315** to **127**. Automated continuity buckets moved from `ok_automated=49`, `bad_continuity=22`, `review_raw_fragmented=9` to:
  - `ok_automated=52`
  - `bad_continuity=21`
  - `review_raw_fragmented=7`
- d28 improved from 26 raw ceilings to 12 raw ceilings while keeping no ceiling coverage gaps.
- Remaining tier 7/8 raw pieces are still meaningful signals: 68 overlap non-raw XZ at mismatched height, 37 have no non-raw XZ owner, and 22 are partial/no clear owner. This means the next step should synthesize larger continuous per-part planes, not merely promote each raw support polygon.

## 2026-05-01 — Preserve opposing gable slope direction in raw-owner promotion

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: fixed `_snap_raw_to_oblique()` to compare raw plane slope direction (`atan2(-a, -c)`) with roof cluster azimuth. It previously compared the opposite plane-normal direction (`atan2(a, c)`), which can be 180° wrong for one side of a gable.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: changed raw-owner promotion to group same-plane raw support polygons before emitting candidates. This lets adjacent fragments on the same snapped roof face become one continuous owner instead of multiple `:rawN` computed-room surfaces.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: when a top-gable raw fragment successfully snaps to an existing oblique roof plane during owner promotion, it no longer gets re-snapped/re-anchored by the wall-axis pass. The second snap preserved angle but changed plane offset, breaking coplanarity and preventing same-face grouping.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/test_build.py`**: added regressions for the 180° slope-direction convention and same-plane raw-fragment merging.

### Why
`0a5032e9-85a0-4970-9143-c430bbdaa0f5::tier-ceiling-computed-oblique-room::2:raw1` was visibly nonsensical: it sat next to `::2:raw0` as another same-direction strip, even though the room/wall context is a gable-like pair of opposing roof faces. The source raw planes were already opposing (`raw0` about 350° upslope, `raw1` about 173°), but `_snap_raw_to_oblique()` matched `raw1` to the wrong reconciled face because of the sign convention error.

### Result
- Rebuilt `0a5032e9-85a0-4970-9143-c430bbdaa0f5` with `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`.
- Room 2 now has one merged `tier-ceiling-computed-oblique-room::2:raw0` face at ~352.6° upslope and one opposing `::2:raw1` face at ~172.6° upslope. The previous same-direction `raw2` fragment merged into `raw0`.
- The building has no tier_payload audit defects after the rebuild. LoD2 sanity still flags `footprint_mismatch` only.
- Priors-on corpus rebuild remains **221/223** buildable. The two hard failures are unchanged:
  - `66a72e63-8b3c-4e57-977b-32f5119a9d09`: same-plane wall overlap.
  - `c87c1e25-ff00-44ec-b823-b0966c81af70`: ceiling hole containment.
- Corpus ceiling-source totals after this correction: `flat_ceiling=2783`, `computed_oblique=1413`, `raw_scan=134`; tier 7/8 raw pieces are **92** across 32 buildings. ## 2026-05-01 — Respect clear room-level gable primitives

### What changed
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof_primitive/gable.py`**: changed wall-top parsing so pentagonal gable-end walls derive their top profile from all non-bottom vertices, not only vertices above the wall midpoint. The classifier now scopes candidate walls to the highest/apex-reaching rooms in the wing and uses the observed eave-wall axis for the ridge line, avoiding near-vertical synthetic slopes when the wing's longest footprint axis is actually a gable end.
- **`reconcile_tiers/roof/roof.py`**: lets a detected gable primitive override noisy per-wing cluster obliques under `ARCHITECTURAL_PRIORS=1`. Non-gable primitives remain fallbacks only when the cluster path emits no oblique surfaces.
- **`reconcile_tiers/build.py`**: carries primitive gable evidence into tier classification so later raw/cluster clutter cannot erase `has_gable` when a room-level primitive fired.
- **`tests/reconcile_tiers/roof/test_primitives.py`**: added a regression for pentagonal gable-end walls synthesising two mirrored oblique surfaces.

### Why
The shared examples show rooms where a human sees a gable immediately from the wall shape: two mirrored sloped wall tops meeting at a ridge. The previous primitive missed or underweighted that signal because it classified the sloped shoulders as bottom-wall geometry, and because scan-derived cluster output could prevent the primitive from participating at all.
