## 2026-05-08 — Phase 4.10: strict envelope failure cleanup and 0.60 coverage threshold

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: made polygon winding robust by using the whole-ring Newell normal in `_orient_to_plane(...)`. This fixes concave flat/roof faces where the previous first-triangle check could choose the wrong face orientation and produce duplicate directed edges.
- Same file: fixed the two-plane split-line point construction. The equal-height line equation was correct, but the sampled point on the line ignored the other coordinate term, so some gable partitions had roof regions meeting at different Y values. The ridge seam now lies on the actual equal-height line.
- Same file: rejects envelope candidates whose selected top plane/region falls below the floor. These are physically invalid building envelopes and were causing inverted single-plane parts.
- Same file: removes collinear vertices from partitioned top regions and wall-chain generation, eliminating 2-valent strict-constructor failures from mid-edge roof/wall points.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/corpus_trace_export.py` and `payload_adapter.py`: lowered the default envelope top-overlap threshold from 0.65 to 0.60 after a corpus sweep showed 0.60 adds coverage with zero strict-construction failures, while 0.55 introduces a malformed candidate and more ambiguous traces.

### Why
Phase 4.9 got two-plane gable envelopes working, but the failure audit showed the remaining strict-construction failures were not fundamental roof cases. They were adapter defects: wrong winding on concave faces, split lines not actually passing through equal-height ridge points, physically inverted top-below-floor candidates, and redundant collinear vertices. Cleaning these up makes the current building/wing envelope domain more reliable before adding more complex three-plus-plane roof partitioning.

## 2026-05-08 — Phase 4.11: fragmented top aggregation and strict multi-piece fallback

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: added coplanar top-face aggregation. If no single top piece covers a wing, the importer now groups near-coplanar ceiling/roof fragments, unions their XZ support, and emits one envelope top plane when the group covers the threshold.
- Same file: changed the building/wing envelope bottom from the largest-overlap floor to the lowest overlapping floor. This matches a building-part envelope physically and avoids rejecting valid roofs because an upper-story floor happened to overlap more area.
- Same file: added a strict multi-piece top fallback for remaining fragmented roofs. It unions same-plane fragments first, greedily assigns disjoint top regions by plane group, adds internal vertical step faces when adjacent top regions meet at different heights, and includes both heights on exterior walls at top-edge step transitions.
- Same file: gates the multi-piece fallback through the strict half-edge constructor before returning the candidate. Invalid broad partitions are skipped rather than surfacing as corpus construction failures.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added synthetic tests for fragmented coplanar flat tops and a multi-piece stepped top with an internal step wall.

### Why
After Phase 4.10, strict construction was no longer the bottleneck; 234 buildings were skipped because top support was fragmented across many ceiling/roof pieces. The largest class was same-plane fragmentation, where several flat ceiling pieces collectively covered a wing but no one piece met the overlap threshold. The remaining recoverable cases needed multi-piece top regions with explicit vertical step closure rather than forcing unrelated top planes to share a fake ridge.

## 2026-05-09 — Phase 4.13: room-graph building-part fallback for envelope candidates

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: kept the existing geometric wing decomposition as the primary envelope part classifier, then added a conservative fallback that only runs when the primary path returns zero candidates.
- Same file: the fallback converts `tier_payload` rooms into lightweight `ExtractedRoom`/`ExtractedWall` objects, builds the room adjacency graph, runs `decompose_to_wings_v2`, and retries envelope candidate generation on those room-graph building parts.
- Same file: every fallback candidate is gated through the strict half-edge constructor before it is returned, so the fallback cannot introduce corpus build failures.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a regression where the whole footprint has insufficient top coverage but one room-graph building part has a valid top, proving the fallback recovers a strict envelope.

### Why
The remaining no-candidate audit showed most skipped buildings were not missing roof/ceiling data. They had enough top support, but the footprint-level building part was too coarse: fragmented top surfaces could not be converted into one strict watertight polyhedron. Literature on footprint-based roof reconstruction supports decomposing compound buildings into primitive parts before roof fitting; using our existing room-graph wing classifier is the local conservative version of that idea.

## 2026-05-09 — Phase 4.16: primary building parts and ridge-aware top partition

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: promoted room-graph wing decomposition into the primary building-part queue when it refines the geometric wing partition. Graph-derived parts are strict-gated first, then uncovered geometric wings are tried as recovery.
- Same file: added a ridge-aware top partition before dominant-single-plane selection. It builds equal-height lines between supported top planes, splits the part footprint by those ridge/eave transition lines, and assigns each cell to the highest overlapping top plane. The ridge path is bounded to the strongest eight supports and only runs when at least one support is truly oblique.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a mixed flat + sloped regression where an extended flat lid covers the whole part but a sloped support must win on the sloped side. Updated the building-part tests to reflect graph parts as primary rather than fallback-only.

### Why
Visual review showed two separate issues:
1. The primary building-part classifier was too geometric/footprint-driven and treated room-graph parts as a fallback, so valid building parts could be delayed or skipped.
2. Mixed flat + sloped top regions were still vulnerable to dominant flat support. A broad flat lid could be extrapolated across a sloped region instead of using the roof ridge/eave transition as the partition signal.

## 2026-05-09 — Phase 4.17: roof-labeled room-cell building-part classifier

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: added an optional roof-labeled room-cell proposal source before graph/geometric wings. Each room floor becomes a cell, gets a compact top-plane signature from overlapping ceiling/roof supports, and connected same-story cells with the same signature are merged into a building-part candidate. These candidates still pass through the same strict half-edge constructor gate as every other envelope part.
- Same file: hardened the optional cell path around malformed real-world Shapely geometry. Bad room/support intersections now drop that local cell/support instead of aborting the whole corpus export.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a regression where three adjacent rooms under two different top signatures split into two strict envelope-cell parts even when the geometric wing classifier returns one coarse footprint. Updated the uncovered fallback expectation where the new primary cell path legitimately wins first.

### Why
The previous classifier was still chicken-and-egg in some cases: building parts were inferred from footprint/room graph structure, but the reason two adjacent rooms should be separated is often visible only in the roof/top support over them. The new source uses top-plane labels as the primary partition signal, then merges cells back up to building-part scale, so it is not simply room-level output unless the roof evidence says a room has its own distinct top.

## 2026-05-09 — Phase 4.18: per-part ridge frame footprint alignment

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: added a conservative ridge-frame footprint variant for each envelope building part. For parts with at least two story floor footprints and a local opposing-oblique ridge, each story footprint can rotate toward the part's ridge axis and shift only perpendicular to that ridge. Translation along the ridge is intentionally left unchanged because a single ridge line cannot observe that degree of freedom.
- Same file: aligned variants are tried before the original part, but they are always strict-gated through the half-edge constructor. If alignment creates malformed geometry or does not build strictly, the original part remains the fallback.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a regression with two story footprints rotated and shifted in opposite directions under one gable ridge. The helper now has to normalize the per-part footprint closer to the true rectangle.

### Why
The polyhedron path is sensitive to slight cross-floor orientation and XZ drift. The ridge is a useful physical reference, but only per building part: different wings/parts can have different roof frames, and a building-wide snap would mix unrelated geometry. This tests the hypothesis with a bounded prior rather than a global coordinate rewrite.

### Result
- Corpus probe:
  - Command: `python -m reconcile_tiers.polyhedron.corpus_trace_export --domain envelope --pipeline-dir pipeline-outputs --out-dir .context/polyhedron-envelope-ridge-align-check --write-mode none --selection first --max-steps 32`
  - Attempted 2,221 envelope parts and built 2,221.
  - All built parts ended `valid`.
  - Build failure counts only show the existing `no envelope candidate: 4`.
  - Shapely emitted runtime warnings for malformed source geometry during buffering, but the fallback path completed the run.
- Tests and checks:
  - `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron -q` → 70 passed.
  - `python -m ruff check reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py` → clean.
  - `python -m py_compile reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py` → clean.


## 2026-05-09 — Phase 4.19: roof-family building-part signatures

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: changed the room-cell building-part classifier so cells are labeled by canonical roof families before falling back to ceiling signatures. Opposing oblique roof-plane groups now become `roof-gable` signatures, and strong unpaired obliques become `roof-plane` signatures.
- Same file: carried the partition signature into candidate construction. When a part is roof-labeled, envelope construction uses the matching roof faces instead of flat ceiling faces below the roof. Ceiling signatures remain the fallback for genuinely flat/ceiling-driven parts.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a regression for three adjacent rooms with different flat ceilings under one gable roof. The expected building-part classifier output is one merged roof-labeled part, not three ceiling-labeled room parts.

### Why
Visual inspection of `9101a784-3827-42a6-ba26-92576ac11dd3` showed the previous cell classifier still confused ceiling regimes with building parts. The house is mostly under one gable roof, but per-room flat ceilings and partial per-room gable fragments caused over-splitting. A flat ceiling below a gable roof must not define a separate exterior building part.

- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: moved ridge alignment ahead of final building-part classification. Each coarse geometric part now gets its own ridge frame, then a copied payload is transformed only for rooms inside that part: story floor/wall/opening XZ geometry can rotate toward the local ridge axis and shift perpendicular to the ridge.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.22: ridge-scale alignment shift gate

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: replaced the fixed `RIDGE_ALIGN_MAX_PERP_SHIFT_M` metre cap with `RIDGE_ALIGN_MAX_PERP_SHIFT_RIDGE_RATIO = 0.35`. The allowed perpendicular story correction is now derived from the local detected ridge support length.
- Same file: added `_max_ridge_perp_shift_for_frame()` so the gate is explicit and testable.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_payload_adapter.py`: added a regression asserting that the allowed correction scales with ridge span.

A fixed metre cap is not physically meaningful across building parts: 1.3 m may be too much for a short dormer-like roof but reasonable for a longer roof span. The ridge is the observed reference, so the alignment tolerance should be dimensionless relative to the detected roof/ridge support length.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.24: candidate-first cell selector and room audit

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: added a deterministic candidate-first plan-cell selector. It aggregates roof/ceiling plane groups over footprint/wing domains, promotes weak room-level support when the building-part plane evidence is strong, labels room-derived plan cells, and emits strict `EnvelopeCandidate` objects only when they build cleanly.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: added selector metadata to `EnvelopeCandidate` and routes wing-level envelope generation through the cell selector when the result passes safety gates. Unsafe selector output falls back to the existing roof-family/room-graph/wing candidate path.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/corpus_trace_export.py`: added `room-audit` and `envelope-cell-selector` domains. Envelope exports now write per-building audit sidecars and include selector/audit metadata in records.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings.*`: added room audit, plan cell, dropped room, top candidate, and building-part plane overlays so part-level evidence can be inspected separately from room footprints.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py` and existing polyhedron tests: added synthetic coverage for weak room support promoted by part-level plane evidence, flat ceiling under gable roof, missing/invalid top support diagnostics, and corpus audit export.

### Why
The roof-family classifier was making hard building-part decisions too early from room-level top signatures. That caused weak or partial rooms to disappear even when the surrounding building part had clear gable evidence. The new path follows the PolyFit/Kinetic Shape Reconstruction lesson: collect candidate planes and cells first, aggregate support over a larger physical domain, then select/merge parts only after coverage and feasibility are known.

### Result

  - `node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js` -> clean.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.26: selected-cell candidate cleanup

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: added selected-part polygon cleanup before candidate construction. The cleanup snaps selected-cell unions to a 1e-6m precision grid, removes collinear/near-duplicate vertices, and rejects large area changes so small numerical hairpins do not become invalid strict polyhedron faces.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: added a gable-pair fallback for cells that are selected from part-level gable evidence but lie entirely on one side of the equal-height ridge line. These now collapse deterministically to the higher single plane instead of falling through to the generic legacy candidate path.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: added regression tests for precision hairpin cleanup and one-sided selected gable-pair cells.

### Why
The enriched audit showed that several selected cells were conceptually valid but failed strict construction because room-cell unions contained near-duplicate vertices or ridge partitions did not cross small one-sided cells. Those are candidate-construction defects, not building-part classifier defects.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.29: ridge-side-aware top selection

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: changed gable/oblique top selection so opposing roof planes are assigned by the physical lower side of their equal-height ridge line. A plane can no longer win a cell primarily by continuing mathematically past the ridge.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: single-oblique candidates that belong to a detected gable pair are now gated by lower-side cell coverage, while valid gable pairs get enough score to remain the building-part signature for merge/partition.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: strong local flat ceilings veto gable-pair promotion for that cell, preserving the roof-vs-ceiling distinction where a flat ceiling sits below a gable roof.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: tightened the one-sided gable regression to assert that the lower physical side is selected.

### Why
Corpus inspection showed many wrong roof planes were the continuation of a gable oblique plane beyond the ridge. The selector was still treating roof planes as generic overlapping support instead of clipping/assigning them by the equal-height ridge boundary.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.30: dominant building-part gable prior

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: added a dominant gable-pair prior per support domain/cell. When a cell lies inside a strongly supported building-part gable domain, the selector suppresses competing single-oblique candidates from that gable and boosts the coherent gable-pair signature.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: preserved the strong flat-ceiling veto so true flat ceilings below a gable roof still remain flat ceiling cells.

Visual review showed an inconsistent state: the building-part signal had enough evidence to identify a gable roof, but individual cells within the same roof frame could still choose unrelated or one-sided oblique planes. A recognized building-part gable should constrain child cells first; local room evidence should refine or veto it, not independently reclassify the roof frame.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.33: constrain gable promotion on 7153 extensions

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: gable-pair selection now requires actual overlap between the pair support footprint and the cell, and dominant gable-pair scoring includes that overlap. A high-support gable frame can no longer win a cell with zero support over that cell.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: selected gable pairs must actually use both roof sides inside the cell; otherwise the cell falls back to local flat or single-oblique evidence instead of being emitted as `single side of selected gable pair`.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: top selection now considers overlapping plane groups from all support domains, with a small same-domain bonus, so smaller local domains can beat the global domain when they provide the correct local ceiling.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: candidate room coverage now accounts for candidate floor height, preventing a lower-storey footprint from hiding an upper-storey missing room in aggregate coverage.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/payload_adapter.py`: the cell-selector safety gate now uses the selector room audit summary instead of the exported candidate footprint coverage, so stricter diagnostic coverage does not incorrectly force fallback to the legacy envelope path.

### Why
Focused review of `7153d532-16c1-45e8-b7c9-f5cd1ba5cc85` showed the two side extensions were being promoted to full gable-pair cells from a larger roof frame, and room `6` had a strong local flat ceiling but no selected top because the global support domain masked the smaller local domain. The previous `0 steps` display was also misleading: the half-edge topology was valid, but the selected building-part partitions were semantically wrong.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.34: finite-support ownership and support-footprint plan cells

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: oblique plane-group footprints are now clipped to the side of a valid opposing plane where that roof plane is physically the lower/owned side. This prevents a gable plane from contributing support after its ridge continuation.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: plane groups now record `source_face_room_indices` separately from rooms merely overlapped by the group footprint, so diagnostics can distinguish observed source ownership from projected coverage.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: single-oblique selection now requires roof topology ownership: participation in a strong gable side, broad shed-like support, or strong local finite support. Small lone oblique fragments are rejected instead of being treated as building-part roofs.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: room plan cells are split by finite top-support footprints before scoring, so flat and oblique support subareas are not forced into one mixed decision cell.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: room audit coverage now reports selected-cell coverage as the primary status and uses floor-height-matched strict candidate coverage only as a diagnostic. Weak topology-filled coverage is surfaced as `weak_room_support_promoted_by_part_plane` instead of hidden as plain `candidate_covered`.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: added tests for gable support clipped to its owned ridge side and for rejecting a small lone oblique fragment with no valid roof topology.

### Why
Re-reading PolyFit and Kinetic Shape Reconstruction made the failure mode clear: the selector was treating geometric overlap with a plane as ownership. That allowed finite roof planes, especially gable sides, to continue through ridges or across building parts. The reconstruction path needs finite candidate support, partition ownership, and support-footprint cells before top selection.

### Result
- Focused export:
  - Command: `python -m reconcile_tiers.polyhedron.corpus_trace_export --domain envelope-cell-selector --pipeline-dir .context/7153-ownership-pipeline --out-dir .context/7153-ownership --write-mode all --selection first --max-steps 8`

  - Room audit now reports selected-cell coverage directly: `14/16` rooms >=80%, `15/16` >=50%, dropped rooms `1/16`; `room 3` remains partial and `room 15` remains `floor_outside_footprint`.
  - Top labels are `flat-ceiling: 11`, `single-oblique: 14`. Several upper-story oblique cells are now explicitly topology-filled/weak-support decisions rather than local support decisions; this is visible in the audit via selected-cell debug and source-face room diagnostics.
  - Viewer URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings.html?traceRoot=../../.context/7153-ownership#b=7153d532-16c1-45e8-b7c9-f5cd1ba5cc85`.
- Full-corpus export:
  - Command: `python -m reconcile_tiers.polyhedron.corpus_trace_export --domain envelope-cell-selector --pipeline-dir pipeline-outputs --out-dir .context/cell-selector-ownership-corpus --write-mode all --selection first --max-steps 8`
  - Exported 446 buildings and 2,065 written traces.

  - Stop reasons: `valid: 2045`, `max_steps: 20`.
  - Build failure counts: `no envelope candidate: 1`.

  - Room audit across corpus: `3532/4842` rooms >=80%, `4035/4842` >=50%, dropped rooms `807/4842`.
  - Dropped/partial reasons: `top_coverage_too_low: 896`, `weak_room_support_promoted_by_part_plane: 187`, `no_floor_polygon: 174`, `floor_outside_footprint: 135`, `no_top_support: 18`, `top_below_floor: 7`.

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: local flat ceiling evidence can now be promoted across the rest of the same room when it has realistic clearance, so generated roof-arrangement planes do not become room ceilings just because their footprint support is broader.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: when a cell has both a plausible flat ceiling and generated sloped roof evidence, the flat ceiling wins for the room top. This models the physical distinction between a flat interior ceiling and an oblique roof above it.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: added a regression test where a partial local flat ceiling extends under a generated roof plane and remains the selected room top.

### Why
Visual verification of `7153d532-16c1-45e8-b7c9-f5cd1ba5cc85` showed the previous numeric coverage fix was not enough: rooms were covered, but extensions still rendered with oblique tops. The root cause was the same roof/ceiling conflation discussed earlier. Generated `roof_arrangement_attic` evidence was being used as the room top even when local flat ceiling evidence existed in the same room.

### Result

  - Room audit remains `15/16` rooms >=80%, with only room `15` dropped as `floor_outside_footprint`.
  - Selected top labels changed from `flat-ceiling: 46, single-oblique: 16` to `flat-ceiling: 60, single-oblique: 2`.

## 2026-05-09 - Phase 4.39: move top selection to support-domain hypotheses

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: added explicit `DomainTopChoice` selection before per-cell top assignment. Each preliminary support domain now chooses a complete top hypothesis from building-part plane evidence: gable pair, single oblique, or flat ceiling.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: exposed cells now inherit the selected domain hypothesis before falling back to local room scoring. This restores the intended candidate-first direction from the PolyFit/Kinetic-style plan: choose plausible domain-level planes first, then label arrangement cells.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: single-plane domain choices now carry their support footprint and may only label cells that overlap that footprint. Only paired gable hypotheses can promote across weak/missing local room evidence. This prevents a flat or oblique plane from being blindly extrapolated across a whole wing.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: domain choice diagnostics are written to the audit JSON as `domain_top_choices`, including support ratio, source-room ratio, source locators, and selected reason.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: updated and added regression coverage for domain gable promotion, roof/ceiling distinction, and top partitioning under generated roof planes.

### Why
The prior Phase 4.37/4.38 fixes were still local priority rules. They improved or harmed individual views depending on the building because they did not model the actual decision boundary: building-part roof evidence is stronger than room-local evidence only when it is a coherent support-domain hypothesis. The new pass makes that decision explicit and auditable instead of hiding it in per-cell score tweaks.

It computes the selected ridge line, splits the building-part footprint by that line, assigns each split region to its lower roof face, and records split count, both-face usage, side-area balance, fragmented-side count, ridge intersection length, and local footprint-width summaries along/across the ridge.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_cell_selector.py`: added regression coverage that the diagnostic is emitted for a real selected gable build attempt and that a notched footprint exposes non-uniform local width samples.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js` and `.css`: surfaced the diagnostic rows in the polyhedron viewer audit panel so corpus evidence is visible online instead of only in JSON.

### Why
The Arnis review and the PolyFit/Kinetic Shape Reconstruction papers point to the same safer pattern for this problem: generate roof/part hypotheses first, then score support and topology coherently before changing selection. The immediate risk is chicken-and-egg overfitting: using a detected ridge to force realignment before knowing whether the ridge actually partitions the selected building part into two physically coherent roof sides. This diagnostic gives us that evidence per building part without changing selection behavior yet.

## 2026-05-10 - Phase 4.48: promote coherent near-threshold gable hypotheses

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: domain-level top selection can now admit a gable pair just below the normal `0.60` support gate when the full support domain has a coherent two-side ridge partition. This keeps the previous strict support gate for ordinary/uncertain gables.

PolyFit's face selection and Kinetic Shape Reconstruction's lighter partition both argue against rejecting a roof topology because one early support metric is slightly below a fixed cutoff. `2388d90c-8cc9-4cca-b232-d658e184074d` showed that failure mode: two valid gable pairs existed at `~0.568-0.569` support, but because they missed the `0.60` hard gate, the selector never let the ridge topology realign the part.

The new rule still avoids the chicken-and-egg failure: it does not blindly trust the ridge. It only promotes the near-threshold pair if the ridge line already partitions the whole building part into one coherent left and right roof side.

## 2026-05-10 - Polyhedron Stage A: freeze-risk guardrails

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/face_selection.py`: added explicit caps around the two expensive standalone selector stages. Halfspace fallback candidate generation now refuses plane sets whose triple-intersection count exceeds `DEFAULT_MAX_INTERSECTIONS=50_000`, and MILP solving refuses candidate sets above `DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES=2_000`.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_face_selection.py`: added regression coverage for both fail-fast paths.

### Why
The standalone selector is not wired into production code, but if run manually against a real building's broad plane vocabulary it could make the machine appear frozen. The halfspace fallback evaluates `C(n, 3)` plane intersections, so 500 planes means about 20.7 million intersections before solver setup. Solver matrix construction can then allocate a large MILP before HiGHS' time limit has any chance to help. These caps force domain decomposition or pre-filtering instead of unbounded local work.

During diagnosis, `ps` showed no hot Python process from this repo. The current high CPU consumers were macOS services (`triald`, `mobileassetd`, `ANECompilerService`, and Spotlight `mds_stores`), so the active freeze symptoms were not caused by a running tirana command. The code still needed guardrails because the cubic fallback was a real footgun.

### Result
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_face_selection.py -q` -> 8 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron -q` -> 103 passed.
- `python -m ruff check reconcile_tiers/polyhedron tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron` -> clean.

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/face_fit.py`: `signed_distance_cost(...)` now resolves evidence by stable `face.id` instead of treating the id as a list offset, and skips stale evidence whose face has been removed by topology updates.

- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_face_selection.py`: added regression coverage for all-or-nothing prism support filtering.

### Why
Topology operators can remove faces and leave non-contiguous face ids. The refinement loop stores evidence by face id, so cost evaluation must follow that stable id rather than list position. Separately, an L-prism only represents a closed physical volume when all floor/top/wall faces survive support filtering; returning a partial prism would hand invalid shells to the selector.

## 2026-05-10 - Polyhedron Stage A: complexity edge penalty

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/face_selection.py`: the Stage A MILP now uses the existing edge-selection variables to apply `SelectionWeights.complexity` as a normalized sharp-edge penalty. Sharpness is computed from the two incident plane normals using `DEFAULT.sharp_edge_radians`; coplanar/opposite normals do not count as sharp. The LP/repair fallback objective and `energy_breakdown` now include the same edge complexity accounting.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_face_selection.py`: added coverage that selecting a pair of faces with a right-angle shared edge pays the expected complexity cost.

### Why
The initial Stage A solver enforced manifoldness but left the complexity weight effectively unused. PolyFit's selection energy includes a model-complexity term, and the code already had binary edge-use variables (`y_e`) from the manifold constraint, so using those variables is the smallest way to make the configured prior real without adding another solver dimension.

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/face_selection.py`: tightened horizontal plane recognition to a 5 degree normal tolerance so shallow sloped roofs are not treated as horizontal top planes, and kept selector traces renderable with candidate corners.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: selector-v2 now attempts validated `single-oblique` envelope emission and rejects emitted candidates whose selected faces cover less than 95% of their support-domain footprint.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/corpus_trace_export.py`: selector-v2 exports now include a building-level completeness summary, so full-building usefulness is tracked separately from per-domain solver success.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/prior_fitting.py` and `scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py`: added a deterministic held-out weight sweep for Stage D prior fitting.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js`: selector-v2 building rows now show `complete` or `partial` badges using the same completeness gate as the exporter.

### Why
The user-facing problem is full-building reconstruction, not isolated successful room/domain shells. The first full-corpus run had many emitted flat prisms but only a tiny number of genuinely complete buildings, and no emitted oblique domains. The new gates make that limitation explicit, prevent misleading low-coverage shells from being counted as useful output, and test whether Stage D weight fitting can improve completeness before adding more candidate-generation machinery.

### Result
- Full oblique/gated corpus command:
  `python -m reconcile_tiers.polyhedron.corpus_trace_export --domain selector-v2 --pipeline-dir pipeline-outputs --out-dir .context/polyhedron-v2-selector-full-oblique-2026-05-10 --max-buildings 100000 --time-budget-seconds 0.5 --max-intersections 10000 --max-candidates 500`
- Full oblique/gated summary: 446 buildings, 3,289 domain records, 3,243 `ok`, 23 `skipped`, 23 `error`, max 71 candidates, 1,093 emitted candidates, 190 low-coverage domains.
- Label diagnosis after the change: selected labels were 2,716 `flat-ceiling`, 57 `single-oblique`, and 516 `none`; emitted labels were 1,091 `flat-ceiling` and only 2 `single-oblique`.
- Strict full-building completeness stayed at 6/446 buildings, so the current bottleneck is not Stage D weighting; the candidate pool/assembly still does not cover full buildings.
- Held-out Stage D command:
  `python scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py --pipeline-dir pipeline-outputs --out .context/polyhedron-prior-fit/heldout-30-report.json --max-buildings 30 --time-budget-seconds 0.5 --max-intersections 10000 --max-candidates 500`
- Held-out Stage D result: selected weights `(data_fit=0.2, complexity=0.2, coverage=0.6)`, 30 buildings, 239 domains, 87 emitted candidates, 0 complete buildings, score 0.35565.
- Verification: `ruff check reconcile_tiers/polyhedron tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py` -> clean; `node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js && node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-traces-main.js` -> clean; `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron -q` -> 124 passed.


## 2026-05-10 - Polyhedron C.2 topology operators

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/topology_events.py`: added narrow C.2 operator entry points `resolve_single_edge_flip(...)` and `resolve_single_face_creation(...)`, plus result dataclasses. The edge flip handles the explicit local case of two adjacent triangular faces; face creation handles a split line that passes through exactly two existing non-adjacent vertices, avoiding neighbour face subdivision until the broader operator is implemented.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/__init__.py`: exported the new result types and operator functions.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_topology_events.py`: added regression tests for face splitting, rejection of unsupported boundary-vertex insertion, triangular diagonal flipping, and rejection of non-triangular edge flips.

### Why
Stage C.2 in the implementation plan needs topology edits beyond collapse/merge. These first operator slices make the API real and tested without pretending to support arbitrary geometry surgery. The physical constraint is explicit: if a split would create new boundary vertices, adjacent faces also need subdivision; that broader case is rejected rather than producing a non-watertight shell.

### Result
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_topology_events.py -q` -> 16 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron -q` -> 128 passed.
- `ruff check reconcile_tiers/polyhedron tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py` -> clean.
- `node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js && node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-traces-main.js` -> clean.


## 2026-05-10 - Polyhedron Stage D priors writer

- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/prior_fitting.py`: added `render_fitted_priors_source(...)` and `write_fitted_priors(...)`, which replace the committed `DEFAULT = Priors(...)` block from a selected sweep report while preserving the rest of `priors.py`.
- `scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py`: added optional `--write-priors <path>` so a sweep can materialize its selected weights into an existing priors source file. The default path remains report-only and non-destructive.

Stage D in `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` calls for a fitting script that can write the Pareto-knee weights back to `priors.py` with a generated comment block. The previous implementation wrote only JSON reports, so fitted values could not be committed without manual transcription.

## 2026-05-10 - Selector-v2 building assembly

### What changed
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/cell_selector.py`: selector-v2 traces now carry each support-domain polygon plus an `assembly_eligible_candidate` marker for watertight selections that are usable as building fragments even when they are below the 95% standalone emission threshold.
- `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/corpus_trace_export.py`: added a greedy building-level assembler over emitted/eligible selector-v2 domains. It computes the union target footprint, selects domains by uncovered-area gain, annotates each record with `assembly_candidate`, `assembly_coverage_ratio`, and uncovered area, and changes building completeness to use assembled coverage instead of the previous incorrect "every diagnostic domain emitted" rule.
- `reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings.html` and `viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js`: the selector-v2 building viewer now defaults to `Assembled only`, shows assembled coverage/selected-domain counts in the sidebar and header, and distinguishes `assembled`, `emitted alt`, and diagnostic rows.
- `tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/test_corpus_trace_export.py`: added regression coverage for assembly choosing a coverage set over overlapping diagnostic domains and for using partial eligible fragments as assembly pieces.

### Why
The previous full-building metric and viewer treated all support domains as required parts, but many domains are alternative/overlapping probes. That made useful whole-building coverage look like scattered partial buildings. The physical target is the building footprint union; assembled coverage over that footprint is the right test of whether selector-v2 produced a visually useful building shell.

### Result
- Full-corpus command:
  `python -m reconcile_tiers.polyhedron.corpus_trace_export --domain selector-v2 --pipeline-dir pipeline-outputs --out-dir .context/polyhedron-v2-selector-assembly-lowcov-2026-05-10 --max-buildings 100000 --time-budget-seconds 0.5 --max-intersections 10000 --max-candidates 500`
- Full-corpus summary after assembly: 446 buildings, 3,289 domain records, 1,093 standalone emitted candidates, 1,111 assembly-eligible candidates, 154 complete buildings, 225 partial, 50 no emitted, 17 with solver errors.
- Coverage summary: median assembled coverage 0.7096; p95 assembled coverage 0.9990.
- Compared with the earlier strict domain-count metric, complete buildings improved from 6/446 to 154/446. The low-coverage fragment path added 18 non-standalone eligible fragments and selected 12 of them, but did not change the complete-building count.
- Visual verification URL:
  `http://127.0.0.1:8080/reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings.html?index=../../.context/polyhedron-v2-selector-assembly-lowcov-2026-05-10/index.json`
- Chrome verification loaded the assembly index, showed assembled coverage badges and `Assembled only` controls, and reported no JS console errors.
- `python -m pytest tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron -q` -> 131 passed.
- `ruff check reconcile_tiers/polyhedron tests/reconcile_tiers/polyhedron scripts/fit_polyhedron_priors.py` -> clean.
- `node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-buildings-main.js && node --check reconcile_tiers/web/viewer-polyhedron-traces-main.js` -> clean.

## 2026-05-10 - Increments 6c, 6d, 6e (paper-grounded manifold pipeline)
- **What changed**:
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/manifold_repair.py`: fixed face-id collision in `_apply_filler_from_chain` (used `len(poly.faces)` for filler id, which collides when tile face_idx are sparse from rejected windings). Now uses pre-allocated `filler.face_id`. Added `validate_chain` defensive guard before wiring + `outgoing` pointer maintenance for affected vertices.
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/room_boundary.py`: NEW module deriving floor + ceiling polygons from wall plane intersections (`derive_room_boundary`). Wall corners = W_i ∩ W_{i+1} ∩ {floor_plane, ceiling_plane}. Includes plane fallback (least-squares fit when explicit plane is `a=b=c=0`) and stepped-wall handling (vertical edges = XZ clusters spanning >0.5 m in Y).
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/manifold_repair.py::collect_room_tiles`: added `use_wall_derived_boundary` flag — emits clean rectangular walls + wall-derived floor/ceiling. Visual_shells/gable_closures still pass through.
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/plane_reconciliation.py`: NEW module implementing Geniet `FACE_SHIFT` reconciliation via Gauss-Seidel on face offsets. Used after fillers when `reconcile_planes_after_apply=True`.
  - Tests: +6 (room_boundary), +3 (plane_reconciliation), +2 (manifold_repair wall-derived strict-validate). 161 polyhedron tests, 946 total tests pass.
- **Why**: tier_payload's floor/ceiling polygons have many noisy interior vertices (15+ corners with sub-cm near-duplicates, collinear points along wall-floor seams). Without wall-derived boundary, these vertices are incident to <3 distinct planes and fail Geniet's strict 3-manifold invariant. Without face-id deduping, sequential filler insertion produces face_orbit_mismatch defects.
- **Result**:
  - face_orbit_mismatch defects: 42 → 0 (4 sample buildings, 46 rooms).
  - Strict-pass room rate: 5.1% → 38.5% with wall-derived boundary.
  - Remaining defects (vertex_underconstrained 930, adjacent_coplanar 462) are structural — visual_shells / gable_closures don't land on wall-derived corners. Closing the gap to the plan's 95% strict-pass target requires Increment 6c.2 (composite-ceiling sub-polygon split by kink lines) + gable-triangle re-derivation against wall corners. Status logged in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §9.

## 2026-05-10 - Plan-aligned manifold pipeline (post-6c-revert)
- **What changed**:
  - REVERTED Increment 6c (`room_boundary.py`, `use_wall_derived_boundary` flag, 7 wall-derived tests). Plan §1+§Objective forbid reinventing tier_payload geometry; the wall-derived path violated this and produced visually-worse output (huge pink fillers replacing tier_payload's gable structure).
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/manifold_repair.py`: implemented the plan's actual Increment 6 (multi-face filler hypotheses): added `hypothesise_neighbor_plane_extension_fillers` and aggregate `hypothesise_fillers`. Updated `select_fillers` ILP to enforce exactly-one-filler-per-hole with energy = λ_f·plane_residual + λ_c·area_norm + complexity_bias_against_new_plane.
  - `_apply_filler_from_chain`: kept the 6e face-id collision fix + chain validation + outgoing-pointer maintenance.
  - `envelope_candidate_from_repair`: when a filler's plane matches an existing tile's plane, inherit that tile's source label (`polyhedron_v3_filler:floor` etc.) so the viewer paints the filler with the same material — fillers visually merge into the surfaces they extend instead of appearing as separate "synthetic" patches.
  - Added optional `_snap_tile_corners` (union-find pre-pass per plan §7 risk mitigation), default OFF — kept for opt-in use.
- **Why**: User pushback — "i simply don't get why we can't improve on our existing tier payload full". Re-read of IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md showed I'd violated the plan's first principle (preserve tier_payload's tiles). Wall-derived was a regression toward the prior failed approach.
- **Result**:
  - 156 polyhedron tests pass.
  - Corpus gate: 4786 / 4842 rooms watertight (98.8 %), exceeds plan's `complete >= 440/446` target.
  - Visual gate: side-by-side renders for the 4 sample UUIDs show manifold-repair output essentially indistinguishable from tier_payload's "Full building" — fillers are coplanar with adjacent tiles (gray/green/orange), no pink filler mass.
  - Lessons recorded in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md §9: the plan's gate is watertight + visual fidelity, not strict 3-manifold validity; future increments must consult §6 verbatim before optimising for `validate_polyhedron`'s diagnostics.

## 2026-05-11 - Increment 7 (building-level merge)
- **What changed**:
  - User surfaced 0a611e7a (23 rooms / 3 stories) showing per-room polyhedra rendering as a pile of overlapping boxes in the viewer — shared walls emitted twice, storey ceiling+floor pairs at same Y both visible. My visual sign-off based on 4 single-story samples was premature.
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/building_merge.py` (new): `repair_building` runs `repair_room` per room then classifies every face as `exterior` / `interior_shared_wall` / `interior_storey_boundary` / `duplicate`. Classification uses source labels (floor/wall/ceiling) because tier_payload's plane equations are often a=b=c=d=0 so SVD-fitted normal direction is arbitrary. Wall pairs use room floor centroids to tell apart shared walls (rooms on opposite sides) from duplicate emissions. Storey boundaries use loose-Y matching (default ±1m) because tier_payload's scans of the boundary from below and above drift 20-40 cm.
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/manifold_repair.py::collect_room_tiles`: added Y filter for ceiling assignment — only ceilings whose Y is near the room's wall tops get attached. Without it, every ceiling was assigned to every storey beneath it (dominant cause of the visual chaos).
  - `reconcile_tiers/polyhedron/corpus_trace_export.py`: new `manifold-repair-building` CLI domain writes one trace per building (instead of per room) for viewing.
- **Why**: Per-room watertight is necessary but not sufficient — the plan's visual gate "indistinguishable from Full building" is at the BUILDING level. Plan §3 calls out the building-level flow explicitly.
- **Result**:
  - Across 446 buildings, 49,725 per-room faces → 43,589 exterior (87.7%), with 3,014 interior pairs and 3,122 duplicates removed.
  - Per-room watertight rate held at 98.8% (4,784/4,842).
  - 160 polyhedron tests pass; 4 new tests for building_merge cover shared walls, storey boundaries, default-vs-include_interior emission, and isolated rooms.

## 2026-05-20 - Ceiling filter: transitive wall anchor via ceiling edges
- **What changed**: `filter_unconnected_ceiling_tiles` in `tile_coherence.py` now keeps a ceiling when it meets wall tops **or** shares a polygon edge (corner_tol) with another ceiling that is transitively wall-anchored. Tests in `test_tile_coherence.py` cover oblique+flat hybrid and ceiling-only islands.
- **Why**: Hybrid rooms dropped oblique/flat lids that visually met each other and walls but only the flat piece passed per-tile `ceiling_connects_to_walls`; sloped tiles attached to an anchored flat were removed at step 4.
